---
title: "Figures — melanoma ICB gut metaproteomics (outline v2)"
output: html_document
---

Rebuilt from `figures_v1.Rmd` against `analysis_v17.Rmd` and
`MANUSCRIPT_OUTLINE_v2.md`. Run **in the session that has just knit v17**, or in a
session where the bundle has been loaded, so the analysis objects are present.

Three things differ from v1.

**Every panel is wrapped.** `panel()` catches a missing object or a failed
computation and returns a placeholder carrying the error text instead of aborting
the knit. A figure with one grey box is more useful than no figure and a
traceback, and the box names what to wire up.

**Panels recompute what v17 does not export.** v17's chunks are wrapped in
`local()` so they cannot collide across 78 chunks; only `MP`, `G`, `kos`, `pat`,
`MGm`, `MPm` and `gen_coupling` leave their chunks. Anything else a panel needs —
the coupling matrix, the family-level table, the denominators — is recomputed
here from those, with the same code. Slower, but it cannot silently diverge from
a stale copy.

**Figure order is one switch.** `LEAD_WITH_COUPLING` decides whether the paper
opens on the design and the permutation framework or on gene capacity against
protein output. Setting it TRUE does not merely swap Figures 1 and 2: it
promotes coupling to 1 and clade to 2 and demotes design to 3. With it FALSE,
the written order is design, coupling, clade, state, external.

```{r knit-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r fig-setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(tibble); library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork); library(ggrepel) })

## S1A and S1B failed in a render with "could not find function map_dfr" and
## "could not find function assay": both come from packages this document never
## loaded, so whether a panel works depended on what the calling session happened
## to have attached. Declare the rest of the dependencies, and name any that are
## missing rather than letting a panel fail with a confusing message much later.
.deps <- c("SummarizedExperiment", "fgsea", "scales", "survival")
.absent <- .deps[!vapply(.deps, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(.absent))
  message("figures_v2: these packages are not installed, and the panels using ",
          "them will fail: ", paste(.absent, collapse = ", "))

## ---- preflight: make this runnable in a fresh session ------------------------
## v17 writes figure_inputs.rds at the end of a full run. If the objects are not
## already in the session, load them from there. Two names matter: v17 reuses
## `kos` (as a function, in §12a) and `stat` (in §8b's C2), so the figures use
## the snapshots cpl_kos and stat_pitt instead — never the bare names.
if (!exists("paths")) {
  OUT_DIR <- Sys.getenv("ICB_OUT_DIR", here::here("final_run"))
  paths <- list(out_dir = OUT_DIR)
}
FI <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "figure_inputs.rds")
## ALWAYS RELOAD. This was guarded by `!exists("OP")`, so a session that had
## rendered once skipped the load entirely and a re-knit's new objects never
## arrived — the panels kept failing on objects that were in the file all along.
## The bundle is the source of truth for this document; set FIG_NO_RELOAD to
## override when rendering inside a live analysis session.
if (file.exists(FI) && !isTRUE(getOption("FIG_NO_RELOAD"))) {
  .fi <- readRDS(FI)
  list2env(.fi, envir = globalenv())
  cat(sprintf("loaded %d objects from %s (written %s)\n",
              length(.fi), FI, format(file.mtime(FI), "%d %b %H:%M")))
} else if (!file.exists(FI)) {
  cat("no figure_inputs.rds at ", FI, " — knit analysis_v17.Rmd first\n", sep = "")
}
## `off3` is `off2` plus one derived column, the per-set standard deviation of
## plex offsets. v17 builds it but does not export it, so it is rebuilt here --
## which needs `set_offset` and `prot_of`, and THOSE are not in the bundle
## either. In a fresh session the rebuild therefore yields NULL, which is why
## this now runs BEFORE the WANT audit: the audit lists `off3`, and listing it
## is only useful if its value is already settled when the audit reads it.
## Reaching for the rebuild at all is the fallback; add off3 to want_supp in
## analysis_v17.Rmd and this branch stops being load-bearing.
off3 <- if (exists("off3") && !is.null(off3)) off3 else if (exists("off2") &&
         exists("set_offset") && exists("prot_of")) {
  tryCatch(
    off2 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(spread)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(sd_based = vapply(Pathway, function(p) {
        pl <- set_offset(prot_of(p))
        if (is.null(pl) || !all(is.finite(pl))) NA_real_ else stats::sd(pl)
      }, numeric(1))),
    error = function(e) { message("off3 could not be rebuilt: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
} else {
  cat("off3 NOT rebuildable: off2 ", if (exists("off2")) "present" else "absent",
      ", set_offset ", if (exists("set_offset")) "present" else "absent",
      ", prot_of ", if (exists("prot_of")) "present" else "absent",
      " -- S4D will be a placeholder.\n", sep = "")
  NULL
}
WANT <- c(   # every object any panel asks for, not a subset of them
  ## EXPANDED 28 Sep 2026. The panels require 44 objects and this list
  ## loaded 25, so a panel whose object was bundled but unlisted failed with
  ## a message about the object rather than about the list — and where the
  ## name collided with a base function (scan, bs, tot) the failure was
  ## "mutate applied to an object of class function", which points nowhere
  ## near the cause. Derived from the need() calls in this document.
  "OP", "cpl_MP", "cpl_G", "cpl_kos", "cpl_pat", "cpl_stats",
  "gen_coupling", "MGm", "MPm", "SETS_P", "stat_pitt", "pep_g", "pep_ph",
  "pep_fa", "hs", "INFL", "chap_new", "ribo_new", "CHAPERONE_KO",
  "RIBO_KO", "noise_diag",
  "gd_analysis_universe", "MG_DB", "MG_DB_HUMANN", "OS", "SETS_S",
  "annot_new", "bs", "comp_all", "depth", "hi", "off2", "pep_ph_s", "phy",
  "qf", "r2", "sets_s", "sh_comp", "sh_phy", "st0", "st1", "st_s",
  "sysv", "tot", "tot_res", "tot_exposure", "ribo_genus_scan",
  "ribo_blautia_sheba",
  ## ADDED 10 Oct 2026, when these three were asked for by need() and were NOT
  ## in v17's want_supp, so nothing reported them and two panels (S4D, S7C)
  ## were written as error boxes the first time this was knit in a fresh
  ## session. `bp`/`bs4` carry the SHARED-database (vOct22_202403) Bacteroidota
  ## fractions that S7C must plot, which the standalone MetaPhlAn profiles
  ## cannot replace. FIXED ON v17'S SIDE: all three are in want_supp now, so a
  ## current bundle carries them and this listing is the check rather than the
  ## gap. Listing them does not create them -- it makes the knit say so in its
  ## first 20 lines instead of in a panel.
  "off3", "bp", "bs4")
## G, MP, kos and pat are also need()-ed but are aliased from cpl_* below, and
## `paths` comes from the session (stopifnot, below), so none of the four belong
## in this list.
## REMOVED 13 Oct 2026: chap_frac_of, norm_id, mg_clean and scan. These are
## FUNCTIONS, not data, so the present-means-not-a-function rule below reported
## all four as missing on every knit -- a warning that always fires is a warning
## nobody reads, and it would have hidden a real absence. None of the four is a
## panel's data dependency: chap_frac_of is used by no panel here, norm_id has a
## local fallback at the one place it is called, mg_clean is a helper, and the
## genus-scan panel asks for `ribo_genus_scan` and only falls back to `scan` when
## that name happens to hold a data frame, which it checks for itself. Re-derive this with:
##   setdiff(unlist(regmatches(l <- readLines("figures_v2.Rmd"),
##           gregexpr('(?<=need\\()[^)]*', l, perl = TRUE))), WANT)
## exists() alone would report `scan`, `bs` and `tot` as present when they are
## only the base/package functions of those names, which is what made three
## panels fail with messages pointing nowhere near the cause. An object counts as
## present only if the name resolves to something that is not a function.
## Matches need(): absent, shadowed by a function, and present-but-NULL are all
## "not in the session". Without the NULL arm the audit calls `off3` present
## when its rebuild returned NULL, which is the exact state that put an error
## box in S4D.
.have <- function(x) {
  if (!exists(x)) return(FALSE)
  v <- get(x)
  !is.function(v) && !is.null(v) && length(v) > 0L &&
    !(is.data.frame(v) && nrow(v) == 0L)
}
present <- vapply(WANT, .have, logical(1))
if (!all(present)) {
  shadowed <- WANT[!present & vapply(WANT, exists, logical(1))]
  cat("NOT IN SESSION (their panels will be placeholders):\n  ",
      paste(WANT[!present], collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  if (length(shadowed))
    cat("  of these, ", paste(shadowed, collapse = ", "),
        " resolve to FUNCTIONS of the same name, not to data.\n", sep = "")
  if (file.exists(FI))
    cat("  Absent from the bundle — re-knit analysis_v17.Rmd.\n")
}
## the figures use the snapshots; alias them to the short names used below
MP <- if (exists("cpl_MP")) cpl_MP else NULL
G   <- if (exists("cpl_G"))   cpl_G   else NULL
kos <- if (exists("cpl_kos")) cpl_kos else NULL
pat <- if (exists("cpl_pat")) cpl_pat else NULL

stopifnot(exists("paths"), exists("OP"))
FIG_DIR <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "figures_v2")
dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
## capabilities("cairo") reports COMPILE-TIME support, not whether the library
## loads. On this machine (24 Sep 2026) it returns TRUE while cairo.so fails to
## dlopen for want of XQuartz's libXrender/libSM — so the old guard passed, every
## ggsave threw, and the loop printed a line per figure having written nothing.
## Test the device by OPENING one; do not ask whether it exists.
PDF_IS_CAIRO <- FALSE
## Ghostscript, for embedding fonts when the cairo device is unavailable.
## DO NOT RELY ON Sys.which ALONE. On 10 Oct the console reported
## Sys.which("gs") == "/opt/homebrew/bin/gs" while the knit wrote every figure
## with fonts unembedded: a knit runs in a child process whose PATH is the
## system default, and Homebrew's /opt/homebrew/bin is not on it. The symptom
## is silent -- GS_BIN is "", the embed step is skipped, and the only sign is
## one warning in a long knit log. So look on the PATH, then in the places
## Ghostscript is actually installed, then ask R's own finder.
## THE LOGIN-SHELL PROBE IS INSURANCE, NOT A FIX. It was added on 13 Oct on the
## belief that the knit had not found gs. That belief was wrong: Sys.which
## resolved /opt/homebrew/bin/gs, the embed step ran, and it was the embed
## INVOCATION that produced no font (see embed_fonts_checked). The probe stays
## because the 10 Oct failure -- a knit PATH without Homebrew -- is real, and a
## guessed list of prefixes only covers the places someone thought of: MacTeX
## puts gs in /Library/TeX/texbin, conda inside the environment, an unlinked
## Homebrew keg in Cellar. `zsh -lc` resolves the PATH the Terminal sees.
GS_BIN <- local({
  from_login <- function() tryCatch({
    sh <- if (file.exists("/bin/zsh")) "/bin/zsh" else "/bin/sh"
    out <- suppressWarnings(system2(sh, c("-lc", "command -v gs 2>/dev/null"),
                                    stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE))
    out <- trimws(out[nzchar(trimws(out))])
    if (length(out)) out[1] else ""
  }, error = function(e) "")
  cand <- c(Sys.getenv("R_GSCMD"),
            unname(Sys.which(c("gs", "gswin64c"))),
            from_login(),                     # the profile's PATH, not ours
            "/opt/homebrew/bin/gs",           # Homebrew, Apple silicon
            "/usr/local/bin/gs",              # Homebrew, Intel; MacPorts
            "/opt/local/bin/gs",              # MacPorts
            "/Library/TeX/texbin/gs",         # MacTeX
            "/usr/bin/gs",
            Sys.glob("/opt/homebrew/Cellar/ghostscript/*/bin/gs"),
            Sys.glob("~/*conda*/bin/gs"), Sys.glob("/opt/*conda*/bin/gs"),
            tryCatch(tools::find_gs_cmd(), error = function(e) ""))
  cand <- cand[nzchar(cand) & file.exists(cand)]
  if (length(cand)) unname(cand[1]) else ""
})
if (nzchar(GS_BIN)) Sys.setenv(R_GSCMD = GS_BIN)
## Print the VERSION too. Whether a given build embeds a base-14 reference
## depends on the invocation, and when it does not, the version is the first
## thing anyone will ask for. 13 Oct: 10.08.0 embeds with the first invocation
## in embed_fonts_checked(); so do 9.55 and 10.02.
cat(sprintf("Ghostscript: %s\n", if (nzchar(GS_BIN))
  paste(GS_BIN, suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
    paste0("(", system2(GS_BIN, "--version", stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)[1], ")"),
    error = function(e) "(version unknown)")))
  else "NOT FOUND -- fonts will not be embedded"))
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## PDF_ENGINE: which device writes the text
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## "cairo"  grDevices::cairo_pdf. Shapes text through HarfBuzz, which applies
##          ligatures (fi, fl become single glyphs) and positions every glyph
##          individually. Handles any Unicode character in any font.
## "base"   grDevices::pdf with WinAnsi encoding. Positions glyphs from the
##          font's own metrics and applies its kerning pairs, which is what
##          gives evenly spaced text. It cannot draw a character outside the
##          encoding, so check the knit log for "conversion failure".
##
## WHY THE SWITCH EXISTS. The 12 Oct set was set in Helvetica at the right
## sizes and still read wrong: the tracking is loose and uneven, clearest in
## "relative", where the gap between v and e is wide enough to read as a word
## break, and "inflammatory" carries an fl ligature the rest of the label does
## not match. Both are cairo shaping, not the font and not the size.
##
## DEFAULT CHANGED TO "base" ON 12 OCT, on a controlled comparison: the same
## string, the same point size and the same family, rendered through both
## devices on one machine and cropped at 1200 dpi. cairo set it 2.2% wider with
## visibly uneven tracking -- a gap inside "relative" wide enough to read as a
## word break, another in "total", and an fl ligature in "inflammatory" that
## the rest of the label does not match. The base device set it evenly.
##
## It is also cleaner downstream. After the Ghostscript step this file already
## runs, the base device leaves ONE embedded subset named Helvetica; cairo
## leaves two, a simple font and a CID font, both renamed NimbusSans-Regular.
##
## WHAT TO WATCH IN THE LOG. WinAnsi carries the en dash, em dash and the
## characters these labels use, but it cannot draw anything outside it. If a
## panel reports "conversion failure on ...", that character has to be spelled
## out -- or set this back to "cairo" and accept the spacing.
PDF_ENGINE <- "base"         # "base" or "cairo"

PDF_DEV <- local({
  if (identical(PDF_ENGINE, "base")) {
    PDF_IS_CAIRO <<- FALSE
    cat("device: grDevices::pdf, WinAnsi encoding (metric spacing, no ligatures)\n")
    return(function(filename, ...)
      grDevices::pdf(file = filename, useDingbats = FALSE,
                     encoding = "WinAnsi.enc", ...))
  }
  ## Close anything this test leaves open, whichever way it exits.
  on.exit(while (grDevices::dev.cur() > 1L) grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  ok <- isTRUE(capabilities("cairo")) && tryCatch({
    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"); warned <- NULL
    ## withCallingHandlers, not tryCatch: cairo_pdf WARNS ("failed to load cairo
    ## DLL") and keeps going, so a warning handler that unwinds would abort
    ## before dev.off() and leak the device. Muffle, record, then judge.
    withCallingHandlers({
      grDevices::cairo_pdf(f); plot.new(); grDevices::dev.off()
    }, warning = function(cond) { warned <<- conditionMessage(cond)
                                  invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
    isTRUE(is.null(warned) && file.exists(f) && file.size(f) > 1000)
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  PDF_IS_CAIRO <<- ok
  if (ok) grDevices::cairo_pdf else {
    message("cairo does not load at runtime — using the base pdf device. ",
            "Every label in this document is ASCII, so no glyph is lost; only ",
            "font embedding differs. Install XQuartz to restore cairo.")
    function(filename, ...) grDevices::pdf(file = filename, useDingbats = FALSE, ...)
  }
})

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## PNG_DEV / PNG_DPI: a raster copy of every figure beside the vector one
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The PDFs are the archival form and are what the journal wants. Word is not a
## PDF reader: what lands in a .docx is whatever raster the paste produced, and
## the four main figures went to collaborators on 29 Oct 2026 as 80-94 dpi
## bitmaps wrapped in EMF+ with no GDI fallback -- soft in Word and BLANK in
## every renderer that is not Word (LibreOffice's PDF export of the manuscript
## had four empty rectangles where the figures are). So each figure is also
## written here as a PNG at its final printed size, and THAT is the file to
## place in the manuscript. The PDFs still go to the journal.
##
## 600, not 300: Nature asks 300 minimum and 600 for line art, which is what
## these are. 180 mm at 600 dpi is 4252 px, a few MB a figure.
PNG_DPI <- 600

PNG_DEV <- local({
  tag <- function(f, lab) { attr(f, "backend") <- lab; f }
  ## ragg first. It shapes text through the same engine on every platform, so a
  ## figure does not change metrics between this machine and another, and it
  ## needs no X11. grDevices::png(type=) is the fallback -- cairo, then quartz
  ## on macOS -- TESTED rather than assumed, because a type the build does not
  ## carry errors only at the moment of writing, which is the end of a knit.
  if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat("png device: ragg::agg_png at", PNG_DPI, "dpi\n")
    return(tag(function(filename, width, height, ...)
                 ragg::agg_png(filename = filename, width = width, height = height,
                               units = "in", res = PNG_DPI, background = "white"),
               "ragg::agg_png"))
  }
  on.exit(while (grDevices::dev.cur() > 1L) grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  for (ty in c("cairo", "quartz")) {
    ok <- tryCatch({
      f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png"); warned <- NULL
      withCallingHandlers({
        grDevices::png(f, width = 2, height = 2, units = "in", res = 72, type = ty)
        plot.new(); grDevices::dev.off()
      }, warning = function(cond) { warned <<- conditionMessage(cond)
                                    invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
      isTRUE(is.null(warned) && file.exists(f) && file.size(f) > 100)
    }, error = function(e) FALSE)
    if (isTRUE(ok)) {
      cat(sprintf("png device: grDevices::png(type=\"%s\") at %d dpi\n", ty, PNG_DPI),
          "            ragg is not installed; install.packages(\"ragg\") gives text\n",
          "            metrics that match the PDFs on any machine\n", sep = "")
      return(tag(local({
        ty2 <- ty
        function(filename, width, height, ...)
          grDevices::png(filename = filename, width = width, height = height,
                         units = "in", res = PNG_DPI, type = ty2, bg = "white")
      }), sprintf("png(type=\"%s\")", ty)))
    }
  }
  warning("neither ragg nor a cairo/quartz png device works; the PNGs will use ",
          "png()'s default raster backend and its bitmapped fonts.", call. = FALSE)
  tag(function(filename, width, height, ...)
        grDevices::png(filename = filename, width = width, height = height,
                       units = "in", res = PNG_DPI, bg = "white"), "png(default)")
})

## png_dim(): width and height straight out of the IHDR chunk. The whole point
## of writing the PNG is that it is big enough, and a size-in-bytes check cannot
## see that; reading it back through an image package would add a dependency
## for the sake of eight bytes.
png_dim <- function(f) {
  con <- file(f, "rb"); on.exit(close(con))
  if (!identical(as.integer(readBin(con, "raw", 8L)),
                 c(137L, 80L, 78L, 71L, 13L, 10L, 26L, 10L)))
    return(c(NA_integer_, NA_integer_))
  readBin(con, "raw", 8L)                            # chunk length + "IHDR"
  c(readBin(con, "integer", 1L, size = 4L, endian = "big"),
    readBin(con, "integer", 1L, size = 4L, endian = "big"))
}

## save_png(): the PNG twin of a figure already written as `pdf_path` -- same
## object, same millimetres, written from the same loop, so the two cannot
## drift apart the way a separately maintained export would.
save_png <- function(plot, pdf_path, w_mm, h_mm, label) {
  f <- sub("\\.pdf$", ".png", pdf_path)
  if (file.exists(f)) unlink(f)
  ggsave(f, plot, width = w_mm, height = h_mm, units = "mm",
         device = PNG_DEV, bg = "white", limitsize = FALSE)
  want <- c(round(w_mm / 25.4 * PNG_DPI), round(h_mm / 25.4 * PNG_DPI))
  got  <- png_dim(f)
  if (!file.exists(f) || is.na(got[1L]))
    stop(label, " PNG did not write to ", f, call. = FALSE)
  ## A pixel of rounding either way is the device; more than that means dpi or
  ## units never reached it, and the file is not the resolution it is about to
  ## be labelled with. Stop rather than warn: the reason this exists at all is
  ## that low-resolution figures went out looking fine on screen.
  if (any(abs(got - want) > 2L))
    stop(sprintf("%s PNG is %d x %d px; %g x %g mm at %d dpi should be %d x %d. The resolution did not reach the device.",
                 label, got[1L], got[2L], w_mm, h_mm, PNG_DPI, want[1L], want[2L]),
         call. = FALSE)
  invisible(c(w = got[1L], h = got[2L], kb = round(file.size(f) / 1024)))
}

## SETTLED 16 Oct 2026, by removing the design figure rather than by reordering.
## This switch chose whether to lead with the design or the coupling result;
## with `design` gone from order_keys both of its branches named the same four
## keys. It is left defined because the chunk-level audit below and several
## notes still mention it, and FALSE is what every render has used.
LEAD_WITH_COUPLING <- FALSE   # no longer consulted; see order_keys

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## JOURNAL STYLE. Two switches; every size, weight and letter case below is
## read from here and nowhere else.
##
## The house styles genuinely disagree, so this cannot be hard-coded to a guess
## at the target. Nature sets panel labels in LOWERCASE bold 8 pt and all other
## text at 5-7 pt; Cell Press sets them in CAPITALS and allows 6-8 pt. Widths
## and line weights differ too. Picking one and writing it in would have to be
## undone if the paper moves.
##
## PANEL_TITLES is the larger change. Every panel here carries a sentence-case
## argumentative title and a subtitle holding its statistics -- "A patient's own
## metagenome barely beats a stranger's", "median 0.234; +0.006 advantage".
## Published figures in these journals carry neither. In Carter et al. Nature
## 2026 (the comparison paper) not one panel in the main figures or the Extended
## Data has a title or a subtitle: sub-panel headers are bare category names,
## statistics are annotated next to the thing they describe, and everything else
## is in the legend. That is the convention, not that paper's taste.
##
## So the titles are kept for working renders and dropped for submission, and
## when they are dropped their text is written to figure_captions.tsv so it can
## be folded into the legends rather than lost. Nothing is deleted from the code.
## SPLIT 11 Oct 2026. These were one switch, and that was wrong, because the
## two elements are not the same kind of thing and do not deserve the same fate.
##
## The TITLES are argumentative sentences -- "The assays are not too noisy to
## couple", "A patient's own metagenome barely beats a stranger's". They
## duplicate the legend, which Nature requires to carry the panel-by-panel
## meaning anyway, and a claim printed on the artwork reads as advocacy rather
## than as a result. Nothing is lost by dropping them: the legends already
## describe every panel, and the harvest writes the text to
## figure_captions.tsv regardless. Default FALSE.
##
## The SUBTITLES are not duplication. 38 of the 53 carry statistics -- "observed
## -2.41; 1 of 996 draws at or below it", "rho = +0.002, p = 0.99",
## "40 patients, 24 events". Dropping those silently removes numbers from the
## figures, and the published convention is not that such numbers vanish but
## that they are annotated NEXT TO the thing they describe. That is a
## panel-by-panel rewrite, not a switch, so the switch stays TRUE until it is
## done and the triage list in figure_captions.tsv is worked through.
##
## Nature's own final-submission page does not prohibit either one. It
## specifies Helvetica or Arial, panel labels in 8 pt bold lowercase, all other
## text 5-7 pt, and lines 0.25-1 pt, and says nothing about titles. The case for
## dropping them is convention plus duplication, not a written rule -- so this
## is a defensible default, not a compliance fix.
JOURNAL         <- "nature"  # "nature", "cell", or "none" to keep the working look
PANEL_TITLES    <- FALSE     # argumentative, duplicates the legend -- off for submission
PANEL_SUBTITLES <- TRUE      # carry statistics; see the triage note above before flipping

JSTYLE <- list(
  ## Nature: nature.com/nature/for-authors/final-submission and the Nature
  ## research figure guide. Panel labels lowercase bold 8 pt; other text 5-7 pt;
  ## Helvetica or Arial; widths 89 / 120-136 / 183 mm; lines 0.25-1 pt. The
  ## figure guide says a figure should be no taller than 170 mm; the submission
  ## page gives 247 mm as the full page depth, which is what a figure printed on
  ## a page of its own may use. Extended Data is capped at 18 x 24 cm.
  nature = list(tag_case = "lower", tag_size = 8, base = 7, text_max = 7,
                w_full = 183, w_half = 136, w_single = 89,
                h_pref = 170, h_max = 247,
                ## Extended Data is capped at 18 x 24 cm, not set to the grid.
                w_max_supp = 180, h_max_supp = 240,
                lwd_min = 0.25, lwd_max = 1, family = "Helvetica"),
  ## Cell Press: cell.com/figureguidelines. Panel labels in CAPITALS; Arial
  ## only; text 6-8 pt; widths 85 / 114 / 174 mm; strokes 0.5-1.5 pt; every
  ## figure must fit one 8.5 x 11 in page, so the height cap below is that page
  ## less conventional margins rather than a number the guidelines state.
  ## Cell also asks that red and green never carry meaning together -- the
  ## Okabe-Ito palette used here already satisfies that.
  cell   = list(tag_case = "upper", tag_size = 8, base = 7, text_max = 8,
                w_full = 174, w_half = 114, w_single = 85,
                h_pref = 200, h_max = 230,
                w_max_supp = 174, h_max_supp = 230,
                lwd_min = 0.5, lwd_max = 1.5, family = "Arial"),
  ## The look this file had before any journal profile existed.
  none   = list(tag_case = "upper", tag_size = 10, base = 8, text_max = 8.4,
                w_full = 180, w_half = 120, w_single = 90,
                h_pref = 250, h_max = 260,
                w_max_supp = 180, h_max_supp = 260,
                lwd_min = 0.25, lwd_max = 1, family = NA_character_))
if (!JOURNAL %in% names(JSTYLE)) stop("JOURNAL must be one of: ",
                                      paste(names(JSTYLE), collapse = ", "))
JS <- JSTYLE[[JOURNAL]]
TAG_LEVELS <- if (identical(JS$tag_case, "lower")) "a" else "A"

## Only ask for the journal's font if the device can actually find it. A missing
## family does not error in ggplot -- it silently substitutes, and the figure
## looks right here and wrong at the publisher. Check once and say so.
FIG_FAMILY <- local({
  f <- JS$family
  if (is.na(f)) return(NULL)
  ## THIS CHECK COULD NOT FAIL. systemfonts::match_fonts() always returns a
  ## row -- that is what it is for, it resolves a request to the best available
  ## face -- so nrow(...) > 0 was true whether or not the machine had the font,
  ## and the file would have asked for Helvetica and silently accepted whatever
  ## fontconfig handed back. Compare the resolved family to the requested one
  ## and say which was used, so a substitution is visible in the knit log
  ## rather than in the proofs.
  ## font_info() takes the FILE, not the family: passing the path positionally
  ## would hand it to the `family` argument and resolve the fallback all over
  ## again, which is the error this block exists to remove. match_fonts() is the
  ## current spelling and match_font() the old one; both are tried.
  got <- tryCatch({
    if (!requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE))
      if (f %in% names(grDevices::postscriptFonts())) f else NA_character_
    else {
      m <- tryCatch(systemfonts::match_fonts(f),
                    error = function(e) systemfonts::match_font(f))
      pth <- as.character(m$path)[1]; idx <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(m$index)[1])
      if (is.na(idx)) idx <- 0L
      fi <- systemfonts::font_info(path = pth, index = idx)
      as.character(fi$family)[1]
    }
  }, error = function(e) NA_character_)
  if (is.na(got)) {
    message("figures_v2: cannot resolve a font family; using the device ",
            "default. ", JOURNAL, " asks for ", f, ".")
    return(NULL)
  }
  if (!identical(tolower(trimws(got)), tolower(trimws(f))))
    message("figures_v2: ", f, " resolved to ", got, ". ", JOURNAL,
            " asks for ", f, " -- install it, or expect ", got,
            " in the proofs.")
  else
    cat(sprintf("font: %s, resolved\n", f))
  f
})
CAPTIONS <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())   # filled by wrap_titles()

## fig_dims(): snap a declared width to the journal's column grid and check the
## height against its cap. The widths in this file were all written as 180 mm,
## which is not a width either journal uses -- Nature's double column is 183 mm
## and Cell's is 174 mm. Three millimetres is invisible on screen and is a
## rescale at the publisher, so the snap happens here rather than by editing
## twenty literals that would then be wrong for the other journal.
fig_dims <- function(w, h, what, supp = FALSE) {
  ## MAIN figures are set to the journal's column grid. SUPPLEMENTARY ones are
  ## NOT: Nature's Extended Data is sized to the page, capped at 18 x 24 cm, so
  ## snapping 180 mm up to the 183 mm double-column width would push every
  ## supplementary figure 3 mm OVER the limit it is actually judged against.
  ## They are capped instead, and left alone when they already fit.
  if (supp) {
    w2 <- min(w, JS$w_max_supp)
    if (w2 < w)
      cat(sprintf("  %-6s width %g -> %g mm (%s supplementary cap)\n",
                  what, w, w2, JOURNAL))
  } else {
    grid <- c(JS$w_single, JS$w_half, JS$w_full)
    w2   <- grid[which.min(abs(grid - w))]
    if (abs(w2 - w) > 0.5)
      cat(sprintf("  %-6s width %g -> %g mm (%s column grid)\n", what, w, w2, JOURNAL))
  }
  cap <- if (supp) JS$h_max_supp else JS$h_max
  if (h > cap)
    warning(sprintf(
      "%s is %g mm tall; %s caps %s at %g mm. It must be shortened or split.",
      what, h, JOURNAL, if (supp) "supplementary figures" else "a full-page figure",
      cap), call. = FALSE)
  else if (!supp && h > JS$h_pref)
    cat(sprintf("  %-6s %g mm tall: over the %g mm that fits beside its legend,\n",
                what, h, JS$h_pref),
        sprintf("         so it will be set as a full-page figure (cap %g mm).\n", cap),
        sep = "")
  list(w = w2, h = h)
}


PAL_RESP   <- c(NR = "#D55E00", R = "#0072B2")            # Okabe-Ito, as in v1
PAL_COHORT <- c(Pittsburgh = "#E69F00", Sheba = "#CC79A7")
## Two point sizes, not nine. The figures used 1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, 1.8,
## 2 and 2.2 with no principle behind the choices, which reads as carelessness
## when panels sit side by side.

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## COG CATEGORY NAMES, ONE COPY. These lived inside p3c, which was fine while
## one panel named categories. Figure 5b now labels them too, and a second copy
## is how the names drift apart between two panels of the same paper. Hoisted
## here so both read the same map; nothing else about them changed.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Single-letter COG codes are not readable as a main-figure axis. Name the
## categories; keep the letter in brackets so the set is still identifiable.
COGN <- c(J = "Translation [J]", A = "RNA processing [A]", K = "Transcription [K]",
          L = "Replication, repair [L]", B = "Chromatin [B]", D = "Cell cycle [D]",
          Y = "Nuclear structure [Y]", V = "Defence [V]", T = "Signal transduction [T]",
          M = "Cell wall, membrane [M]", N = "Cell motility [N]", Z = "Cytoskeleton [Z]",
          W = "Extracellular structures [W]", U = "Trafficking, secretion [U]",
          O = "Protein turnover, chaperones [O]", C = "Energy production [C]",
          G = "Carbohydrate metabolism [G]", E = "Amino acid metabolism [E]",
          F = "Nucleotide metabolism [F]", H = "Coenzyme metabolism [H]",
          I = "Lipid metabolism [I]", P = "Inorganic ion transport [P]",
          Q = "Secondary metabolites [Q]", R = "General function [R]",
          S = "Function unknown [S]")
## MERGED CODES WERE PRINTED RAW. A KO can sit in several COG categories, and
## those sets carry composite codes -- GM, EH, CQ, IJM, ET, IQ. None is in
## COGN, so pretty_set fell through to the bare string and the axis showed
## "GM" with nothing to say what it meant. Composites are expanded from their
## letters, which handles any combination rather than the six that happen to
## appear in this run.
COG_BARE <- sub(" \\[[A-Z]\\]$", "", COGN)
expand_merged <- function(x) {
  ls <- strsplit(x, "")[[1]]
  if (!all(ls %in% names(COG_BARE))) return(NA_character_)
  sprintf("%s [%s]", paste(COG_BARE[ls], collapse = " + "), x)
}
pretty_set <- function(x) {
  named <- c(O_chap = "COG O: chaperone members",
             O_chap_noGD = "COG O chaperones, minus GroEL/DnaK",
             O_remainder = "COG O: the remainder",
             chaperones = "All chaperones",
             ribosomal = "Ribosomal proteins")
  vapply(x, function(k) {
    if (k %in% names(COGN)) return(unname(COGN[k]))
    if (k %in% names(named)) return(unname(named[k]))
    m <- if (grepl("^[A-Z]{2,}$", k)) expand_merged(k) else NA_character_
    if (!is.na(m)) m else k
  }, "")
}

PT_SMALL  <- 1.3   # scatters and dot plots
PT_BIG    <- 2.1   # a few points carrying a result
PT_JITTER <- 0.7   # points overlaid on a boxplot, deliberately smaller

## Clades had been drawn in the RESPONSE colours: Bacteroidota was the
## non-responder orange and Bacillota the responder blue. Two hues therefore
## meant a phylum in Figure 3 and a patient group in Figures 2, 4 and 5 -- and
## because Figure 3c reports that chaperone protein is densest in Bacillota
## while Figure 4 draws the chaperone result orange, the chaperone story changed
## colour between adjacent figures.
##
## The old scale also failed on its own terms: Pseudomonadota was a pure grey
## (#999999, zero chroma) sitting at dE 5.4 from Actinomycetota under
## protanopia and 14.4 for normal vision -- two clades most readers cannot
## separate. Okabe-Ito has eight slots and this paper needs eight meanings
## (2 response, 2 cohort, 4 clade), so the clade axis is drawn from Paul Tol's
## muted set instead, chosen with the validator rather than by eye: worst pair
## dE 13.3 deutan / 17.5 tritan / 25.2 normal, against 5.4 / 8.6 / 14.4 before.
## None of these four is the response orange or blue.
##
## Order matters: the palest member goes to Pseudomonadota, which no result
## turns on, and the darkest to Bacteroidota, which is the subject of Figure 3.
PAL_CLADE  <- c(Bacteroidota = "#332288", Bacillota = "#117733",
                Actinomycetota = "#AA4499", Pseudomonadota = "#88CCEE")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## style_enrichment(): bring fgsea::plotEnrichment into this file's palette.
##
## Its defaults are a saturated green curve with red dashed rules. That is a
## red-green pair, which is the one combination Cell's figure guidelines name
## explicitly ("do not use red and green together") and the canonical failure
## for the ~8% of men with deuteranopia. It is also the only place in these
## figures where a colour arrives from a package default rather than from the
## palette above, so two panels were drawn in a vocabulary the other fifty-nine
## do not use.
##
## The curve takes the non-responder colour because that is what it shows: a set
## running negative is enriched in non-responders, which is the same thing the
## orange carries everywhere else. The rules go grey -- they are reference
## marks, not results. The member ticks are thinned because at 321 members in a
## 6,939-gene ranking the stock segments merge into a solid black bar.
##
## Both enrichment panels go through this, which they did not before: Figure 4A
## had the tick fix applied by hand and the Sheba panel had nothing, while the
## Sheba panel's own subtitle tells the reader to compare the two.
style_enrichment <- function(g, curve = PAL_RESP[["NR"]]) {
  for (k in seq_along(g$layers)) {
    gm <- class(g$layers[[k]]$geom)[1]
    ap <- g$layers[[k]]$aes_params
    if (gm %in% c("GeomLine", "GeomPath")) {
      ap$colour <- curve; ap$linewidth <- 0.5; ap$size <- NULL
    } else if (gm == "GeomPoint") {
      ap$colour <- curve; ap$size <- 0.5
    } else if (gm == "GeomHline") {
      ap$colour <- "grey60"; ap$linetype <- 2
      ap$linewidth <- 0.3; ap$size <- NULL
    } else if (gm == "GeomSegment") {
      ap$colour <- "grey20"; ap$alpha <- 0.35
      ap$linewidth <- 0.15; ap$size <- NULL
    }
    g$layers[[k]]$aes_params <- ap
  }
  g
}
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
## NAMED, 12 Oct 2026, because theme_set() alone did not reach the panels.
## The first Extended Data set came out with 12 pt panel letters, 11 pt axis
## titles and 8 pt ticks -- ggplot2's factory sizes -- against the 8 and 7 pt
## this block asks for, in a file with no chunk caching and no other complete
## theme call. Whatever the cause, a submission figure must not depend on the
## value of a global at render time, so the theme is an object now and
## wrap_titles() installs it into every panel it passes.
JOURNAL_THEME <- theme_classic(base_size = JS$base, base_family = FIG_FAMILY %||% "") +
          theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
                ## A long title ran under the NEXT panel's tag in Figures 2 and 4.
                ## Titles now wrap rather than overflow, and every panel carries a
                ## right margin so nothing reaches its neighbour's tag position.
                ## Stronger hierarchy: the title should carry the panel and the
                ## subtitle should recede, which at equal weight it does not.
                ## The tag is drawn at npc (0, 1). Without a top margin the
                ## title occupies that same band, and in Figure 4 the B tag
                ## printed inside "Where the signal sits inside COG O". 2 mm
                ## clears a 10 pt bold tag on every panel.
                ## Capped at the journal's maximum for non-label text: Nature
                ## allows 5-7 pt, Cell 6-8. The old 8.4 pt title exceeded both.
                plot.title = element_text(size = JS$text_max, face = "bold",
                                          lineheight = 1.05,
                                          margin = margin(t = 2, b = 1.2, unit = "mm")),
                ## THE TOP MARGIN IS CONDITIONAL, and that is the point.
                ## With PANEL_TITLES on, the title carries the 2 mm that keeps
                ## the patchwork tag out of the text and the subtitle sits under
                ## it. With titles OFF -- the submission render -- the subtitle
                ## becomes the topmost element, inherits no clearance, and is
                ## drawn straight through the tag: in the first Extended Data
                ## set the "e" tag sat on panel d's subtitle and "i" landed
                ## inside panel h's. The subtitle takes the title's clearance
                ## whenever there is no title.
                plot.subtitle = element_text(size = JS$text_max - 0.6,
                                             lineheight = 1.1, colour = "grey35",
                                             margin = margin(t = if (PANEL_TITLES) 0 else 2.6,
                                                             b = 1.8, unit = "mm")),
                ## Sub-panel headers are category names, so they are set plain.
                ## Carter et al. use a light strip with upright text; bold reads
                ## as a title, which is the thing these figures must not have.
                strip.text = element_text(size = JS$base, colour = "grey20"),
                ## "plot" puts the title flush with the plot edge — which is
                ## where patchwork draws the A/B/C tag, so every title collided
                ## with its own letter. "panel" starts it at the panel edge,
                ## past the axis, and the two no longer overlap.
                plot.title.position = "panel",
                plot.margin = margin(3, 4, 1.5, 1.5, "mm"),
                plot.tag   = element_text(size = JS$tag_size, face = "bold"),
                ## A faint grid along the value axis. theme_classic has none, so
                ## reading a value off a dot or bar meant tracking across empty
                ## space; at this weight it sits under the data rather than
                ## competing with it.
                ## Published figures in these journals carry no background
                ## grid; Carter et al. have none in any panel. Kept for the
                ## working view, dropped for submission.
                panel.grid.major = if (PANEL_TITLES || PANEL_SUBTITLES)
                  element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = .25) else element_blank(),
                panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                ## linewidth is in mm; the journals specify points. Both
                ## floors (0.25 pt Nature, 0.5 pt Cell) convert through 1 pt =
                ## 0.3528 mm, and anything thinner can drop out in print.
                axis.line  = element_line(colour = "grey30",
                                          linewidth = max(.3, JS$lwd_min * 0.3528)),
                axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "grey30",
                                          linewidth = max(.3, JS$lwd_min * 0.3528)),
                legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
                legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
                legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "mm"))
theme_set(JOURNAL_THEME)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## type_report(): say what the figures are set in, every time they are written
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The first Extended Data set went out at 12 pt panel letters and 11 pt axis
## titles and nothing in the run said so -- the console reported widths, heights
## and font embedding, all of which were right, and never once printed a type
## size. A knit should not be able to produce a figure set at the wrong size
## silently, so both export loops call this.
type_report <- function() {
  esz <- function(th, el) { e <- th[[el]]
                            if (is.null(e) || is.null(e$size)) NA_real_ else e$size }
  cat(sprintf("type: %s -- base %g pt, panel letters %g pt, titles %g pt\n",
              JOURNAL, JS$base, JS$tag_size, JS$text_max))
  gt <- ggplot2::theme_get()
  bad <- c(if (!isTRUE(isTRUE(all.equal(esz(gt, "plot.tag"), JS$tag_size))))
             sprintf("plot.tag %s", format(esz(gt, "plot.tag"))),
           if (!isTRUE(isTRUE(all.equal(esz(gt, "text"), JS$base))))
             sprintf("text %s", format(esz(gt, "text"))))
  if (length(bad))
    warning("the GLOBAL theme disagrees with JS on ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "),
            " -- something has called theme_set() since this file did. The ",
            "figures are unaffected, because wrap_titles() installs ",
            "JOURNAL_THEME into every panel, but find out what did it.",
            call. = FALSE)
  invisible(NULL)
}
## Wrap a title to the panel width. Titles are set literally elsewhere, so this
## is applied at assembly rather than by editing each one.
## 42, not 46. At 46 a title's last word ran under the neighbouring panel's bold
## tag in the assembled figure — "...barely beats aB", "...output weakly buD".
## The tag is drawn at the panel's top-left corner, so the title must clear the
## width the tag occupies as well as its own.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## SUBTITLE_DROP -- added 11 Oct 2026, after the titles came off
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## With PANEL_TITLES FALSE the subtitles moved up into the space the titles
## vacated and began reading as titles. Each of the 53 was judged against one
## question: does a reader need this to READ THE PANEL? Three things earn a
## subtitle -- a key to an unlabelled graphical element (what the dashed line
## is), a statistic the panel does not already carry, or a caveat without which
## the panel misleads. Nothing else does.
##
## These 15 fail that test. The text is NOT deleted: every subtitle is still in
## the code and still harvested to figure_captions.tsv, so anything wanted in a
## legend is there. Move a name out of this vector to put its subtitle back.
SUBTITLE_DROP <- c(
  ## --- NOTES TO SELF. These two shipped in the 12 Oct Extended Data set, in
  ## a submission render, shouting a word in capitals at a reader who has no
  ## idea what is being corrected. They are reminders written during analysis,
  ## not descriptions of a panel, and nothing in them belongs on artwork.
  "pS1c",    # "the 76% figure is the per-SAMPLE share, an aggregate -- not this"
  "pS10",    # "the gate tests THIS and nothing else -- preservation, extraction
             #  and platform all differ"
  ## --- arguments, not descriptions. A claim printed on the artwork is the
  ## thing a reviewer objects to, and these say nothing the legend cannot.
  "p2var",   # "gene family identity carries most of the variance and most of
             #  the confounds; what the metagenome adds beyond it is the middle
             #  bar" -- three lines of interpretation, the worst of the set
  "p2g",     # "same samples, same two assays, same pipeline; 9.6-fold apart"
             #  -- and the panel already annotates +0.031 and +0.301
  "p3g",     # "both shares move; their ratio does not"
  "p5d",     # was "database share is modest; detection concentrates it". The
             #  subtitle was rewritten on 31 Oct to name the two database
             #  percentages, after a reader took the middle bar for the
             #  database. It STAYS DROPPED from the artwork: the axis labels
             #  now say what each bar counts, and the claim itself belongs in
             #  the Results and the legend, not printed on the panel. The new
             #  text still reaches figure_captions.tsv, which is the point.
  "pS3b",    # "plex structure masks it: within plex the association is stronger"
  "pS5",     # "sizes differ by cohort; ribosomal and chaperone invert"
  "pS6b",    # "the unassignable remainder is not small and is not tested"
  "pS8b",    # "Bacteroidota sits on the 0.05 rule at every floor; Bacillota
             #  reaches it at none" -- readable straight off the panel
  "p3cb",    # "9.7% against 0.9% -- the classes are not evenly distributed
             #  across clades": the two numbers ARE the bars, and the clause
             #  after the dash is the argument
  ## --- duplicates something already inside the panel
  "p3mx",    # "median 0.0024; the chaperone sets' own corrected value is 0.86"
             #  -- 0.86 is in the panel's own FWER inset. The null median 0.0024
             #  is not, and belongs in the legend.
  "p2b",     # "own higher in 34 of 47 patients" -- the panel is a scatter
             #  against the diagonal, so the count is what the reader sees; the
             #  figure also annotates rho = 0.780 inside
  ## --- methods and scope: legend material by Nature's own definition, which
  ## asks the legend to describe what a figure depicts
  "p2c",     # "both axes residualized on plex -- the slope shown is the slope
             #  modelled"
  "pS18d",   # "joint model, each term adjusted for the other; bars at the 235
             #  orthologs both cohorts detect in every sample, range across
             #  prevalence floors 0 to 1" -- the longest subtitle in the set
  "p5led",   # "orthologs contributing two or more proteins" -- already in the
             #  Figure 5 legend, verbatim
  "pS16")    # "the pre-specified primary; compare Figure 4A" -- a cross-
             #  reference, which is what legends are for

wrap_titles <- function(p, width = 42, axis_width = 46, keep_breaks = FALSE) {
  ## strwrap() treats a single "\n" as a space, so an authored line break was
  ## flattened and the text re-flowed at the default widths -- which are set for
  ## half-width panels. keep_breaks wraps each authored line on its own, for a
  ## full-width panel whose subtitle is laid out by hand (Figure 1c). Off by
  ## default, so no other panel changes.
  wr <- function(x, w) {
    if (!keep_breaks) return(paste(strwrap(x, w), collapse = "\n"))
    paste(unlist(lapply(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]],
                        function(l) if (nzchar(trimws(l))) strwrap(l, w) else "")),
          collapse = "\n")
  }
  ## The object's own name, so the harvested caption can be matched to the
  ## panel it came from. Every panel reaches a figure through this function,
  ## which makes it the one place that sees both the text and the identity.
  nm <- tryCatch(deparse(substitute(p)), error = function(e) NA_character_)
  if (!inherits(p, "ggplot")) return(p)
  lb <- p$labels
  ## HARVEST BEFORE STRIPPING. Many subtitles are built with sprintf at render
  ## time, so the source carries the format string and only the object carries
  ## the numbers. Taken here, written to figure_captions.tsv at the end.
  if (!is.na(nm) && grepl("^p[A-Za-z0-9_]*$", nm))
    assign(nm, list(panel = nm,
                    title = if (is.null(lb$title)) "" else lb$title,
                    subtitle = if (is.null(lb$subtitle)) "" else lb$subtitle),
           envir = CAPTIONS)
  ## SUBMISSION RENDER: no panel titles, no subtitles. See the note on
  ## PANEL_TITLES above -- this is the convention in all three journals, and
  ## the text is not lost, it moves to the legend via figure_captions.tsv.
  if (!PANEL_TITLES)    p$labels$title    <- NULL
  ## Per-panel drop, on top of the global switch. Keyed on the object's own
  ## name, which is why this sits here and not in each panel's labs() call:
  ## one list to review rather than 53 edits to audit.
  drop_sub <- !PANEL_SUBTITLES || (!is.na(nm) && nm %in% SUBTITLE_DROP)
  if (drop_sub) p$labels$subtitle <- NULL
  ## NO EARLY RETURN. The version of this function that stripped both and
  ## returned here also skipped the axis-label wrapping below, which is the
  ## only thing that keeps a long axis title inside its panel. That was
  ## harmless while the switch was global -- either every panel kept its
  ## subtitle and nothing returned early, or the whole set was stripped and
  ## every axis was clipped equally, which is visible at once. With a
  ## per-panel drop list it stopped being harmless: the 15 dropped panels
  ## silently lost axis wrapping while the other 52 kept it, and Figure 2b
  ## shipped reading "added by each term (log scal". Wrap first, always.
  if (PANEL_TITLES && !is.null(lb$title))
                             p$labels$title    <- wr(lb$title, width)
  if (!drop_sub && !is.null(lb$subtitle))
                             p$labels$subtitle <- wr(lb$subtitle, width + 6)
  ## Axis labels were never wrapped, so a long one either ran off the panel
  ## (Figure 2b lost "cale)" from "(log scale)") or collided with the label of
  ## the panel beside it (the multiplicity panel ran into the survival panel).
  ## Wrap them on the same rule.
  if (!is.null(lb$x) && is.character(lb$x))
    p$labels$x <- wr(lb$x, axis_width)
  if (!is.null(lb$y) && is.character(lb$y))
    p$labels$y <- wr(lb$y, axis_width)
  ## INSTALL THE JOURNAL THEME INTO THE PANEL, under its own overrides.
  ## theme_set() is consulted at render time, so in principle every panel
  ## already renders at JS$base. In practice the first Extended Data set did
  ## not: it came out at ggplot2's factory 11 pt with 12 pt tags. Rather than
  ## leave a submission figure depending on the state of a global, the theme is
  ## written into the object here -- and the panel's own theme() calls, the
  ## deliberate 4.8 to 5.6 pt axis labels that keep long tick text inside its
  ## panel, are re-applied on top so none of them is lost.
  own <- p$theme
  if (isTRUE(attr(own, "complete"))) {
    ## A panel that installs a complete theme of its own (p1s, the schematic)
    ## keeps it; only the panel letter is forced, so the tags match across the
    ## figure set.
    p <- p + theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = JS$tag_size, face = "bold"))
  } else {
    p$theme <- JOURNAL_THEME
    if (length(own)) p <- p + own
  }
  p
}

## A panel that fails should say so inside the figure, not stop the knit.
## A panel that fails draws a dashed placeholder box and the knit CONTINUES,
## which is right -- one broken panel should not cost you the other 66. But the
## box is then just another small plot in a 6-panel figure, and a knit whose
## console output has scrolled past looks exactly like a clean one. Two panels
## (S4D, S7C) were written as error boxes on 10 Oct and were caught only by
## byte-diffing the PDFs against an earlier set. Every failure now also lands
## in this register, which is reported next to the font check at the end.
.PANEL_FAILS <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

panel <- function(expr, title = "") {
  ## Strip ANSI colour codes: rlang errors carry them, and they rendered as
  ## "[38;5;254m" inside the placeholder box.
  clean <- function(x) gsub("\033\\[[0-9;]*m", "", gsub("\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m", "", x))
  out <- tryCatch(force(expr), error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(out, "error")) {
    assign(if (nzchar(title)) title else paste0("<untitled ",
             length(ls(.PANEL_FAILS)) + 1L, ">"),
           clean(conditionMessage(out)), envir = .PANEL_FAILS)
    msg <- paste(strwrap(clean(paste0(title, ": ", conditionMessage(out))), 42), collapse = "\n")
    return(ggplot() + annotate("text", 0, 0, label = msg, size = 2.4, colour = "grey30") +
             theme_void() + theme(panel.background =
               element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed")))
  }
  out
}
## Archives extract with their own top folder, so `final_run/nulls_sheba` can
## contain `nulls_sheba/` rather than the draws themselves. Search the root and
## up to two levels below it, and report the tree when nothing matches.
## Locate one file by pattern under any of several roots, searching downward.
find_first <- function(roots, pattern, depth = 3L) {
  roots <- roots[dir.exists(roots)]
  seen <- roots
  for (k in seq_len(depth))
    seen <- unique(c(seen, unlist(lapply(seen, list.dirs, recursive = FALSE))))
  for (dd in seen) {
    hit <- list.files(dd, pattern, full.names = TRUE)
    if (length(hit)) return(hit[1])
  }
  NA_character_
}

## `prefer`: "first" takes the first directory found, "most" the one holding the
## most matching files. "most" matters where an archive was unzipped inside a
## folder of the same name — the outer nulls_pitt_full/ still holds the old
## 1,000-draw run while the 10,000 sit in nulls_pitt_full/nulls_pitt_full/, and
## taking the first match silently renders the superseded correction.
find_draws <- function(roots, pattern, depth = 2L, prefer = c("first", "most")) {
  prefer <- match.arg(prefer)
  roots <- roots[dir.exists(roots)]
  seen <- roots
  for (k in seq_len(depth))
    seen <- unique(c(seen, unlist(lapply(seen, list.dirs, recursive = FALSE))))
  hit <- Filter(function(x) length(list.files(x, pattern)) > 0, seen)
  if (length(hit)) {
    if (prefer == "most") {
      nf <- vapply(hit, function(x) length(list.files(x, pattern)), 0L)
      if (length(hit) > 1)
        cat("  draw directories found: ",
            paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", basename(hit), nf), collapse = ", "),
            " -> using the largest\n", sep = "")
      return(hit[which.max(nf)])
    }
    return(hit[1])
  }
  stop("no draws matching ", pattern, "\n  searched:\n    ",
       paste(seen, collapse = "\n    "),
       if (length(seen)) paste0("\n  files in ", seen[1], ": ",
         paste(head(list.files(seen[1]), 5), collapse = ", ")) else "",
       call. = FALSE)
}

## THE ADVANTAGE ESTIMATOR. Every own-versus-stranger number in this paper is
## reported beside a Wilcoxon signed-rank P, and the location estimate that
## belongs to that test is the Hodges-Lehmann pseudomedian, not the median of
## the paired differences. The two were treated as interchangeable until 11 Oct,
## when the ulcerative-colitis cohort showed they are not: median +0.012,
## HL +0.006, difference of medians -0.003 -- three quantities that do not even
## agree in sign. Across the five cohorts only that one moves materially, which
## is the cohort whose per-subject spread (-0.045 to +0.045) is four times any
## point estimate, exactly the regime where a median is unstable and HL is not.
##
## wilcox.test() supplies the estimate and the interval from one call, so the
## interval is the test's own rather than a separate bootstrap that could
## disagree with the P printed next to it.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

hl <- function(d) {
  d <- d[is.finite(d)]
  if (length(d) < 3L) return(c(est = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_,
                               p = NA_real_, n = length(d)))
  w <- suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(d, conf.int = TRUE))
  c(est = unname(w$estimate), lo = w$conf.int[1], hi = w$conf.int[2],
    p = w$p.value, n = length(d))
}

## ---- a subtitle statistic must come from the data -------------------------------
## Six subtitles carried a number typed in when it was first measured. They are
## invisible to every guard here: panel() catches a missing object and need()
## catches a name shadowed by a function, but a literal that has simply gone
## stale renders perfectly. The 13 Oct 2026 sample correction moved several of
## them, and ED7f ended up printing a range its own point labels contradicted.
## stat_sub() formats from the live object and, when that object is absent,
## says so in the panel rather than falling back on the old value.
stat_sub <- function(expr, what = "statistic") {
  tryCatch(expr, error = function(e)
    paste0("[", what, " unavailable in this session \u2014 re-knit analysis_v17.Rmd]"))
}

## the per-clade value a subtitle names, from the table the panel just built
clade_val <- function(d, clade, col) {
  i <- match(clade, d$phylum)
  if (is.na(i)) stop("clade ", clade, " not in this table", call. = FALSE)
  d[[col]][i]
}

need <- function(..., .cols = NULL) {         # use inside panel(): names must exist
  ## `exists()` ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, and three panels failed because of it.
  ## Several v17 objects are named after base or package functions — `scan`,
  ## `bs`, `tot` — so when the data object is absent, exists() finds
  ## base::scan or splines::bs instead, the guard passes, and the panel fails
  ## later with "no applicable method for 'mutate' applied to an object of class
  ## function". Require the name to resolve to something that is NOT a function,
  ## and name the collision when it happens.
  nm <- c(...)
  miss <- nm[!vapply(nm, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) stop("missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  shadow <- nm[vapply(nm, function(x) is.function(get(x)), logical(1))]
  if (length(shadow))
    stop("the data object", if (length(shadow) > 1) "s" else "", " ",
         paste(shadow, collapse = ", "), " ",
         if (length(shadow) > 1) "are" else "is",
         " not in the session; the name", if (length(shadow) > 1) "s" else "",
         " resolve", if (length(shadow) > 1) "" else "s",
         " to a function (base or package). Load the bundle, or run this where ",
         "the v17 chunk that builds ", paste(shadow, collapse = ", "), " has run.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ## NULL IS NOT PRESENT, and this is how S4D shipped an error box reading
  ## "supply both 'x' and 'y' or a matrix-like 'x'". `off3` is rebuilt in the
  ## preamble from off2 + set_offset + prot_of; the last two are not in
  ## figure_inputs.rds, so in a fresh session the rebuild assigns NULL.
  ## exists("off3") then returns TRUE, need() passed, and the failure surfaced
  ## in the cor() inside the subtitle -- a message naming neither the object
  ## nor the reason. An object that is present but empty is a missing object.
  empty <- nm[vapply(nm, function(x) {
    v <- get(x)
    is.null(v) || length(v) == 0L || (is.data.frame(v) && nrow(v) == 0L)
  }, logical(1))]
  if (length(empty))
    stop(paste(empty, collapse = ", "), " ", if (length(empty) > 1) "are" else "is",
         " NULL or empty: present in the session but carrying no data, so ",
         "whatever builds ", if (length(empty) > 1) "them" else "it",
         " failed or was skipped. Add ", paste(empty, collapse = ", "),
         " to want_supp in analysis_v17.Rmd and re-knit it, so the bundle ",
         "carries the object itself rather than the ingredients for a rebuild.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ## Columns. exists() cannot see one, so a frame rebuilt by a narrower path
  ## than v17's passes every check above and then fails on `$col` -> NULL.
  if (!is.null(.cols)) for (x in nm) {
    v <- get(x)
    if (is.data.frame(v)) {
      mc <- setdiff(.cols, names(v))
      if (length(mc))
        stop(x, " is present but has no column ", paste(mc, collapse = ", "),
             " (it has: ", paste(head(names(v), 12), collapse = ", "),
             if (length(names(v)) > 12) ", ..." else "", ")", call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}
## §8f builds the two covariates inside its chunk, as columns of a local data
## frame, so they are not in the session. Rebuilt here with the same definitions.
covars <- tryCatch({
  pw <- purrr::map_dfr(unique(pep_ph$tax), function(p) {
    idx <- pep_ph$row[pep_ph$tax == p]
    tibble(phylum = p, sample = OP$d$sample,
           int = colSums(OP$a[idx, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
  }) |> group_by(sample) |> mutate(frac = int / sum(int)) |> ungroup() |>
    select(sample, phylum, frac) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = phylum, values_from = frac, values_fill = 0)
  inflam   <- colMeans(hs[INFL, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  host_all <- colMeans(hs[,     OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(sample = OP$d$sample, infl_rel = inflam - host_all) |>
    inner_join(pw |> transmute(sample,
                 lr = log2((Bacteroidota + 1e-6) / (Bacillota + 1e-6))), by = "sample")
}, error = function(e) { message("covariates unavailable: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

## draws for the Pittsburgh null, read once
## ONLY DRAWS MADE ON THIS DESIGN (13 Oct 2026). The sample set moved twice that day
## -- 55 to 53 to 54 and back to 55 -- invalidating draws without changing a file name,
## so a draws directory is used only if run_null_2026-10-13.R stamped it with the
## design the figures are drawn from. Panels that need draws degrade to placeholders
## until the new ones are here; they do not quietly render the superseded null.
source(here::here("pitt_sample_corrections.R"))
FIG_DESIGN <- tryCatch(pitt_design_id(OP$d$sample), error = function(e) NA_character_)
## The analysed Pittsburgh arm, for the Figure 1a schematic, derived rather than
## typed: that label read "55 samples" through two changes of the sample set,
## because it is drawn by hand and nothing recomputes it. 75 channels, 55 in the
## arm after section 2's plex rule, minus whatever pitt_drop_list() drops.
PITT_FIG_N <- 55L - length(pitt_drop_list())
draws_match <- function(dir) {
  f <- file.path(dir, "design.txt")
  !is.na(FIG_DESIGN) && file.exists(f) && identical(readLines(f, warn = FALSE)[1], FIG_DESIGN)
}
NULL_DIR <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "nulls_pitt")
pitt_draws <- if (!draws_match(NULL_DIR)) NULL else tryCatch({
  fs <- list.files(NULL_DIR, "^null_pitt_[0-9]+\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(fs, function(f) as.data.frame(readRDS(f))))
}, error = function(e) NULL)
pitt_obs <- if (is.null(pitt_draws)) NULL else
  tryCatch(as.data.frame(readRDS(file.path(NULL_DIR, "observed_pitt.rds"))),
           error = function(e) NULL)
if (!draws_match(NULL_DIR))
  message("nulls_pitt/ was not generated on this design (or is absent): the panels ",
          "built on the permutation null are placeholders in this render")
cat(sprintf("null draws loaded: %s; observed sets: %s\n",
            if (is.null(pitt_draws)) "none" else nrow(pitt_draws),
            if (is.null(pitt_obs)) "none" else nrow(pitt_obs)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The SECOND COHORT'S primary draws, cached the same way
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## WHY THIS IS HERE AND NOT INSIDE A PANEL. Reviewer 5 §4 replaces Figure 5b
## with per-set permutation p in both cohorts, which needs every set's null in
## the second cohort, not just COG O's. p5b already reads this archive for one
## set; reading it twice is a thousand file reads for nothing, so it is read
## once here and both the new panel and anything later can use it.
##
## THE ARM IDENTIFICATION IS THE HARD PART and is NOT re-derived. The directory
## holding the pre-specified primary cannot be found by name -- `sheba_pooled`'s
## draw files match no "^(null|draw)_N" pattern, and two rounds were lost to
## guessing. A draw directory is one holding many .rds files plus an observed
## table, and the primary is the one whose observed COG O matches the
## pre-specified value. That is the same test p5b applies inline; the two must
## stay in step, and p5b should be switched to this helper in its own pass
## rather than in the same change that adds a panel.
SHEBA_PRIMARY_NES <- -1.48
sheba_primary_dir <- function() {
  if (!exists("paths")) return(NA_character_)
  has_obs <- function(x) any(grepl("^observed", list.files(x, "\\.rds$"), ignore.case = TRUE))
  n_draw  <- function(x) sum(!grepl("^observed", list.files(x, "\\.rds$"), ignore.case = TRUE))
  roots <- list.dirs(paths$out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  roots <- roots[grepl("sheba", roots, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  cand  <- Filter(function(x) n_draw(x) >= 100 && has_obs(x), roots)
  if (!length(cand)) return(NA_character_)
  score <- vapply(cand, function(dd) {
    ob <- try(as.data.frame(readRDS(sheba_obs_file(dd))), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(ob, "try-error") || !"NES" %in% names(ob)) return(NA_real_)
    v <- ob$NES[sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(ob$pathway)) == "O"]
    if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_real_
  }, 0)
  ok <- which(is.finite(score) & abs(score - SHEBA_PRIMARY_NES) <= 0.05)
  if (!length(ok)) return(NA_character_)
  cand[ok][which.max(vapply(cand[ok], n_draw, 0L))]
}
sheba_draw_files <- function(x) {
  f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  f[!grepl("^observed", basename(f), ignore.case = TRUE)]
}
sheba_obs_file <- function(x) {
  f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  f[grepl("^observed", basename(f), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
}
.sheba_dir  <- tryCatch(sheba_primary_dir(), error = function(e) NA_character_)
sheba_draws <- if (is.na(.sheba_dir)) NULL else tryCatch(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(sheba_draw_files(.sheba_dir),
                        function(f) as.data.frame(readRDS(f)))),
  error = function(e) NULL)
sheba_obs <- if (is.na(.sheba_dir)) NULL else tryCatch(
  as.data.frame(readRDS(sheba_obs_file(.sheba_dir))), error = function(e) NULL)
## ROWS, NOT DRAWS. The first version printed nrow(sheba_draws) under the label
## "draws" and reported 30000 for a 1,000-draw archive -- the frame is long, one
## row per draw per set, so it is draws x sets. p5b's own line says 1000 and the
## two disagreed in the same knit. Both are printed now, derived rather than
## assumed equal.
cat(sprintf("second cohort: %s; %s rows = %s draws x %s sets; observed sets %s\n",
            if (is.na(.sheba_dir)) "primary archive NOT FOUND" else basename(.sheba_dir),
            if (is.null(sheba_draws)) "no" else nrow(sheba_draws),
            if (is.na(.sheba_dir)) "no" else length(sheba_draw_files(.sheba_dir)),
            if (is.null(sheba_obs)) "?" else dplyr::n_distinct(sheba_obs$pathway),
            if (is.null(sheba_obs)) "none" else nrow(sheba_obs)))
```

```{r shared-helpers}
## Coupling between layers for one patient pair, over a KO set. Same definition
## as §11a; recomputed here rather than carried over, so the figure cannot drift.
EPS <- 1e-9
coup <- function(k, i, j) {
  need("MP", "G", "pat")
  x <- MP[k, pat$sample[i]]; y <- G[k, pat$bio[j]]
  ok <- is.finite(x) & x > 0
  if (sum(ok) < 30) return(NA_real_)
  suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[ok] + EPS), log(y[ok] + EPS), method = "spearman"))
}
Kmat <- function(k) vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(j)
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) coup(k, i, j), 0), numeric(nrow(pat)))

share_of <- function(prots) {
  r <- which(OP$rd$Protein %in% prots)
  colSums(OP$a[r, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) /
    colSums(OP$a[, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
}
## within-plex permutation coefficient, as used throughout §8
## 19 Oct: B 2000 -> 10000. The correction elsewhere in this paper runs at
## 10,000 permutations and this null ran at 2,000, so the reported p had a
## granularity of 1/2001 while the family-wise one had 1/10001.
## WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: it was expected to reconcile the 0.024 here with
## a 0.026 reported elsewhere. It does not. Recomputed at B = 10000 the
## chaperone p is 0.0238 against 0.0240 at 2,000 -- both print 0.024 -- and
## the ratio is 0.760 against 0.756. Only the ribosomal share moves a digit,
## 0.0130 to 0.0141. The 0.026/0.015 pair came from MANUSCRIPT_v18 and SI v3
## and is not in the current text at all, so there was nothing to reconcile.
## Note also that p4e recomputes the same two shares under seeds 51 and 52:
## at B = 10000 seed 51 gives 0.0269 for the chaperone share against seed
## 31's 0.0238. That spread is Monte Carlo noise at about two standard
## errors, not a disagreement -- but it is why the same quantity can print
## two ways, and the seeds are fixed so each panel is reproducible.
perm_coef <- function(y, B = 10000, seed = 1) {
  d <- OP$d |> mutate(yy = y) |> filter(is.finite(yy)) |> droplevels()
  o <- coef(summary(lm(yy ~ Mixture + resp, d)))["respR", 1]; set.seed(seed)
  nl <- replicate(B, {
    rp <- factor(ave(as.character(d$resp), d$Mixture, FUN = sample), levels = levels(d$resp))
    cf <- coef(summary(lm(d$yy ~ d$Mixture + rp))); cf[grep("^rp", rownames(cf)), 1] })
  list(coef = o, p = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(o))) / (1 + B),
       lo = unname(quantile(nl, .025)), hi = unname(quantile(nl, .975)))
}

## 19 Oct: ONE TEST, ONE NUMBER, FOR THE ON-TREATMENT CHAPERONE SHARE.
## ED7a and Figure 4b both report the p for this one comparison and each was
## computing it independently -- ED7a through perm_coef(seed = 31), Figure 4b
## through B45's own permutation of the same model -- so the paper printed
## 0.024 in one panel and 0.026 in the other for a single test. The estimate was
## never in dispute: B45's gap_logit is -0.189331724 and perm_coef's coefficient
## is the same number to every digit it prints, and the odds ratio and interval
## Figure 4b draws are exp() of that model's coefficient and its standard error.
## Only the permutation draws differed, which at p around 0.024 and B = 10000 is
## about two Monte Carlo standard errors of noise.
## seed 31 is the reported procedure. Cached so that the two panels read one
## object rather than two computations, and so a knit pays for it once.
.chap_pitt <- local({
  .v <- NULL
  function() {
    if (is.null(.v)) .v <<- perm_coef(qlogis(share_of(chap_new)), seed = 31)
    .v
  }
})
```

# Cohort, measurement and sampling panels — all Extended Data now (ED1, ED4)

```{r fig1A}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Figure 1c,d: when each cohort was sampled
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## One panel per cohort, on ONE time scale: both use 5-day bins closed on the
## right (a stool taken on the day of the first dose falls in (-5, 0], the
## before side), and the panels' widths are set in proportion to the days each
## spans, so a day is the same width in c as in d. A mirrored single panel was
## tried on 13 Oct and dropped.
##
## SOURCES, reconciled 13 Oct. On treatment: the session's timing (§8b's `tot`,
## else §2f's `jp`), i.e. Rx_start minus Sample_collection_date from
## Lior_UPF_data.csv -- all 55 analysed samples dated since the 13 Oct sample
## corrections (MF0017, the one undated before, is TMT1_126; MF1640, restored the
## same day, is in that file and in no metadata file). Before treatment:
## the analysis roster (B41), the table Table 1 is built from -- 30 dated of 35.
## Every Pittsburgh date the roster carries agrees with Lior_UPF_data.csv to the
## day.
FIG1_BW <- 5
fig1_timing <- function(which) {
  if (which == "on") {
    if (exists("tot") && all(c("rel", "resp") %in% names(tot)))
      return(tibble(t = tot$rel, resp = as.character(tot$resp)))
    if (exists("jp") && "days_before" %in% names(jp))
      return(tibble(t = -jp$days_before, resp = as.character(jp$resp)))
    stop("no on-treatment sampling timing in the session: run §2f (jp) or §8b (tot)")
  }
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B41_supp_tables", "supp_data_sample_metadata.csv")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("the pre-treatment timing comes from ", f, "; run B41_supp_tables.R")
  r <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  r <- r[grepl("^Sheba", r$cohort) & as.character(r$analysed) == "TRUE", ]
  tibble(t = -suppressWarnings(as.numeric(r$Sample_days_pre)),       # + = on treatment
         resp = as.character(r$response))
}
## The window each panel shows, from its own data, snapped to the bins. The
## pre-treatment window gets one bin of room past day 0 so the first-dose line
## is not drawn on the frame.
fig1_xlim <- function(d, pad_right = 0) {
  t <- d$t[is.finite(d$t)]
  c(floor(min(t) / FIG1_BW) * FIG1_BW, ceiling(max(t) / FIG1_BW) * FIG1_BW + pad_right)
}
fig1_when <- function(m) {                     # "9.5 days after", "1 day before"
  a <- abs(m); n <- sub("\\.0$", "", sprintf("%.1f", a)); u <- if (a == 1) "day" else "days"
  if (m > 0) sprintf("%s %s after", n, u) else if (m < 0) sprintf("%s %s before", n, u) else "on the day of"
}
fig1_timing_plot <- function(d, xlim, label, label_at, sub, legend) {
  cnt <- d |> filter(is.finite(t), resp %in% names(PAL_RESP)) |>
    mutate(bin = ceiling(t / FIG1_BW) * FIG1_BW - FIG1_BW / 2) |>
    count(bin, resp)
  ggplot(cnt, aes(bin, n, fill = resp)) +
    geom_col(width = FIG1_BW, colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    ## The cohort's name in the one top corner its own bars cannot reach.
    annotate("text", x = if (label_at == "right") xlim[2] else xlim[1], y = Inf,
             hjust = if (label_at == "right") 1.02 else -.02, vjust = 1.4, size = 2.1,
             label = label) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_RESP, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    ## NOT CLIPPED, and this is why. The y scale is free with 14% headroom at
    ## the top, and coord_cartesian constrains x only -- no ylim anywhere -- so
    ## the tallest bar cannot be cut off whatever the count reaches. Asked about
    ## Fig 1c at y = 15 on 14 Oct; the answer is structural, not a measurement.
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .14))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Days relative to the first dose", y = "Samples", subtitle = sub) +
    theme(legend.position = if (legend) c(.98, .80) else "none",
```
