```{r fig1B}
p1b <- panel({
  need("OP")
  ch <- intersect(c("Channel", "channel", "TMT_channel"), names(OP$d))
  if (!length(ch)) stop("no channel column in OP$d")
  ## CHANNEL ORDER IS REPORTER-MASS ORDER, NOT ALPHABETICAL. The column is
  ## character, so ggplot sorted it and put 127C before 127N in every plex --
  ## the reverse of the masses, and the first thing a reader who knows TMT
  ## checks. The order is built explicitly: 126, then N before C at each mass.
  TMT_ORDER <- c("126", as.vector(rbind(paste0(127:134, "N"), paste0(127:134, "C"))), "135N")
  obs <- as.character(OP$d[[ch[1]]])
  ## THE KIT'S CHANNELS, NOT ONLY THE OCCUPIED ONES. `lv` was built from the
  ## OBSERVED channels, so a channel carrying no analysed sample in ANY plex
  ## disappeared from the axis instead of standing blank. 131C did exactly that,
  ## and the panel showed ten columns of an eleven-plex while its own subtitle
  ## promised "blanks are reference, excluded or empty channels" -- the one
  ## reading a reader who knows TMT will check. scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE)
  ## below was already right; it had nothing to keep. The kit is inferred from
  ## what was observed rather than hard-coded, so an 18-plex run widens the axis
  ## by itself and a future kit does not need this edited.
  TMT11 <- c("126", as.vector(rbind(paste0(127:130, "N"), paste0(127:130, "C"))),
             "131N", "131C")
  kit <- if (all(obs %in% TMT11)) TMT11 else TMT_ORDER
  lv  <- c(kit, sort(setdiff(obs, kit)))
  d   <- OP$d
  d[[ch[1]]] <- factor(obs, levels = lv)
  ## WHAT IS ABSENT, AND WHY, ON THE PANEL. This is the ANALYSED arm, so a gap
  ## in the grid is a channel that carried a reference, an excluded sample or no
  ## sample -- not a channel that failed -- and a plex missing entirely is one
  ## section 2's plex rule removed. A hole in a grid reads as a defect unless
  ## the panel says otherwise, and the cohort was never named here at all.
  all_plex <- tryCatch(sort(unique(as.character(mp$pitt_annot_use$Mixture))),
                       error = function(e) character(0))
  gone <- setdiff(all_plex, as.character(unique(d$Mixture)))
  ## 19 Oct: FULL STOP after "channels". The continuation begins with \n, but
  ## wrap_titles re-flows the subtitle and the break disappeared, leaving
  ## "...empty channels TMT2, TMT5 held no analysed sample..." as one sentence.
  sub <- sprintf("%d analysed channels in %d plexes; blanks are reference, excluded or empty channels.%s",
                 nrow(d), dplyr::n_distinct(d$Mixture),
                 if (length(gone))
                   sprintf("\n%s held no analysed sample under section 2's plex rule",
                           paste(gone, collapse = ", ")) else "")
  ggplot(d, aes(.data[[ch[1]]], Mixture, fill = resp)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_RESP, name = NULL, na.value = "grey85") +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "TMT channel", y = NULL,
         title = "Plex layout and arm balance, on-treatment cohort",
         subtitle = sub) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = .5, size = 6))
}, "ED1F plex layout")
```

```{r fig1Bsheba}
## ED1E -- the same layout for the pre-treatment cohort. ED1d showed only
## Pittsburgh, so the figure that is titled "measurement and provenance" showed
## the plex structure of one of the two cohorts and left the reader to assume
## the other matched. It does not: Sheba is an 11-plex kit in five plexes where
## Pittsburgh is eleven channels in eight, and the arm balance per plex is the
## quantity every within-plex model in this paper conditions on.
##
## THE SOURCE IS THE B41 ROSTER, NOT OS$d, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING.
## `OS` is arm_objs("sheba", "sheba_ontx") -- the 29-channel MS2 arm of §7c --
## while the analysed pre-treatment cohort is the 35 channels Table 1 counts.
## Drawing OS$d here would have put a panel in the paper that disagrees with
## Table 1 by six channels. The roster is the table Table 1 is built from, and
## fig1_timing("pre") above already reads it with this same filter, so the two
## Sheba panels in this submission come from one source.
##
## ONLY ANALYSED CHANNELS ARE DRAWN, which is ED1d's grammar exactly: a blank
## is a reference, an excluded or an empty channel and the subtitle says so.
## The roster carries the reference and excluded rows for Sheba and not for
## Pittsburgh, so drawing them would have made e say something d cannot.
p1bs <- panel({
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B41_supp_tables", "supp_data_sample_metadata.csv")
  if (!file.exists(f))
    stop("the pre-treatment plex layout comes from ", f, "; run B41_supp_tables.R")
  r <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  r <- r[grepl("^Sheba", r$cohort), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(r)) stop("no Sheba rows in ", basename(f))
  r$keep <- toupper(as.character(r$analysed)) == "TRUE"
  ## THE KIT'S CHANNELS, NOT ONLY THE OCCUPIED ONES -- ED1d's rule, for the
  ## same reason and with more force here: 131C carries the reference in all
  ## five plexes and nothing else, so dropping unused levels would delete the
  ## column the word "reference" in the subtitle points at.
  TMT11 <- c("126", as.vector(rbind(paste0(127:130, "N"), paste0(127:130, "C"))),
             "131N", "131C")
  obs <- as.character(r$channel)
  lv  <- c(TMT11, sort(setdiff(obs, TMT11)))
  ## A plex the 2/2 rule removed is NAMED, not drawn as an empty row -- again
  ## ED1d, which names TMT2 and TMT5 the same way.
  keep_plex <- sort(unique(as.character(r$plex[r$keep])))
  gone      <- setdiff(sort(unique(as.character(r$plex))), keep_plex)
  d <- r[r$keep, , drop = FALSE]
  d$ch   <- factor(as.character(d$channel), levels = lv)
  d$plex <- factor(sprintf("Plex %s", d$plex))
  ## 19 Oct: FULL STOP after "channels" -- see the note on the on-treatment
  ## layout panel; the same re-flow ran the two sentences together here.
  sub <- sprintf("%d analysed channels in %d plexes; blanks are reference, excluded or empty channels.%s",
                 nrow(d), length(keep_plex),
                 if (length(gone))
                   sprintf("\nplex %s held no analysed sample under section 2's plex rule",
                           paste(gone, collapse = ", ")) else "")
  ggplot(d, aes(ch, plex, fill = response)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_RESP, name = NULL, na.value = "grey85") +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "TMT channel", y = NULL,
         title = "Plex layout and arm balance, pre-treatment cohort",
         subtitle = sub) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = .5, size = 6))
}, "ED1G sheba plex layout")
p1bs
```

# Figure 1 — Gene capacity against protein output

```{r fig2A}
K_all <- panel({ need("MP", "G", "kos", "pat"); Kmat(kos) }, "UNPLACED coupling matrix")
p2a <- panel({
  if (!is.matrix(K_all)) stop("coupling matrix unavailable")
  ## THIS PANEL USED TO DRAW THE WRONG GEOMETRY. It showed two pooled marginal
  ## densities -- every patient's own value against all the off-diagonal
  ## pairings heaped together -- and then quoted a PAIRED statistic underneath.
  ## The test is a signed-rank test on one difference per patient, each against
  ## the median of their own row, and a pooled marginal cannot show a paired
  ## quantity: at +0.006 the two curves were visually identical, so the figure
  ## argued the null by superposition instead of showing what was tested.
  ##
  ## One segment per patient, their stranger median to their own. The reader
  ## sees the absolute level (around 0.24, which the text quotes), the pairing
  ## itself, and the fact that the segments are flat -- which IS the result.
  ## The bound is what replicates across three cohorts, so the bound is drawn.
  own    <- diag(K_all)
  mis_pp <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(K_all)),
                   function(i) median(K_all[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
  d   <- own - mis_pp
  ## Hodges-Lehmann, not the median: see hl() above. The bootstrap of the median
  ## that stood here gave +0.006 (-0.002 to +0.014) against HL's +0.004
  ## (-0.002 to +0.011) in this cohort, and the two diverge by a factor of two
  ## in the ulcerative-colitis cohort. The P printed in the text for this panel
  ## is Wilcoxon's, so the estimate beside it is now Wilcoxon's too.
  H   <- hl(d)
  adv <- H[["est"]]; ci <- c(H[["lo"]], H[["hi"]])

  pd <- tibble(patient = seq_along(own), stranger = mis_pp, own = own) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(stranger, own), names_to = "which", values_to = "rho") |>
    mutate(which = factor(which, c("stranger", "own"),
                          c("a stranger's", "their own")))
  med <- pd |> group_by(which) |>
    summarise(rho = median(rho, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot(pd, aes(which, rho)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = patient), colour = "grey75", linewidth = .25, alpha = .8) +
    geom_point(colour = "grey45", size = PT_JITTER) +
    geom_line(data = med, aes(group = 1), colour = PAL_RESP[["R"]], linewidth = .7) +
    geom_point(data = med, colour = PAL_RESP[["R"]], size = PT_BIG) +
    annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = Inf, vjust = 1.4, size = 2.2, colour = "grey25",
             label = sprintf("Hodges\u2013Lehmann %+.3f (95%% CI %+.3f to %+.3f)",
                             adv, ci[[1]], ci[[2]])) +
    labs(x = NULL,
         y = "Coupling of proteome to metagenome (Spearman, across KOs)",
         title = "A patient's own metagenome barely beats a stranger's",
         subtitle = sprintf("one line per patient; %d KOs, %d patients",
                            length(kos), nrow(pat)))
}, "1A own vs mismatched")
p2a
```

```{r fig2B}
p2b <- panel({
  need("MP", "G", "kos", "pat")
  Gp  <- G[kos, pat$bio, drop = FALSE]
  core <- names(which(rowMeans(Gp > 0) >= 0.9))
  sdc  <- apply(log1p(Gp[core, , drop = FALSE]), 1, sd)
  top  <- core[order(-sdc)][seq_len(min(200, length(core)))]
  Kt   <- Kmat(top)
  own  <- diag(Kt); mis <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) mean(Kt[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
  ## the control could have failed: between-patient metagenome similarity is not 1
  simil <- median(cor(log1p(Gp[core, , drop = FALSE]), method = "spearman")[
    upper.tri(diag(ncol(Gp)))], na.rm = TRUE)
  ## EQUAL AXES. With the scales free the equality line was drawn shallow --
  ## x spanned about 0.2 and y about 0.43 -- so points above it did not read as
  ## "own beats stranger", which is the only thing this panel is for.
  .rr <- range(c(own, mis), na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(own, mis, patient = pat$sample) |>
    ggplot(aes(mis, own)) +
    coord_equal(xlim = .rr, ylim = .rr) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL, colour = "#0072B2", alpha = .85) +
    labs(x = "Mean coupling to strangers' metagenomes", y = "Coupling to own",
         ## Was "Restricted to the 200 most variable core KOs" — a restriction, not a
    ## finding, and it left a reader facing a scatter with no idea what the two
    ## axes were being compared for. Every other panel title states its result.
    title = "The advantage is clearer where gene content varies most",
         ## 18 Oct: the similarity figure moved out of the panel and into the
         ## subtitle. Floating text inside a square coord_equal scatter sat on
         ## the data and read as an annotation of one point, not of the panel.
         subtitle = sprintf("own higher in %d of %d patients; between-patient metagenome similarity\non core KOs rho = %.3f",
                            sum(own > mis), length(own), simil))
}, "ED3A variable KOs")
```

```{r fig2C}
p2c <- panel({
  need("MP", "G", "pat", "chap_new", "ribo_new", "CHAPERONE_KO", "RIBO_KO")
  mk <- function(koset, prots, lab) {
    k <- intersect(koset, rownames(G))
    tibble(patient = pat$sample, set = lab,
           mg = colSums(G[k, pat$bio, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
           mp = share_of(prots)[pat$sample])
  }
  bind_rows(mk(CHAPERONE_KO, chap_new, "chaperones"),
            mk(RIBO_KO, ribo_new, "ribosomal")) |>
    ## The reported model is qlogis(share) ~ Mixture + log(capacity) + resp.
    ## Plotting the RAW share against log10 CPM showed neither the logit scale nor
    ## the plex adjustment, which is why the ribosomal facet looked flat despite
    ## carrying the SMALLER p (0.011 against 0.026). Both axes are now residualised
    ## on plex, so the slope drawn is the slope reported.
    group_by(set) |>
    mutate(x = residuals(lm(log(mg) ~ OP$d$Mixture[match(patient, OP$d$sample)])),
           y = residuals(lm(qlogis(mp) ~ OP$d$Mixture[match(patient, OP$d$sample)]))) |>
    ungroup() |>
    ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL, alpha = .8, colour = "grey30") +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, linewidth = .5, colour = "#0072B2") +
    ## FIXED, not free. Both axes are residuals of the same two quantities, so
    ## the facets are already on one scale and the panel exists to compare the
    ## two slopes -- which the manuscript reports as nearly equal, rho 0.33 and
    ## 0.29. Free scales redraw each slope against its own range, so the one
    ## with the narrower spread looks steeper and the comparison the panel asks
    ## the reader to make is one the panel defeats.
    facet_wrap(~ set) +
    labs(x = "Log gene capacity, plex-adjusted", y = "Logit protein share, plex-adjusted",
         title = "Set level: capacity tracks output weakly but really",
         subtitle = "both axes residualized on plex — the slope shown is the slope modelled")
}, "UNPLACED set-level tracking")
```

```{r fig2D}
p2d <- panel({
  need("OP", "chap_new", "ribo_new", "pat", "G", "CHAPERONE_KO", "RIBO_KO")
  one <- function(koset, prots, lab) {
    k  <- intersect(koset, rownames(G))
    mg <- log10(colSums(G[k, pat$bio, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) + 1)
    d  <- OP$d |> filter(sample %in% pat$sample) |> droplevels()
    d$y <- qlogis(share_of(prots)[d$sample]); d$cap <- mg[match(d$sample, pat$sample)]
    ## BOTH MODELS. The adjusted estimate alone cannot show what the Results
    ## claim from this panel -- that the response difference keeps 99% and 96%
    ## of its unadjusted value -- because the unadjusted value was not drawn.
    grab <- function(fit, m) { cf <- coef(summary(fit))
      tibble(set = lab, model = m, est = cf["respR", 1], se = cf["respR", 2]) }
    bind_rows(grab(lm(y ~ Mixture + resp, d),       "no capacity term"),
              grab(lm(y ~ Mixture + cap + resp, d), "gene capacity in the model"))
  }
  .d <- bind_rows(one(CHAPERONE_KO, chap_new, "chaperones"),
                  one(RIBO_KO, ribo_new, "ribosomal"))
  .d$model <- factor(.d$model, levels = c("no capacity term", "gene capacity in the model"))
  .kept <- vapply(split(.d, .d$set), function(z)
    100 * z$est[z$model == "gene capacity in the model"] /
          z$est[z$model == "no capacity term"], 0)
  .d |>
    ggplot(aes(est, set, colour = model)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = est - 1.96 * se, xmax = est + 1.96 * se), size = .3,
                    position = position_dodge(width = .5)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("no capacity term" = "grey55",
                                   "gene capacity in the model" = "#0072B2"),
                        name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Response coefficient", y = NULL,
         subtitle = sprintf("with capacity in the model the difference keeps %.0f%% of its unadjusted value for chaperones and %.0f%% for ribosomal proteins",
                            .kept[["chaperones"]], .kept[["ribosomal"]]),
         ## Was "The difference persists with capacity adjusted". Which difference?
    ## This panel sits in the coupling figure, where a reader has been reading
    ## about gene capacity and not about response, so the title assumed context
    ## the figure does not supply. Named explicitly, it also earns its place
    ## here: it is a statement about what gene capacity does NOT explain.
    title = "Gene capacity does not explain the response difference") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
          legend.key.size = grid::unit(3, "mm"))
}, "ED7C conditioned response")
p2d
```

```{r fig2E}
p2e <- panel({
  need("OP", "pep_g", "chap_new", "pat")
  gen <- count(pep_g, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  base <- perm_coef(qlogis(share_of(chap_new)), B = 500, seed = 11)$coef
  out <- bind_rows(lapply(gen, function(g) {
    drop_rows <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g]
    keep <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(OP$a)), drop_rows)
    y <- colSums(OP$a[intersect(keep, which(OP$rd$Protein %in% chap_new)),
                      OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) /
         colSums(OP$a[keep, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    d <- OP$d |> mutate(yy = qlogis(y)) |> filter(is.finite(yy)) |> droplevels()
    tibble(genus = g, est = coef(summary(lm(yy ~ Mixture + resp, d)))["respR", 1])
  }))
  ## THE AXIS MUST INCLUDE ZERO. The whole range is a few thousandths wide, and
  ## an axis fitted to the data alone spread it edge to edge and turned a 4%
  ## variation into a dramatic one -- `rng` was computed to say so and then never
  ## used. Including zero puts the spread on the scale of the effect it is a
  ## sensitivity analysis of, which is the only scale on which "no single genus
  ## carries it" can be judged.
  rng <- diff(range(out$est))
  ggplot(out, aes(est, reorder(genus, est))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 1, linewidth = .3, colour = "grey75") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = base, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3, colour = "#0072B2") +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = range(c(0, out$est, base)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = .04)) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.2)) +
    ## 19 Oct: SHORTER AXIS TITLE. At 43 characters it sat just under
    ## wrap_titles' 46-character axis wrap, so it never wrapped and lost its
    ## final "d" off the edge of a 60 mm cell. The y axis names the genera, so
    ## "this" was carrying nothing the reader did not already have.
    labs(x = "Coefficient with this genus removed", y = NULL,
         title = "No single genus carries it",
         subtitle = sprintf("dashed: all genera included (%.3f); the whole range spans %.4f, against zero on the same axis",
                            base, rng)) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.5))
}, "ED8G leave-one-genus-out")
p2e
```

```{r fig2F}
## the clade result: phylum, family and genus on one panel
## SUPERSEDED by Figure 3 panel A, which draws the same quantity with the clade
## structure as its subject rather than as an aside. Retained because it is cheap
## and a reviewer may ask for it standalone, but it is not assembled into any
## figure.
p2f <- panel({
  need("gen_coupling")
  ## §11c's family table lives inside its local() block, so it is rebuilt here
  ## from the two exported layer matrices rather than assumed to be in scope.
  d <- gen_coupling |> transmute(level = "genus", taxon = genus, phylum, rho = rho_clr)
  fam <- tryCatch({
    need("MGm", "MPm", "pep_fa", "pep_ph")
    fp <- pep_fa |> select(row, family = tax) |>
      inner_join(pep_ph |> select(row, phylum = tax), by = "row") |>
      count(family, phylum) |> group_by(family) |> slice_max(n, n = 1) |> ungroup()
    tx <- intersect(colnames(MGm), fp$family)
    if (length(tx) < 4) stop("family layer not available at this resolution")
    clrf <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
    a <- clrf(MGm[, tx, drop = FALSE]); b <- clrf(MPm[, tx, drop = FALSE])
    tibble(level = "family", taxon = tx,
           phylum = fp$phylum[match(tx, fp$family)],
           rho = vapply(tx, function(t) suppressWarnings(
             cor(a[, t], b[, t], method = "spearman")), 0))
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(fam)) d <- bind_rows(d, fam)
  d$level <- factor(d$level, levels = c("genus", "family"))
  ggplot(d, aes(rho, level, colour = phylum)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(height = .12), size = 1.3, alpha = .9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_CLADE, name = NULL, na.value = "grey70") +
    labs(x = "Metagenome against proteome,\nacross patients (CLR, Spearman)", y = NULL,
         title = "Every clade couples except Bacteroidota") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}, "UNPLACED clade coupling")
p2f
```

```{r fig2-assemble}
p2g <- panel({
  ## THE POSITIVE CONTROL, and the strongest single comparison in the paper.
  ## Both quantities on the same axis: one feature, correlated across patients.
  ## The measurement chain is not too noisy to couple — it couples taxonomy about
  ## ten times better than it couples function, in the same samples.
  need("noise_diag")
  nd <- noise_diag
  d <- bind_rows(
    tibble(rho = nd$rho_genus,  what = "genus abundance"),
    tibble(rho = nd$rho_family, what = "gene-family protein output")) |>
    filter(is.finite(rho)) |>
    mutate(what = factor(what, levels = c("genus abundance", "gene-family protein output")))
  md <- d |> group_by(what) |> summarise(m = median(rho), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  ratio <- md$m[1] / md$m[2]
  ggplot(d, aes(rho, what, fill = what)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_violin(colour = NA, alpha = .45, scale = "width") +
    geom_boxplot(width = .16, outlier.size = .3, linewidth = .3, fill = "white") +
    geom_point(data = md, aes(m, what), size = 1.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    ## 28 Oct: NUDGED CLEAR OF THE VIOLIN. vjust alone lifts the label by a
    ## fraction of a line, which left it sitting on the violin fill; a
    ## scale = "width" violin reaches 0.45 above the row centre, so the label
    ## has to be nudged past that in data units and the top of the scale
    ## expanded to give the upper row's label somewhere to go.
    geom_text(data = md, aes(m, what, label = sprintf("%+.3f  (n = %d)", m, n)),
              position = position_nudge(y = 0.47), vjust = 0,
              size = 2.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    ## 19 Oct: CLIP OFF. The label is centred on the median, and for the genus
    ## row that put "(n = 29)" past the panel edge with its bracket cut. This
    ## panel sits beside a spacer in ED3, so the overflow has somewhere to go
    ## and the axis keeps its range.
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.55, 0.9))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("genus abundance" = "#0072B2",
                                 "gene-family protein output" = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "Metagenome vs proteome, across patients\n(Spearman)", y = NULL,
         title = "The assays are not too noisy to couple — they couple taxonomy",
         subtitle = sprintf("same samples, same two assays, same pipeline; %.1f-fold apart", ratio)) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.4))
}, "ED3E positive control")

p2h <- panel({
  ## The noise objection from the other two directions: depth and resampling.
  ## NOT A CEILING. The resample is drawn from a multinomial centred on the
  ## patient's OBSERVED gene vector, so it asks what a FURTHER round of counting
  ## noise costs, not what the coupling would be with noise removed. Reporting
  ## it as "observed is 99% of the ceiling" is the error analysis_v17 §11[C]
  ## corrects and the SI disclaims; the deeper-sequencing claim rests on the
  ## depth result in the subtitle, which is [A]. If counting noise of this
  ## magnitude limited the coupling, points would sit below the diagonal and the
  ## advantage would rise with depth. Neither happens.
  need("noise_diag")
  nd <- noise_diag
  d <- tibble(own = nd$own, ceiling = nd$ceiling,
              depth = if (length(nd$depth) == length(nd$own)) nd$depth else NA_real_) |>
    filter(is.finite(own), is.finite(ceiling))
  ## 28 Oct: WRAPPED. One line at this size overran the panel and the last word
  ## was sheared off at the right edge -- the annotation is drawn inside the
  ## panel, so nothing in wrap_titles() reaches it. The scatter runs along the
  ## diagonal and its top-left quadrant is empty, so three short lines sit there
  ## clear of both the points and the reference line.
  lab <- sprintf("observed %.3f;\n%.3f after a further\nround of resampling",
                 median(d$own), median(d$ceiling))
  ggplot(d, aes(ceiling, own)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = 3, colour = "grey55") +
    geom_point(aes(colour = log10(depth)), size = 1.3) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "Log10 reads", na.value = "grey45",
                           guide = guide_colourbar(barheight = unit(12, "mm"))) +
    annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = lab, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.25,
             size = 2.2, lineheight = 0.95) +
    labs(x = "Coupling after the counts are drawn again\nat the scale of the normalized table",
         y = "Observed coupling",
         title = "Deeper sequencing would not close the gap",
         subtitle = sprintf("points on the diagonal; advantage against depth rho = %+.3f, p = %.2f",
                            nd$depth_rho, nd$depth_p)) +
    ## BOTTOM, not right. p2h is half width now (ED3 is one row of two), and a
    ## vertical colour bar on the right takes that width out of the plotting
    ## area. Horizontal underneath costs height, which this figure has.
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
          legend.key.height = grid::unit(2.4, "mm"),
          legend.key.width  = grid::unit(7, "mm"))
}, "ED3C noise ceiling")

## 2E (leave-one-genus-out) is a control for the RESPONSE effect and belongs with
## the other controls in Supplementary 12, not in a Pillar 1 figure. 2F duplicates
## Figure 3's panel A. Both are replaced by the two panels above, which are what
## R2 now argues.
## p2h ("Deeper sequencing would not close the gap") moves to Supplementary: it
## excludes an explanation rather than establishing a result. p2g, the taxonomy
## positive control, STAYS — it is the evidence that the assays work at all,
## without which the coupling null cannot be read as a finding.
## p2d ("The difference persists with capacity adjusted") is a RESPONSE result in
## the coupling figure; it is left in place for now but belongs with Figure 4.
p2var <- panel({
  ## From B2's variance partition, 33,561 patient-KO rows on the 55-sample /
  ## 48-paired design (v17 section 11b, 13 Oct 2026).
  ##
  ## 18 Oct: ONLY THE TWO COMPETING TERMS ARE PLOTTED, ON A LINEAR AXIS.
  ## The panel used to carry all three increments on a log axis from 5e-5 to 9.
  ## That put the one term that is not a finding -- gene family identity at
  ## 0.74786, which says only that abundant proteins are abundant -- in charge
  ## of the scale, and jammed the two terms the panel exists to compare into
  ## the leftmost few millimetres. The eightyfold difference could not be read
  ## off it; the printed values were doing the work, which makes it a table.
  ## Gene family identity is the model's starting point and now says so in the
  ## subtitle instead of being drawn.
  ##
  ## BARS ARE CORRECT HERE, AND WERE NOT BEFORE. The old objection was specific
  ## to the log axis, where a bar runs from log(axis minimum) rather than from
  ## zero, so its length is set by `limits` and not by the data. On a linear
  ## axis with a real zero, length IS the value and the 80x ratio is the
  ## picture rather than a caption.
  ##
  ## TYPED, NOT DRAWN: B2 is not in the run_reanalysis chain, so these do not
  ## move when the design does. They were 0.75092 / 0.00010 / 0.00675 over
  ## 32,912 rows on the 47-paired design and were still being plotted after
  ## the design moved to 48. Change them here against v17's printed partition.
  KO_ID <- 0.74786                       # context only, not plotted
  d <- data.frame(
    term = factor(c("Abundance of that gene\nin the same patient",
                    "Which patient the sample came from"),
                  levels = c("Which patient the sample came from",
                             "Abundance of that gene\nin the same patient")),
    inc  = c(0.00008, 0.00662) * 100)
  ggplot(d, aes(inc, term)) +
    geom_col(width = .38, fill = "grey35") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f%%", inc)), hjust = -0.2, size = 2.3) +
    ## LIMIT 1.0, NOT 0.8. The 0.662 bar leaves 0.138 of axis to its right at
    ## 0.8, and "0.662%" at 2.3 pt needs about 0.15 -- the per cent sign was
    ## clipped at the panel edge on the 18 Oct render. 1.0 is also the natural
    ## bound for an axis in per cent.
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .02))) +
    labs(x = "Variance in protein output explained, added by each term (%)",
         y = NULL,
         title = "The patient matters more than their own gene abundance",
         subtitle = sprintf(paste("both are added to a model that already knows which gene family",
                                  "it is (%.1f%%);\nknowing only which patient, with no sequence at",
                                  "all, adds %.0f times what the\nmatched metagenome adds"),
                            KO_ID * 100, 0.00662 / 0.00008)) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}, "1B variance partition")

## Panel order follows the order the text cites them, not the order they were
## written. The variance partition is cited immediately after the own-versus-
## stranger result, so it is B; everything after it shifts one letter.
## REVIEWER 5 §4. p2d out, p5e in, and the panel count is unchanged so the
## height is too. p2d (the conditioned response coefficients on gene capacity)
## is two points with intervals that nearly touch zero and carried less than a
## sentence of text here; it moves to ED8, beside the other response
## coefficients. p5e comes the other way from ED3: it is the per-arm advantage
## WITH the coupling level in each row label, so it is the one panel that shows
## coupling rising 0.24 -> 0.68 across resolutions while the advantage stays at
## zero. That is the answer to "your assays are too noisy to agree" and it was
## only in Extended Data.
## ASSEMBLED LATER, not here. p5e is defined further down the file, so composing
## this figure in its own chunk would be a forward reference -- `object 'p5e' not
## found` -- which is the failure the clade figure already taught this file once.
## Both Figure 2 and Figure 4 are now composed in `assemble-mains`, immediately
## before the write loop, where every panel they use exists.
```

```{r fig2-five-cohort}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## p2five -- the own-minus-stranger advantage in all five cohorts, one estimator
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ADDED 15 Oct. The five-cohort result was the paper's broadest claim and its
## least visible one: Figure 2 showed only this study's two cohorts, and the
## three independent datasets lived in Supplementary Note 7. Read quickly, that
## makes a general result about metagenomic inference look like a melanoma
## multi-omics paper with a supplement.
##
## ONLY THE ADVANTAGE IS PLOTTED, never the absolute coupling. The five studies
## quantify protein three different ways -- TMT reporter intensity, spectral
## counts, LFQ MS1 -- and absolute coupling is not comparable across them; Note
## 7 says so explicitly. The own-minus-stranger difference IS comparable,
## because it is a within-subject contrast: each subject's own pairing against
## their own strangers, on that study's own scale. That is the whole reason
## this panel can exist and a coupling-vs-coupling panel cannot.
##
## The three quantification methods are named in the row labels rather than
## hidden, because the platform spread is the argument: three ways of counting
## protein, five cohorts, four disease states, and no interval clears zero.
p2five <- panel({
  .f <- file.path(dirname(paths$out_dir), "hl_all_cohorts.tsv")
  if (!file.exists(.f)) .f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "hl_all_cohorts.tsv")
  if (!file.exists(.f))
    stop("p2five: hl_all_cohorts.tsv not found beside or under ", paths$out_dir,
         ". It is written by the B30 external-coupling scripts.", call. = FALSE)
  .d <- utils::read.delim(.f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  ## "swap MG" is the comparison the paper reports -- a patient's proteome
  ## against their own metagenome versus against strangers'. "swap MP" is the
  ## symmetric control and belongs in the supplement, not here.
  .d <- .d[.d$direction == "swap MG", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(.d) != 5L)
    stop("p2five: expected 5 swap-MG rows, found ", nrow(.d), call. = FALSE)
  ## Plain-language cohort labels. The file's own names are internal.
  .lab <- c("Pittsburgh"  = "Melanoma, on treatment",
            "Sheba"       = "Melanoma, before treatment",
            "Tanca 2017"  = "Healthy adults",
            "Elinav ISR"  = "Crohn's disease",
            "Elinav UC"   = "Ulcerative colitis")
  .miss <- setdiff(.d$cohort, names(.lab))
  if (length(.miss))
    stop("p2five: unlabelled cohort(s): ", paste(.miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  ## 18 Oct: THE PITTSBURGH ROW IS RECOMPUTED, NOT READ FROM THE FILE.
  ## hl_all_cohorts.tsv was written on 12 Oct against the 47-paired design and
  ## still carried n = 47 for this cohort while panel a and the Results report
  ## 48. The two agreed only to the printed precision -- 0.00385 against
  ## 0.00407, both of which render as +0.004, and the interval rounded the same
  ## way too -- so nothing visibly contradicted and the stale row would have
  ## shipped. Deriving it from the matrix panel a already builds removes the
  ## second source of truth rather than refreshing it, so the two panels cannot
  ## drift apart again when the design moves.
  if (exists("K_all") && is.matrix(K_all) && exists("hl")) {
    .own <- diag(K_all)
    .str <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(K_all)),
                   function(i) median(K_all[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
    .dd  <- .own - .str
    .H   <- hl(.dd)
    .i   <- which(.d$cohort == "Pittsburgh")
    if (length(.i) == 1L && is.finite(.H[["est"]])) {
      .d$n[.i]     <- .H[["n"]]
      .d$pos[.i]   <- sum(.dd > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
      .d$hl[.i]    <- .H[["est"]]
      .d$hl_lo[.i] <- .H[["lo"]]
      .d$hl_hi[.i] <- .H[["hi"]]
      .d$P[.i]     <- .H[["p"]]
    }
  } else {
    message("p2five: K_all or hl() unavailable -- Pittsburgh row left as the ",
            "file has it. Check its n against panel a before shipping.")
  }
  .d$this_study <- .d$cohort %in% c("Pittsburgh", "Sheba")
  ## COLOUR BY COHORT, NOT BY "is it ours". Both of this study's rows were
  ## drawn in PAL_COHORT[["Pittsburgh"]], so SHEBA WAS AMBER HERE AND PINK IN
  ## PANEL c -- the same cohort, two colours, one figure, with c's legend
  ## sitting directly above d naming pink as Sheba. PAL_COHORT is keyed by
  ## site and is what every other panel in this file uses; the three
  ## independent datasets keep the neutral grey that says "not ours".
  .d$ckey <- ifelse(.d$this_study, .d$cohort, "external")
  .d$row <- sprintf("%s\n%s, n = %s", .lab[.d$cohort], .d$quant, .d$n)
  ## Order: this study first, then the independent datasets by size. The point
  ## of the panel is that the three below behave like the two above.
  .d <- .d[order(!.d$this_study, -as.numeric(.d$n)), , drop = FALSE]
  .d$row <- factor(.d$row, levels = rev(.d$row))
  ggplot(.d, aes(hl, row, colour = ckey)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = hl_lo, xmax = hl_hi), linewidth = .6) +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL * 1.4) +
    ## guide = "none" STAYS: panel c is immediately above with the same two
    ## cohort colours and its own legend, so a second copy of it here would be
    ## the same key twice in one figure.
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Pittsburgh = unname(PAL_COHORT[["Pittsburgh"]]),
                                   Sheba      = unname(PAL_COHORT[["Sheba"]]),
                                   external   = "grey35"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .12))) +
    ## 18 Oct: matches the y title of panel c -- two lines, method in
    ## smaller type via plotmath scriptstyle().
    labs(x = bquote(atop("Own" - "stranger",
                         scriptstyle("(Hodges\u2013Lehmann, 95% interval)"))), y = NULL,
         title = "The same answer in five cohorts, on three quantification platforms",
         subtitle = paste("no interval excludes zero and none reaches +0.015;",
                          "absolute coupling is not comparable across platforms",
                          "and is not shown"))
}, "1D five cohorts")
p2five
```

```{r fig3AB}
p3a <- panel({
  need("stat_pitt", "SETS_P")   # NOT `stat`: C2 reassigns it in §8b
  g <- style_enrichment(fgsea::plotEnrichment(SETS_P[["O"]], stat_pitt))
  g + labs(title = "COG O running enrichment, Pittsburgh",
           x = "Rank in the response-ordered proteome", y = "Enrichment score")

p3b <- panel({
  if (is.null(pitt_draws)) stop("null draws not found")
  x <- pitt_draws$NES[pitt_draws$pathway == "chaperones"]
  ob <- pitt_obs$NES[pitt_obs$pathway == "chaperones"]
  ggplot(data.frame(NES = x), aes(NES)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 44, fill = "grey82", colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    ## The shaded draws are those AT OR BELOW the observed value -- one-sided, in
    ## the required direction. That area is NOT the reported p. `p_drop` is
    ## two-sided with NES < 0 required, so it counts |NES| >= |observed| and comes
    ## out larger: 3 draws for this set against the 1 shaded here, p = 0.004
    ## against 1/996. Label the count for what it is and let the legend carry the
    ## difference; do not describe the shaded area as the p-value.
    geom_histogram(data = data.frame(NES = x[x <= ob]), bins = 44,
                   fill = PAL_RESP[["NR"]], alpha = .5, colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ob, colour = PAL_RESP[["NR"]], linewidth = .6) +
    labs(x = "NES under permutation", y = "Draws", title = "Chaperone set against its null",
         ## na.rm: a draw that failed to score leaves an NA, and without this the
         ## whole count printed as "NA of 1000 draws".
         subtitle = sprintf("observed %+.2f; %d of %d draws at or below it",
                            ob, sum(x <= ob, na.rm = TRUE), sum(is.finite(x))))
}, "3C chaperone null")
p3a; p3b
```

```{r fig3C}
p3c <- panel({
  if (is.null(pitt_obs)) stop("observed sets not found")
  ## THE FOUR CHAPERONE SETS ARE NESTED, and stacked at the bottom of an
  ## ordered panel they read as four independent hits. They are not: COG O
  ## contains its chaperone members, which contain those minus GroEL and DnaK,
  ## and the full chaperone set overlaps all three. Marked with a hollow shape
  ## and stated in the subtitle, because a reader counting extreme rows is the
  ## failure mode this panel has.
  NESTED <- c("O", "O_chap", "O_chap_noGD", "chaperones")
  q <- pitt_obs |> mutate(hl = pathway %in% c("O", "O_chap", "chaperones"),
                          nested = pathway %in% NESTED,
                          lab = pretty_set(pathway))
  ## NO SHADED BAND HERE, deliberately. A grey region on a NES plot reads as a
  ## significance threshold to most readers, and nothing in this family is
  ## significant — the family-wise value for these sets is 0.86. A band marking
  ## "the most extreme tenth" would be descriptive but would be read as a
  ## threshold, which is exactly the overclaim this manuscript spends its
  ## multiplicity section avoiding. The highlight colour already separates the
  ## reported sets from the rest.
  ## TWO COLUMNS OF FIFTEEN. Thirty named rows in one column had about 1.7 mm
  ## each, and 5.5 pt type needs 2.2; raising the panel to 1.7 of a row bought
  ## height and still lost. No font size solves thirty rows in fifty millimetres.
  ## Split by rank instead: the panel is a one-dimensional scatter given the full
  ## page width, so the width is there to spend, and fifteen rows per column have
  ## room for 6 pt -- above the journal floor rather than under it. Ordering
  ## still reads down the left column and on down the right.
  q <- q[order(q$NES), ]
  q$col <- rep(c("lower half", "upper half"),
               c(ceiling(nrow(q) / 2), nrow(q) - ceiling(nrow(q) / 2)))
  ggplot(q, aes(NES, reorder(lab, NES), colour = hl)) +
    facet_wrap(~ col, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    ## Hollow for the nested sets, filled for every independent one. Shape, not
    ## colour: colour already carries "reported", and the two facts are
    ## different -- a set can be reported and independent (ribosomal) or nested
    ## and not separately reported (O_chap_noGD).
    geom_point(aes(shape = nested), size = PT_SMALL) +
    ## A FILLED DIAMOND, NOT A HOLLOW CIRCLE. Open against filled is the
    ## near-universal not-significant / significant channel in this literature,
    ## so a hollow point said the opposite of what these four sets are.
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 18, `FALSE` = 16), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL_RESP[["NR"]], `FALSE` = "grey65"),
                        guide = "none") +
    ## Was "All 30 sets in the family". Since the multiplicity work, "the family"
    ## means the 565-set correction family throughout the manuscript; these are
    ## the 30 reported sets, which is a different thing.
    labs(x = "Observed NES", y = NULL, title = "The 30 reported sets, ranked",
         ## ONE LINE, not four. At the 5.5 pt floor the 30 labels need every
         ## millimetre of this panel; the nesting is spelled out in the legend.
         subtitle = "diamonds are four nested sets, not four independent hits") +
    ## 4.8 pt was below Nature's 5 pt floor AND still overlapping, because 30
    ## rows do not fit the height this panel had. Type goes to the floor and the
    ## HEIGHT is what gives way -- see the heights in `assemble-mains`. Shrinking
    ## the type further is not available: it is already at the limit.
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6), strip.text = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(2, "mm"))
}, "3E all sets")
p3c
```

```{r fig3EF}
p3f <- panel({
  need("OP", "chap_new")
  d <- OP$d |> mutate(share = 100 * share_of(chap_new))
  ggplot(d, aes(resp, share, colour = resp)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = .55, linewidth = .4) +

    ## The medians, stated. This is the per-sample form of the paper's response

    ## the text quotes.
    ## A LABEL, NOT BARE TEXT. The median annotation printed straight over the

    ## without moving it off the value it names.
    stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "label", size = 2.2, fontface = "bold",
                 vjust = -0.7, label.size = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.8,
                 label.padding = grid::unit(0.5, "mm"),

                 show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_RESP, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.05, .14))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Chaperone share of microbial protein (%)",
         title = "Non-responders carry a larger chaperone share",
         subtitle = sprintf("medians %.1f%% against %.1f%%, a %.2f-fold difference",
                            median(d$share[d$resp == "NR"]), median(d$share[d$resp == "R"]),
                            median(d$share[d$resp == "NR"]) / median(d$share[d$resp == "R"])))
}, "ED7B per-sample share")
p3e; p3f
```

```{r fig3G}
## the specificity control, in the main figure by design
p3surv <- panel({
  ## Time to progression against the chaperone share.
  ##
  ## TERTILES ARE FOR DISPLAY ONLY. The test is on the continuous predictor — a
  ## Cox model stratified by plex, with the permutation p B18b computes — and
  ## re-dichotomising to draw a curve is exactly what this analysis was written
  ## to avoid. Three groups rather than two, so the panel shows a gradient
  ## instead of a split, and the caption says the test is not the curve.
  if (!requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) stop("survival not installed")
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B18_survival", "survival.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("B18 output not found; run B18_survival.R")
  b <- readRDS(f)
  need("OP", "chap_new")
  d <- merge(OP$d, b$data, by = "sample")
  d$share <- share_of(chap_new)[d$sample]
  q <- quantile(d$share, c(1/3, 2/3), na.rm = TRUE)
  d$grp <- cut(d$share, c(-Inf, q, Inf), labels = c("Lowest third", "Middle", "Highest third"))
  d <- d[!is.na(d$grp), , drop = FALSE]
  d$grp <- droplevels(d$grp)
  if (nlevels(d$grp) < 2) stop("fewer than two non-empty tertiles")
  fit <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ grp, data = d)
  ## rep(levels, fit$strata) relies on survfit returning strata in factor-level
  ## order, which it does — but it mislabels every row in silence if a level is
  ## empty, so the levels are dropped above and the lengths checked here.
  if (length(fit$strata) != nlevels(d$grp))
    stop("survfit returned ", length(fit$strata), " strata for ", nlevels(d$grp), " groups")
  st <- data.frame(time = fit$time, surv = fit$surv,
                   grp = rep(levels(d$grp), fit$strata))
  ## start every curve at 1
  st <- rbind(data.frame(time = 0, surv = 1, grp = levels(d$grp)), st)
  ## ORDERED LEGEND. st$grp is a character vector, so the key came out
  ## alphabetical -- Highest, Lowest, Middle -- for a variable that is ordinal.
  st$grp <- factor(st$grp, levels = levels(d$grp))
  ## NUMBERS AT RISK, drawn INSIDE the panel in a band below 0%. Text placed
  ## below the panel is positioned in DATA units, so its offset in millimetres
  ## scales with the plot area: tuned against a standalone render of this
  ## panel, the rows landed 8 to 16 mm outside its cell in the assembled figure
  ## and printed over panel e. Nothing drawn below the axis is reserved by the
  ## layout, and axis text is reserved but cannot carry a colour, so the scale
  ## is expanded to -0.45 and the rows live inside it. They cannot be clipped
  ## by the cell, and they keep the curves colours.
  by  <- if (max(d$time) > 1800) 600 else if (max(d$time) > 450) 300 else 100
  xb  <- seq(0, max(d$time), by = by)
  sr  <- summary(fit, times = xb, extend = TRUE)
  rk  <- data.frame(time = sr$time, n = sr$n.risk,
                    grp  = sub("^grp=", "", as.character(sr$strata)))
  if (!all(rk$grp %in% levels(d$grp)))
    stop("survfit strata names do not match the tertile labels")
  rk$grp <- factor(rk$grp, levels = levels(d$grp))
  rk$y   <- -0.14 - 0.12 * (as.integer(rk$grp) - 1L)
  ggplot(st, aes(time, surv, colour = grp)) +
    geom_step(linewidth = .55) +
    ## THE KEYS MUST MATCH cut()'s labels EXACTLY. They were lower-case here
    ## against "Lowest third"/"Middle"/"Highest third" above, so every curve fell
    ## through to na.value and the panel shipped as three identical grey steps
    ## with no legend -- the direction of the survival claim invisible.
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Lowest third" = "#0072B2", "Middle" = "grey55",
                                   "Highest third" = "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +
    annotate("segment", x = -Inf, xend = -Inf, y = 0, yend = 1,
             colour = "black", linewidth = .4) +
    annotate("segment", x = -Inf, xend = Inf, y = -0.045, yend = -0.045,
             colour = "grey88", linewidth = .3) +
    geom_text(data = rk, aes(time, y, label = n, colour = grp), size = 1.9,
              inherit.aes = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = xb) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.45, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       labels = scales::percent,
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
    labs(x = "Days from sampling to progression or death", y = "Event-free",
         title = "A higher chaperone share tracks earlier progression or death",
         subtitle = stat_sub({
           ck <- readRDS(file.path(paths$out_dir, "B18_survival", "checks.rds"))
           sprintf("HR %.2f (%.2f\u2013%.2f), P = %.3f",
                   ck$hr_per_arm_diff, ck$hr_arm_lo, ck$hr_arm_hi, ck$perm_P)
         }, "3D survival scale")) +
    theme(legend.position = c(.78, .82), legend.background = element_blank(),
          ## the y axis line is drawn only where the scale is labelled, by the
          ## segment above; the band below 0% holds the at-risk rows.
          axis.line.y = element_blank())
## 19 Oct: TAG WAS "4F survival". p3surv has rendered as Figure 3d since the
## survival panel moved out of the supplement; the tag still named a Figure 4
## slot that does not exist. The stat_sub() label inside already said 3D,
## which is why this went unnoticed -- the two strings are different things.
}, "3D survival")

p3g <- panel({
  need("OP", "chap_new", "ribo_new")
  ch <- share_of(chap_new); rb <- share_of(ribo_new)
  rows <- bind_rows(
    ## seed 31 via .chap_pitt() -- the same object Figure 4b prints. See the
    ## note at perm_coef for why this is shared rather than recomputed.
    tibble(what = "chaperone share",  !!!.chap_pitt()),
    tibble(what = "ribosomal share",  !!!perm_coef(qlogis(rb), seed = 32)),
    tibble(what = "chaperone : ribosomal", !!!perm_coef(log(ch / rb), seed = 33)))
  ## THE RANGE IS THE NULL, NOT A CONFIDENCE INTERVAL. perm_coef() returns
  ## lo/hi as quantile(nl, .025/.975) of the within-plex PERMUTATION
  ## distribution, which is centred on zero by construction. Drawn as a
  ## geom_pointrange it read as a CI on the coefficient, so the panel appeared
  ## to contradict the p-value printed beside it: bars spanning zero next to
  ## p = 0.024. Drawn as a band BEHIND the point it reads as what it is -- the
  ## spread that shuffling response labels within plex produces by chance --
  ## and the observed point sitting outside that band IS the small p-value.
  ## geom_segment, not geom_linerange(xmin=, xmax=): the horizontal-orientation
  ## inference differs across ggplot2 versions and this file is knit elsewhere.
  rows |> mutate(what = factor(what, levels = rev(what))) |>
    ggplot(aes(coef, what)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = lo, xend = hi, yend = what), linewidth = 2.4,
                 colour = "grey84", lineend = "butt") +
    geom_point(size = 1.9) +
    ## P TO THE RIGHT MARGIN. At hjust = -0.15 each label sat on its own
    ## interval line and the whisker struck through the text.
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("p = %.3f", p)), x = Inf,
              hjust = 1.05, vjust = 0.5, size = 2.2) +
    labs(x = "Response coefficient (within plex)", y = NULL,
         title = "Not selective chaperone induction",
         subtitle = paste("point: observed coefficient; band: central 95% of the",
                          "within-plex\npermutation null, not a confidence interval.",
                          "Both shares move;\ntheir ratio does not"))
}, "ED7A shares and ratio")
p3g
```

```{r fig3-assemble}
p3mx <- panel({
  ## The correction shown rather than asserted: the distribution of the maximum
  ## statistic across the 565-set family, with the reported sets marked on it.
  ## This is the honest centrepiece of an exploratory claim.
  ## Self-sufficient: the draws and the observed values are both in the run
  ## directory, so the correction is computed here rather than read from a
  ## scored CSV that may sit somewhere else.
  ## (no filename pattern here: the directory is found by structure below, and a
  ## name-based filter is what selected the superseded 1,000-draw run twice)
  ## Same lesson as 5A: find the directory by STRUCTURE, not by file name, and
  ## take the largest. The 10,000-draw archive unzipped into
  ## nulls_pitt_full/nulls_pitt_full/ while the old 1,000-draw run sits in the
  ## outer folder, and a name-based pattern kept selecting the superseded one.
  all_d <- list.dirs(paths$out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  cnt <- vapply(all_d, function(x) {
    f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$")
    sum(!grepl("^observed", f, ignore.case = TRUE))
  }, 0L)
  ok <- cnt >= 100 & vapply(all_d, function(x)
          any(grepl("^observed", list.files(x, "\\.rds$"), ignore.case = TRUE)), TRUE)
  ## and only a directory stamped with the current design (13 Oct 2026): the
  ## superseded 10,000-draw run would otherwise win on size
  ok <- ok & vapply(all_d, draws_match, TRUE)
  if (!any(ok)) stop("no directory under ", basename(paths$out_dir),
                     " holds >=100 draw .rds files plus an observed table made on the ",
                     "current design (stamped design.txt; run_null_2026-10-13.R)", call. = FALSE)
  cat("  4D draw directories: ",
      paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", basename(all_d[ok]), cnt[ok]), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  d <- all_d[ok][which.max(cnt[ok])]
  fs <- list.files(d, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  fs <- fs[!grepl("^observed", basename(fs), ignore.case = TRUE)]
  of <- list.files(d, "^observed", full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(of)) stop("draws found in ", d, " but no observed_*.rds beside them")
  sc <- as.data.frame(readRDS(of[1]))
  ## BUILD THE DRAW MATRIX INCREMENTALLY. rbind-ing every draw into one frame
  ## first costs 565 x 10,000 rows before the matrix is even formed; at 1,000
  ## draws that was tolerable and at 10,000 it is not. Each draw contributes one
  ## row, keyed by set name, so the matrix is filled directly.
  cat(sprintf("  4D: %d draws in %s\n", length(fs), basename(d)))
  ## The manuscript reports the 10,000-draw correction. A render off 1,000 draws
  ## quotes FWER 0.57 where the paper says 0.86, so refuse rather than mislabel.
  ## WHAT THE READER SEES AND WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES ARE NOT THE SAME TEXT.
  ## This refusal used to raise the whole engineering note, and `panel()` draws a
  ## stop message into a grey box inside the figure -- so a submitted PDF carried
  ## "CONFIRMED 28 Sep 2026 ... Transfer the 10,000-draw archive from the compute
  ## server" as rendered artwork. Reviewer 5 found it twice, once per position.
  ## The diagnosis goes to the knit log, where it is useful; the panel says only
  ## what a reader needs, which is that the panel is pending.
  if (length(fs) < 5000) {
    cat("  4D REFUSED: found ", length(fs), " draws in ", basename(d),
        ". The manuscript reports the\n       10,000-draw correction (FWER 0.86); a render off 1,000 draws ",
        "would quote 0.57.\n       This panel recomputes from draws by design so figure and text cannot\n",
        "       diverge. Restore the 10,000-draw archive to render it.\n", sep = "")
    stop("panel pending regeneration of the 10,000-draw run", call. = FALSE)
  }
  sets <- sc$pathway
  M <- matrix(NA_real_, length(fs), length(sets), dimnames = list(NULL, sets))
  for (i in seq_along(fs)) {
    x <- as.data.frame(readRDS(fs[i]))
    M[i, ] <- abs(x$NES)[match(sets, x$pathway)]
  }
  M <- M[, colSums(!is.na(M)) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  ## MINIMUM-p WESTFALL-YOUNG, not max|NES|. The per-set null spread of |NES|
  ## runs 0.13 to 0.48, so NES is not comparable across sets and a maximum is
  ## dominated by whichever sets have wide nulls — scoring this panel that way
  ## gave 0.059 where the correct procedure gives 0.86 at 10,000 draws.
  P <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(M), ncol(M), dimnames = dimnames(M))
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(M))) {
    a <- M[, j]; okj <- !is.na(a)
    P[okj, j] <- rank(-a[okj], ties.method = "min") / sum(okj)
  }
  mnp <- apply(P, 1, function(r) { r <- r[!is.na(r)]; if (!length(r)) NA_real_ else min(r) })
  mnp <- mnp[!is.na(mnp)]
  sc$p_set <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(sc)), function(i) {
    x <- M[, sc$pathway[i]]; x <- x[!is.na(x)]
    (1 + sum(x >= abs(sc$NES[i]))) / (1 + length(x)) }, 0)
  sc$p_wy <- vapply(sc$p_set, function(q) (1 + sum(mnp <= q)) / (1 + length(mnp)), 0)
  key <- c("reported:O_chap", "reported:chaperones", "reported:O")
  lab <- sc |> filter(pathway %in% key) |>
    mutate(nm = recode(pathway, "reported:O_chap" = "chaperone members of O",
                       "reported:chaperones" = "all chaperones", "reported:O" = "category O"),
           x = abs(NES))
  ## What the correction actually compares: the smallest per-set p reached
  ## ANYWHERE among 565 sets in each permutation, against the observed p.
  lab$x <- lab$p_set
  ggplot(data.frame(mnp = as.numeric(mnp)), aes(mnp)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 45, fill = "grey80", colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    geom_vline(data = lab, aes(xintercept = x, colour = nm), linewidth = .5) +
    ## AN INSET TABLE, NOT REPELLED LABELS. The three reference lines sit within
    ## a few thousandths of each other, so ggrepel with direction = "x" has
    ## nowhere to move and overprints all three into an unreadable block. A small
    ## table in the corner is what comparable panels in the literature use.
    annotate("label", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.02, vjust = 1.05, size = 2.2,
             label.size = 0, fill = "white", alpha = .85, lineheight = 1.15,
             label = paste(c(sprintf("%-22s FWER", ""),
                             sprintf("%-22s %.2f", lab$nm, lab$p_wy)), collapse = "\n")) +
    scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("chaperone members of O" = PAL_RESP[["NR"]],
                                   "all chaperones" = "#0072B2", "category O" = "grey35"),
                        guide = "none") +
    labs(x = sprintf("smallest per-set p reached anywhere among %d sets, in each of %d permutations",
                     ncol(M), nrow(M)),
         y = "Permutations", title = "Why the survey correction is unforgiving",
         subtitle = sprintf("median %.4f; the chaperone sets' own corrected value is %.2f",
                            median(mnp), lab$p_wy[lab$pathway == "reported:O_chap"]))
}, "ED6D multiplicity")

## p3e ("Chaperone evidence by phylum") is DROPPED: it is Figure 3C in raw counts
## rather than shares — same data, same message, in a different figure. p3mx, the
## multiplicity panel, STAYS: with the response finding exploratory, the
## correction is not a control but the result's own boundary.
## Panel order follows the order the text cites them, checked against the
## manuscript rather than assumed: a,b (running score, decomposition) are cited
## together, then the chaperone null, then the multiplicity correction, then the
## ranked sets four paragraphs later, then survival. The null and the correction
## are therefore a row, and the ranked sets sit beside survival. The earlier
## layout put the ranked sets third and the null fourth, which made the text
## cite 4a,b then 4d, 4e, 4c -- out of order at a journal that checks it.
## REVIEWER 5 §4, three moves in one figure.
##   OUT: p3mx, the 565-set correction. It is an honest-reporting panel showing
##        the finding does not survive correction, the FWER values are in the
##        text, and it is the panel that currently refuses to render off 1,000
##        draws. It goes to ED4, which is the figure about how the null and the
##        statistic were chosen, and it takes the slot the deleted pS7b frees.
##   IN:  p3f from ED8. The central biological claim had NO main-figure display
##        of the per-sample data -- a reader could not see 10.9% against 9.7%
##        anywhere in the main figures, only running curves, nulls and rankings.
##        It sits at d, directly after the null, where the claim is made.
##   IN:  p4a from ED7. Robustness to composition and host protein is
##        load-bearing for the chaperone claim and was absent from the mains.
## FOUR ROWS, and p3c full width on the last. Seven panels do not fit two-up in
## three rows, and p3c carries thirty long category labels -- it is the panel
## that most needs the width and least wants a half-column.
## ASSEMBLED LATER -- see the note in the Figure 2 chunk. p4a is defined only
## fourteen lines below this point, which is exactly the kind of near-miss
## forward reference that reads as working code.
```

```{r fig4DE}
p4d <- panel({
  need("OP", "pep_g", "chap_new")
  gen <- count(pep_g, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  community <- perm_coef(qlogis(share_of(chap_new)), B = 500, seed = 41)$coef
  out <- bind_rows(lapply(gen, function(g) {
    r  <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g]
    num <- colSums(OP$a[intersect(r, which(OP$rd$Protein %in% chap_new)),
                        OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    den <- colSums(OP$a[r, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    y <- suppressWarnings(qlogis(num / den))
    d <- OP$d |> mutate(yy = y) |> filter(is.finite(yy)) |> droplevels()
    if (nlevels(d$resp) < 2 || nrow(d) < 20) return(NULL)
    cf <- coef(summary(lm(yy ~ Mixture + resp, d)))
    tibble(genus = g, est = cf["respR", 1], se = cf["respR", 2])
  }))
  ggplot(out, aes(est, reorder(genus, est))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, community), linetype = c(2, 1), linewidth = .3,
               colour = c("grey40", "#0072B2")) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = est - 1.96 * se, xmax = est + 1.96 * se), size = .22) +

         title = "Within genera against the community effect",
         subtitle = "blue: community level") +

}, "ED8F within-genus")
```
