# Figure 4 — The second cohort (and Supplementary 3)

```{r fig5}
p5b <- panel({
  ## Search the plausible directories rather than assuming one. The pooled
  ## (pre-specified primary) run is preferred; the MS2 design is the fallback and
  ## is labelled as such, because they are different analyses.
  ## THIS PANEL RENDERED THE WRONG ARM. find_draws returns the first directory
  ## that matches, which was the SUPERSEDED sampling-episode design (n = 29,
  ## one patient counted twice under opposite labels): NES -1.76, p = 0.040.
  ## The manuscript reports the pre-specified primary, the pooled patient-level
  ## run: NES -1.48, p = 0.155. A figure showing a significant-looking result
  ## where the paper reports a null is worse than no figure.
  ##
  ## The directory search now prefers the pooled run explicitly, and the loaded
  ## observed value is CHECKED against the primary before anything is drawn.
  ## IDENTIFY THE ARM BY ITS OBSERVED VALUE, NOT BY DIRECTORY NAME.
  ## There are several Sheba runs on disk — pooled, MS2-only, two no-83
  ## sensitivities and the superseded sampling-episode design — and choosing by
  ## name is what put the wrong one (NES -1.76) in this panel. Every candidate is
  ## read, its observed NES reported, and the one matching the pre-specified
  ## primary is used. If none matches, the panel says what it found rather than
  ## drawing whichever came first.
  ## SET NAMES MAY CARRY A SOURCE PREFIX. The full-space run names its sets
  ## "reported:O", "COG:O" and so on, so a test for pathway == "O" matches
  ## nothing there — which is exactly what the directory diagnostic reported for
  ## the 10,000-draw archive. Strip any "prefix:" before comparing.
  bare <- function(x) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(x))
  pick_O <- function(df) {
    if (!all(c("pathway", "NES") %in% names(df))) return(NA_real_)
    v <- df$NES[bare(df$pathway) == "O"]
    if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_real_
  }

  ## MATCH ON STRUCTURE, NOT ON FILE NAMES. Two rounds were lost to guessing at
  ## the draw-file naming: `sheba_pooled` holds the pre-specified primary but its
  ## files do not match "^(null|draw)..._N.rds", so it was invisible. A draw
  ## directory is simply one holding many .rds files plus one observed table, and
  ## that is what is tested here.
  PRIMARY_NES <- -1.48
  is_draw <- function(x) {
    f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$")
    ob <- grepl("^observed", f, ignore.case = TRUE)
    sum(!ob) >= 100 && any(ob)
  }
  draw_files <- function(x) {
    f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
    f[!grepl("^observed", basename(f), ignore.case = TRUE)]
  }
  obs_file <- function(x) {
    f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
    f[grepl("^observed", basename(f), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
  }
  roots <- list.dirs(paths$out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  roots <- roots[grepl("sheba", roots, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  ## A directory with draws but no observed table cannot be used, and saying so
  ## is more useful than omitting it: that is the state sheba_pooled is in.
  orphan <- Filter(function(x) {
    f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$")
    sum(!grepl("^observed", f, ignore.case = TRUE)) >= 100 &&
      !any(grepl("^observed", f, ignore.case = TRUE))
  }, roots)
  if (length(orphan))
    cat("  draws present but NO observed table in: ",
        paste(basename(orphan), collapse = ", "),
        "\n    (those runs cannot be used until their observed table is archived)\n", sep = "")
  cand <- Filter(is_draw, roots)
  if (!length(cand))
    stop("no Sheba draw directory with both draws and an observed_*.rds under ",
         paths$out_dir, call. = FALSE)
  info <- lapply(cand, function(dd) {
    ob <- try(as.data.frame(readRDS(obs_file(dd))), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(ob, "try-error") || !"NES" %in% names(ob)) return(NULL)
    v <- pick_O(ob)
    if (!is.finite(v)) return(NULL)
    list(dir = dd, n = length(draw_files(dd)), nes = v)
  })
  info <- Filter(Negate(is.null), info)
  cat("  5A candidates:\n")
  for (z in info) cat(sprintf("    %-28s %5d draws, observed NES %+.2f\n",
                              basename(z$dir), z$n, z$nes))
  hit <- Filter(function(z) abs(z$nes - PRIMARY_NES) <= 0.05, info)
  if (!length(hit))
    stop("no Sheba run on disk has the pre-specified primary's observed NES (",
         PRIMARY_NES, ").\n  Found: ",
         paste(sprintf("%s = %+.2f", vapply(info, function(z) basename(z$dir), ""),
                       vapply(info, function(z) z$nes, 0)), collapse = ", "),
         "\n  The primary's draws may not have been archived.", call. = FALSE)
  d  <- hit[[which.max(vapply(hit, function(z) z$n, 0L))]]$dir
  fs <- draw_files(d)
  nl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fs, function(f) as.data.frame(readRDS(f))))
  ob <- as.data.frame(readRDS(obs_file(d)))
  x  <- nl$NES[bare(nl$pathway) == "O"]; o <- pick_O(ob)
  cat(sprintf("  5A: using %s (%d draws), observed NES %+.2f\n", basename(d), length(fs), o))
  ggplot(data.frame(NES = x), aes(NES)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 44, fill = "grey82", colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    ## Shaded: draws at or below the observed value, as in Figure 4C -- one-sided.
    ## The p printed in the subtitle is two-sided (|NES| >= |observed|), so the
    ## shaded area is not it. The two null panels read the same way; here the
    ## shaded area is large, which is the point — this arm did not detect the
    ## difference.
    geom_histogram(data = data.frame(NES = x[x <= o]), bins = 44,
                   fill = PAL_COHORT[["Sheba"]], alpha = .5, colour = "white",
                   linewidth = .2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = o, colour = PAL_COHORT[["Sheba"]], linewidth = .6) +
    labs(x = "NES under permutation", y = "Draws",
         title = "Sheba, pre-specified primary: not detected before treatment",
         subtitle = sprintf("observed %.2f, p = %.3f", o,
                            (1 + sum(abs(x) >= abs(o), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + sum(is.finite(x)))))
}, "4A Sheba null")

p5d <- panel({
  ## Computed here from annot_new, not transcribed: the observed and
  ## analysis-universe levels are derived, and only the database level — which
  ## needs the raw emapper files (§12a) — is carried as a constant.
  need("annot_new"); need("CHAPERONE_KO")
  GD <- c("K04077", "K04043")
  share <- function(coh, universe = NULL) {
    k <- annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == coh &
           annot_new$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO &
           (if (is.null(universe)) TRUE else annot_new$protein %in% universe)]
    if (!length(k)) return(NA_real_)
    100 * mean(k %in% GD)
  }
  ## The analysis-universe level is COG O's chaperone MEMBERS, not the whole
  ## reported universe — recomputing it the second way drew 42.5 against the
  ## record's 51.5. Taken from the analysis document, which computes it once.
  if (!exists("gd_analysis_universe"))
    stop("gd_analysis_universe not exported — re-knit; do not recompute this here")
  AU <- c(Pittsburgh = unname(gd_analysis_universe[["pitt"]]), Sheba = 84.3)
  DB <- c(Pittsburgh = 15.3, Sheba = 18.0)        # §12a, deduplicated union
  dd <- tibble(
    level = factor(rep(c("search database", "observed PSMs", "analysis universe"), each = 2),
                   levels = c("search database", "observed PSMs", "analysis universe")),
    cohort = rep(c("Pittsburgh", "Sheba"), 3),
    pct = c(DB[["Pittsburgh"]], DB[["Sheba"]],
            share("pitt"), share("sheba"),
            AU[["Pittsburgh"]], AU[["Sheba"]]))
  if (anyNA(dd$pct))
    stop("the three-level comparison is not computable: ",
         paste(dd$level[is.na(dd$pct)], dd$cohort[is.na(dd$pct)], collapse = "; "))
  ggplot(dd, aes(level, pct, fill = cohort)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .8), width = .7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", pct)), position = position_dodge(width = .8),
              vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_COHORT, name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .12))) +
    ## 31 Oct: EACH BAR NOW SAYS WHAT IT COUNTS. A reader testing exactly the
    ## hypothesis this panel exists to answer -- that GroEL and DnaK lead because
    ## they dominate each cohort's database -- read the middle bar as the database
    ## and took 36.5/73.2 for the database shares. They are the OBSERVED shares;
    ## the database shares are 15.3 and 18.0 and are nearly equal between cohorts,
    ## which is the refutation. Three words of axis label are cheaper than the
    ## misreading.
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c("search database" = "in the\nsearch database",
                                "observed PSMs" = "among the\nobserved PSMs",
                                "analysis universe" = "in the\nanalysis universe")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "GroEL/DnaK share of\nchaperone protein (%)",
         title = "The lead is not inherited from the search databases",
         ## The numbers come from DB, not from a typed string, so the sentence
         ## cannot drift from the bars it is describing.
         ## Short on purpose: wrap_titles() folds subtitles at 42 characters, so
         ## the long version ran to five lines in a quarter-width panel. The
         ## title carries the claim, the axis says what each bar counts, and
         ## this puts the two database numbers where a skimmer sees them.
         subtitle = sprintf("%.1f%% and %.1f%% of chaperone protein in the Pittsburgh and Sheba databases",
                            DB[["Pittsburgh"]], DB[["Sheba"]]))
}, "4D three levels")
p5b; p5d
```

```{r fig5-assemble}
## B13's clade arms and B16's signature tables have no panel yet. They are
## reported in the text only, so nothing here reads them; if either becomes a
## figure it should load from its own saved .rds the way S3 and 5E do, rather
## than depend on a knit having populated the session.
p5e <- panel({
  ## THE COMPARISON AS ESTIMATION, both cohorts on one axis (B14). This panel was
  ## titled "coupling not reproduced", which read the own-versus-stranger result
  ## as a test of "above zero". Pillar 1's claim is about magnitude — how much a
  ## patient's own gene abundance adds — so the panel shows how large that
  ## advantage can be in each cohort, at both resolutions, and asks neither to
  ## clear zero. Falls back to B12's single-cohort view, retitled, if B14 has not
  ## run.
  ## WHICHEVER SOURCE CARRIES THE NEWER SCHEMA WINS. The session object comes
  ## from figure_inputs.rds, which is only as fresh as the last v17 knit; the
  ## file on disk is whatever B14 wrote last. Taking the session object first --
  ## which this did -- means that re-running B14 to add the Hodges-Lehmann
  ## columns changes nothing in the figure, because exists() is TRUE and the
  ## fresh file is never opened. Prefer the source that has `hl`, and say which.
  .has_hl <- function(x) !is.null(x) &&
    all(c("hl", "hl_lo", "hl_hi") %in% names(as.data.frame(x$table %||% x)))
  m <- local({
    sess <- if (exists("b14_magnitude")) b14_magnitude else NULL
    f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B14_coupling_magnitude", "magnitude.rds")
    disk <- if (file.exists(f)) readRDS(f) else NULL
    if (.has_hl(sess))      { cat("S3A: B14 from the session (has hl)\n");  sess }
    else if (.has_hl(disk)) { cat("S3A: B14 from ", f, " (has hl; the session copy does not)\n", sep = ""); disk }
    else if (!is.null(sess)) sess
    else disk
  })
  if (!is.null(m)) {
    d <- as.data.frame(m$table)
    ## THE PATHWAY ARM (B36), bound in only if it has run. It is the third
    ## resolution and it carries the point the other two cannot make: summing
    ## orthologs into KEGG maps raises the GENERIC agreement from 0.24 to 0.68
    ## while leaving the patient-specific advantage at zero. So the honest
    ## reading of pillar 1 is not "the assays are too noisy to couple" -- at
    ## pathway level they couple at 0.68 -- but that the individual information
    ## is not there. It also answers the one objection the 200-most-variable arm
    ## cannot: that arm selects on variability, and this one does not.
    f36 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B36_pathway_coupling", "magnitude.rds")
    if (file.exists(f36)) {
      pw <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f36))
      d <- dplyr::bind_rows(d, pw[, intersect(names(pw), names(d)), drop = FALSE])
    }
    ## Order the arms explicitly. The previous version took the table's own row
    ## order, which was fine for two arms from one source and would have put a
    ## bound-in third arm wherever bind_rows happened to leave it.
    arm_order <- c("full profile", "200 most variable", "pathways")
    d$arm <- factor(d$arm, levels = intersect(arm_order, unique(d$arm)))
    d <- d[order(d$cohort, d$arm), ]
    ## THE ROW-LABEL DESIGN IS GONE, and so is the column that fed it. Until
    ## 14 Oct this panel was a forest with the coupling printed in each row
    ## label; coupling is now the x aesthetic, which is the redesign the next
    ## note documents. `lab` went on being computed here long after nothing read
    ## it, and the comment above it described a panel that no longer exists --
    ## which is how the same wrong description reached the figure legend, where
    ## it survived four rounds of review. Removed 15 Oct.
    ## THE LESSON IT CARRIED IS GENERAL AND STILL APPLIES: write "rho", NOT
    ## U+03C1. Helvetica as the base pdf() device references it has no Greek rho,
    ## so every label shipped as "(. 0.24)" -- the glyph silently became a full
    ## stop. Same as U+2229 in p5rank: the word costs nothing and survives every
    ## device.
    ## WHICH ESTIMATOR IS IN THIS TABLE? B14/B36 wrote `median`/`lo`/`hi`; once
    ## they are switched to Hodges-Lehmann they write `hl`/`hl_lo`/`hl_hi`. The
    ## panel reads whichever is present and SAYS WHICH on the axis, because the
    ## two differ by a factor of two in one cohort and a figure that silently
    ## used the older column while the text quoted the newer one is precisely
    ## the failure this document keeps having to catch after the fact.
    est_is_hl <- all(c("hl", "hl_lo", "hl_hi") %in% names(d))
    if (est_is_hl) { d$est <- d$hl; d$elo <- d$hl_lo; d$ehi <- d$hl_hi
      ## A FRESH B14 BOUND TO A STALE B36 is the one combination that fails
      ## quietly: intersect() above drops `hl` from the pathway rows, bind_rows
      ## fills NA, est is NA for that arm and ggplot removes the row with a
      ## warning nobody reads -- the arm simply disappears from the figure.
      if (any(is.na(d$est))) {
        gone <- paste(sprintf("%s/%s", d$cohort[is.na(d$est)],
                              as.character(d$arm)[is.na(d$est)]), collapse = ", ")
        stop("S3A: ", sum(is.na(d$est)), " arm(s) have no Hodges-Lehmann estimate (",
             gone, "). B14 supplies hl columns and B36 does not, so those arms ",
             "would vanish from the panel. Re-run b36() and b36_save().",
             call. = FALSE)
      }
    }
    else           { d$est <- d$median; d$elo <- d$lo; d$ehi <- d$hi
                     message("S3A: B14/B36 still carry median columns; the main ",
                             "text reports Hodges-Lehmann. Re-run B14 and B36 ",
                             "before submission so panel and text agree.") }
    ## COUPLING ON THE AXIS, NOT IN THE ROW LABEL. Redesigned 14 Oct. The forest
    ## version put the one quantity this panel exists to show -- the generic
    ## coupling, which runs from about -0.05 to 0.68 across these arms -- into
    ## the row labels as text, and gave the x-axis to six advantages all sitting
    ## near zero. Read at the speed a figure is actually read, that is a panel
    ## reporting nothing, which is how it came back from review.
    ## With coupling on x the dynamic range IS the geometry: the agreement
    ## between the layers moves across effectively its whole attainable range
    ## while the patient-specific advantage stays flat on zero the entire way.
    ## That is the answer to the noise objection -- the assays are not too noisy
    ## to couple, since at pathway level they couple at 0.68; the individual
    ## information is simply not there -- and it is why this panel was promoted
    ## out of Extended Data rather than a new positive control being built.
    ##
    ## NO x LIMIT AT ZERO. One arm (the second cohort's 200 most variable) has a
    ## NEGATIVE coupling, so limits = c(0, NA) would silently drop the point that
    ## anchors the low end of the range. For the same reason the title claims no
    ## fold-change: a ratio across a sign change is meaningless.
    ggplot(d, aes(own_coupling, est, colour = cohort)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
      geom_linerange(aes(ymin = elo, ymax = ehi), linewidth = .6) +
      geom_point(aes(shape = arm), size = PT_SMALL * 1.4) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_COHORT, name = NULL) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17, 15), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
      scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.08, .12))) +
      labs(x = "Generic coupling between the layers (Spearman rho)",
           ## 18 Oct: TWO LINES, THE METHOD IN SMALLER TYPE. plotmath rather
           ## than ggtext, which is not among the packages this file loads.
           ## atop() stacks the two lines; scriptstyle() sets the second at
           ## about 0.7x. "Own" - "stranger" renders a true minus, not a hyphen.
           y = bquote(atop("Own" - "stranger",
                           scriptstyle(.(sprintf("(%s, 95%% interval)",
                                                 if (est_is_hl) "Hodges\u2013Lehmann" else "median"))))),
           title = "Coupling moves across its whole range; the advantage does not",
           subtitle = paste("one point per resolution per cohort;",
                            "no arm is asked to clear zero")) +
      ## legend.box VERTICAL, not horizontal: p5e sits in an 88 mm column now,
      ## and the shape and colour keys side by side ran off the right edge with
      ## "Sheba" clipped. Stacked, each key gets the full column width.
      theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
            legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
  } else {
    f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("neither B14 nor B12 output found under ", paths$out_dir)
    b <- readRDS(f)
    d <- tibble(delta = b$own_top - b$mis_top)
    ci <- b$boot_ci
    ggplot(d, aes(delta)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
      geom_dotplot(binwidth = diff(range(d$delta, na.rm = TRUE))/28, fill = "grey60",
                   colour = "white", stroke = .2, dotsize = .9) +
      annotate("segment", x = ci[1], xend = ci[2], y = -0.05, yend = -0.05,
               linewidth = .6, colour = "grey30") +
      annotate("point", x = median(d$delta, na.rm = TRUE), y = -0.05, size = 1.4) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = b$pitt_delta, colour = PAL_COHORT[["Pittsburgh"]], linewidth = .5) +
      scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL) +
      labs(x = "Own minus stranger, per patient",
           title = "Second cohort: the advantage, estimated",
           subtitle = sprintf("median %+.4f, 95%% CI %+.4f to %+.4f; line: first cohort's %+.3f",
                              median(d$delta, na.rm = TRUE), ci[1], ci[2], b$pitt_delta))
  }
}, "1C coupling magnitude")

p5f <- panel({
  ## Without this, B12's negative reads as evidence against Pillar 1. With it,
  ## the honest reading is visible: the design resolves a first-cohort-sized
  ## effect about a third of the time and needs more than twice that effect for
  ## 80% power, so it neither replicates nor excludes.
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("B12 output not found at ", f)
  b <- readRDS(f)
  if (is.null(b$power_grid)) stop("this B12 run predates the power curve; re-run it")
  g <- as_tibble(b$power_grid)
  ggplot(g, aes(shift, power)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = b$pitt_delta, colour = PAL_COHORT[["Pittsburgh"]], linewidth = .5) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .5) + geom_point(size = PT_SMALL) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .05))) +
    annotate("text", x = b$pitt_delta, y = 0.05, label = "Pittsburgh", hjust = -0.1,
             size = 2.3, colour = PAL_COHORT[["Pittsburgh"]]) +
    ## MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECT, NOT POWER AT AN OBSERVED ESTIMATE. The
    ## calculation is a design one -- a detection curve swept over a range of
    ## effects at the SECOND cohort's design -- but led by "power at the first
    ## cohort's effect" it reads as retrospective power, which it is not.
    labs(x = "True own-over-others advantage", y = "Probability of detecting it",
         title = "What Sheba could resolve",
         subtitle = sprintf("80%% power at this design needs %s; Pittsburgh's estimate is marked for scale",
                            if (is.na(b$mde)) paste0("more than ", max(g$shift))
                            else sprintf("%+.3f", b$mde)))
}, "ED3D detectable effect")

## Each cohort ranks its own sets with its own data, so this panel compares
## POSITIONS rather than values — the one cross-cohort comparison these cohorts
## support, since they share no proteins and only part of an annotation
## vocabulary. It is also the honest way to show the result: the same panel that
## carries the concordance carries the two sets that reverse.
p5rank <- panel({
  need("paths")
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B26_rank", "rank.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("B26 output not found; run B26_rank_concordance.R")
  b <- readRDS(f); m <- as.data.frame(b$both)
  if (!nrow(m)) stop("no set scored in both cohorts")
  ## Short labels: the first version stacked three two-line labels at ranks 2, 4
  ## and 5 of the pre-treatment ordering and they overlapped.
  ## "O \u2229 chaperones" PULLED IN A SECOND TYPEFACE. Helvetica has no U+2229,
  ## so fontconfig substituted Arial for that one character and Figure 5 shipped
  ## with an Arial glyph in the middle of a Helvetica label. Set notation buys
  ## nothing here that a word does not.
  NICE <- c(O = "COG O", O_chap = "Chaperones in O",
            chaperones = "All chaperones", O_chap_noGD = "Chaperones,\nno GroEL/DnaK",
            ribosomal = "Ribosomal")
  ## ONE VOCABULARY FOR COHORT CATEGORIES. This panel said discovery ->
  ## pre-treatment, which is a role and a timing on one axis, while its
  ## neighbours said Pittsburgh -> Sheba. Category labels and legends now use
  ## the PAL_COHORT names everywhere in this file; a descriptive TITLE may still
  ## say what the cohort is.
  d <- rbind(
    data.frame(key = m$key, cohort = "Pittsburgh", rank = m$rank_nr_1),
    data.frame(key = m$key, cohort = "Sheba",      rank = m$rank_nr_2))
  d$cohort <- factor(d$cohort, levels = c("Pittsburgh", "Sheba"))
  d$lab    <- ifelse(d$key %in% names(NICE), NICE[d$key], d$key)
  d$agrees <- d$key %in% m$key[sign(m$NES_1) == sign(m$NES_2)]
  ggplot(d, aes(cohort, rank, group = key)) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = agrees), linewidth = .55) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = agrees), size = PT_SMALL) +
    geom_text(data = subset(d, cohort == "Sheba"),
              aes(label = lab, colour = agrees), hjust = -0.12, size = 2.1,
              lineheight = .85, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, b$n1)) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.12, 1.6))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = unname(PAL_RESP[["NR"]]), `FALSE` = "grey65"),
                        labels = c(`TRUE` = "Same direction", `FALSE` = "Reverses"),
                        name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = sprintf("position among the %d sets scored in both", b$n1),
         title = "The same category ranks near the top in both cohorts",
         subtitle = "rank 1 = most non-responder-associated within that cohort") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
}, "ED9E rank concordance")

## ===========================================================================
## 5B — the chaperone share, in units, in both cohorts
## ===========================================================================
## WHY THIS PANEL CHANGED AGAIN, AND WHY THIS IS THE LAST SHAPE IT NEEDS.
## Every previous version of 5B plotted the normalized enrichment score. The
## supplementary methods disclaim that axis in writing: scores there are "an
## ordering device within that family" and "carry no effect-size
## interpretation; significance rests on the permutation p in every case". A
## main figure whose axis our own methods say means nothing quantitative is a
## defect regardless of what replaces it. So NES leaves the main figures, and
## this panel plots a quantity with units instead: the share of microbial
## protein going to chaperones, in each cohort, with an interval.
##
## WHY THE ODDS RATIO AND NOT THE FOLD OF MEDIANS. The obvious choice is the
## ratio of medians -- 10.9/9.7 = 1.12 on treatment, 4.17/3.60 = 1.16 before
## it -- and it is the wrong one. A fold of medians is a function of the
## baseline share, and the two responder baselines are 9.70% and 3.60%, a
## 2.7-fold difference in the denominator, because each cohort's protein
## universe is built from its own assembly and the two share no protein
## identifiers. Those two folds are therefore NOT one quantity measured twice,
## and their near-equality is substantially coincidence. What is baseline-free
## is the quantity the model estimates and the permutation tests: the odds
## ratio of the share. The folds stay in the panel as printed description,
## where they cannot be mistaken for a comparison.
##
## WHAT THE PANEL IS ALLOWED TO CLAIM. Not "the effect sizes agree" -- two
## point estimates landing close when one interval is wide is not agreement.
## The claim is the one B45 computes: the pre-treatment interval COVERS the
## on-treatment estimate, so that cohort cannot exclude an effect of this size.
## Underpowered, not absent. That is weaker than agreement and it is what the
## data carry.
##
## THE RIBOSOMAL AND RATIO ROWS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Both were built and
## measured. B45 section 0 reports that the ribosomal set occupies 10.44% of
## the on-treatment cohort's rows and 2.64% of the pre-treatment cohort's, a
## 4.0-fold difference in coverage against 1.47-fold for chaperones. A share
## whose set is four times more sparsely recovered on one side is not the same
## measurement on both, so neither the ribosomal row nor the chaperone-to-
## ribosomal ratio, which carries that set in its denominator, can be shown as
## one quantity in two cohorts. They are reported in the supplement with the
## coverage figures beside them.
p5setp <- panel({
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B45_share_panel", "share_panel_rows.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f))
    stop("5B: B45 output not found. Run source(\"B45_share_panel_data.R\") first; ",
         "expected ", f, call. = FALSE)
  s <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f))
  ## EVERY NAME ASSIGNED HERE IS WRITTEN TO THE GLOBAL ENVIRONMENT. panel()
  ## takes its block as a promise and forces it in the caller's frame, so a
  ## panel's "local" variables are not local -- they overwrite whatever else
  ## holds that name. The first version of this panel called its column list
  ## `need`, and that clobbered the top-level need() helper from fig-setup. The
  ## panel that broke was 5C, with "could not find function need". Internals
  ## here are dot-prefixed so they cannot collide with a helper or a constant.
  .want <- c("cohort", "quantity", "or_NR_over_R", "or_lo", "or_hi",
            "median_NR_pct", "median_R_pct", "fold_of_medians", "n", "n_NR")
  .missing_cols <- setdiff(.want, names(s))
  if (length(.missing_cols)) stop("5B: B45 output lacks ", paste(.missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
                         " -- re-run B45", call. = FALSE)
  d <- s[s$quantity == "chaperones", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) != 2L)
    stop("5B: expected two chaperone rows, found ", nrow(d), call. = FALSE)

  ## COHORT NAMES COME FROM THE PALETTE, NOT FROM B45's LABELS. B45 calls them
  ## "on treatment" and "before treatment"; PAL_COHORT is keyed by site. Map
  ## once, here, so the colours cannot drift from the rest of the figure.
  d$site <- ifelse(grepl("^before", d$cohort), "Sheba", "Pittsburgh")
  d$site <- factor(d$site, levels = c("Sheba", "Pittsburgh"))   # discovery on top
  ## The p to print: the discovery cohort's test is two-sided, the second
  ## cohort's was pre-specified one-sided. Printing one column for both would
  ## misdescribe one of them, so each row carries its own and says which.
  ## FROM d, NOT BY match() INTO s. s holds three quantities per cohort, so
  ## match(d$cohort, s$cohort) returns the first row with that cohort label --
  ## which is whichever quantity happens to come first. d is already the
  ## chaperone subset and carries both p columns.
  if (!all(c("p_one_sided", "p_two_sided") %in% names(d)))
    stop("5B: B45 output lacks the permutation p columns -- re-run B45", call. = FALSE)
  ## 19 Oct: THE ON-TREATMENT p IS seed 31's, not B45's own permutation of the
  ## same model -- see the note at perm_coef. The odds ratio and the interval
  ## still come from B45, because they are exp() of that model's coefficient and
  ## standard error and perm_coef returns a null band rather than a confidence
  ## interval. The pre-treatment row is unchanged: it is Sheba, which perm_coef
  ## cannot reach, and its one-sided p stays B45's.
  .p_pitt <- .chap_pitt()$p
  d$ptxt <- ifelse(d$site == "Pittsburgh",
                   sprintf("P = %.3f, two-sided", .p_pitt),
                   sprintf("P = %.3f, one-sided", d$p_one_sided))
  ## ANCHORED AT THE PANEL'S LEFT EDGE, NOT AT THE ESTIMATE. Placed at the
  ## point with hjust = 0 the text starts wherever the estimate happens to
  ## land and runs off the right edge -- which is what the first render did.
  ## Anchoring it left makes the annotation's position independent of the data.
  ## THE FOLD IS NOT PRINTED, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE PANEL. By fold of
  ## medians the pre-treatment cohort is the larger of the two (1.16 against
  ## 1.12); by odds ratio the on-treatment cohort is (1.21 against 1.07).
  ## Printing both put the two orderings side by side, so a reader comparing
  ## cohorts got opposite answers from the dots and from the text beside them.
  ## The legend already explains why the odds ratio is the plotted quantity;
  ## printing the fold next to it reintroduces exactly the comparison the
  ## choice of axis was made to avoid. Medians stay -- they are the raw numbers
  ## and they order nothing.
  d$lab <- sprintf("%.2f%% vs %.2f%%\n%s",
                   d$median_NR_pct, d$median_R_pct, d$ptxt)
  .covers <- if ("covers_on_treatment" %in% names(s))
    isTRUE(s$covers_on_treatment[grepl("^before", s$cohort) & s$quantity == "chaperones"]) else NA
  .ref <- s$gap_logit[!grepl("^before", s$cohort) & s$quantity == "chaperones"]

  ## A RATIO AXIS IS LOGARITHMIC OR IT LIES. On a linear axis 1/1.2 and 1.2 sit
  ## at different distances from 1, so an interval that is symmetric in the
  ## estimated quantity looks lopsided and the no-difference line looks
  ## off-centre.
  .rng <- range(c(d$or_lo, d$or_hi, 1), na.rm = TRUE)
  .x_lab <- .rng[1]                      # left edge, in data units
  ggplot(d, aes(or_NR_over_R, site, colour = site)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = or_lo, xmax = or_hi), linewidth = .7) +
    geom_point(size = PT_BIG) +
    geom_text(aes(x = .x_lab, label = lab), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, nudge_y = .10,
              size = 1.9, lineheight = .95, colour = "grey30", show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10",
                       breaks = c(.8, .9, 1, 1.1, 1.25, 1.5),
                       labels = function(x) sprintf("%.2g", x),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(.04, .30))) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = c(Sheba = "Before treatment\n(Sheba)",
                                Pittsburgh = "On treatment\n(Pittsburgh)"),
                     expand = expansion(add = c(.40, .95))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_COHORT, guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = .rng) +
    labs(x = "Chaperone share, non-responders / responders (odds ratio, 95% interval)",
         y = NULL,
         title = "Both cohorts put the difference on the same side; one can resolve it",
         subtitle = if (isTRUE(.covers))
           sprintf(paste("the pre-treatment interval covers the on-treatment estimate",
                         "(%+.3f on the logit scale),\nso it cannot exclude a difference",
                         "of that size — underpowered rather than absent"), .ref)
         else
           "intervals from the same plex-adjusted model the permutation tests") +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(lineheight = .9))
}, "4B chaperone share both cohorts")

## ===========================================================================
## ED9F — where the pre-specified set sits among the COG categories
## ===========================================================================
## WHAT THIS PANEL IS FOR. The ensemble of sets does not transfer between
## cohorts: of the 29 scored in both, 11 agree in sign and the scores are
## otherwise unrelated (Spearman -0.05). Stated bare that reads as a failure.
## It is not, and this panel is why -- the ensemble is the SCALE against which
## the pre-specified set's position means something. COG O was fixed in advance
## and was not drawn from this family, so its rank here is descriptive and the
## family supplies a reference, NOT A TEST. The legend must say so.
##
## THE REFERENCE EXCLUDES THE PAPER'S OWN CONSTRUCTED SETS. Five of the 29 are
## ours rather than COG categories -- O_chap, chaperones, O_chap_noGD,
## O_remainder, ribosomal -- and the first three are near-duplicates of the
## target. Ranked against all 29, COG O comes THIRD on the signed product and
## the two sets above it are O_chap and chaperones: the target outranked by
## copies of itself. Dropping the constructed sets puts it first under both
## statistics, 2.2x clear of the runner-up, and removes a question any reader
## would ask. The merged codes stay: they are additional sets, not copies, and
## keeping them is the conservative choice.
##
## THE STATISTIC. min(|NES|) with sign concordance required -- how large the
## SMALLER of the two scores is, given the two agree. It is deliberately not
## named after a cohort: the smaller score is Pittsburgh's for four of the
## nine agreeing categories and Sheba's for five, so "the pre-treatment
## cohort's score" would be wrong a little under half the time. Sign
## concordance only, so categories
## agreeing in the RESPONDER direction stay in the reference and there is more
## to beat. NES is an ordering device here, as the methods say; nothing in this
## panel is an effect size.
p5joint <- panel({
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B45_share_panel", "per_set_scored_both_cohorts.csv")
  if (!file.exists(f))
    stop("ED9F: B45 output not found. Run source(\"B45_share_panel_data.R\") first; ",
         "expected ", f, call. = FALSE)
  j <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (!all(c("set", "NES_pitt", "NES_sheba") %in% names(j)))
    stop("ED9F: B45 table lacks set/NES columns -- re-run B45", call. = FALSE)
  ## Recomputed rather than read, so this panel works off either B45 revision
  ## and cannot inherit a stale classification.
  j$kind <- ifelse(grepl("_", j$set) | grepl("[a-z]", j$set), "constructed",
            ifelse(nchar(j$set) == 1L, "single", "merged"))
  j <- j[j$kind %in% c("single", "merged"), , drop = FALSE]
  j <- j[is.finite(j$NES_pitt) & is.finite(j$NES_sheba), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(j)) stop("ED9F: no COG category scored in both cohorts", call. = FALSE)
  j$agree <- (j$NES_pitt < 0) == (j$NES_sheba < 0)
  j$stat  <- ifelse(j$agree, pmin(abs(j$NES_pitt), abs(j$NES_sheba)), 0)
  j$dir   <- ifelse(!j$agree, "the cohorts disagree",
              ifelse(j$NES_pitt < 0, "agree, non-responders", "agree, responders"))
  ## MERGED CODES ARE NAMED SHORT HERE, AND ONLY HERE. pretty_set expands them
  ## in full -- "Lipid metabolism + Translation + Cell wall, membrane [IJM]" --
  ## which is right on a main-figure axis with a handful of rows and wrong on
  ## this one: at half width those labels take more of the panel than the data
  ## do, and every merged code but one sits at zero anyway. Single-letter
  ## categories keep their usual names, so nothing a reader compares across
  ## figures is renamed.
  j$nm    <- ifelse(j$kind == "merged",
                    sprintf("Merged categories [%s]", j$set), pretty_set(j$set))
  j <- j[order(j$stat, -abs(j$NES_pitt)), ]
  j$nm    <- factor(j$nm, levels = j$nm)
  .iO      <- which(j$set == "O")
  .rk      <- if (length(.iO)) sum(j$stat > j$stat[.iO]) + 1L else NA_integer_
  .PAL_DIR <- c("agree, non-responders" = "#0072B2",
               "agree, responders"     = "#009E73",
               "the cohorts disagree"  = "grey75")
  ggplot(j, aes(stat, nm, colour = dir)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = stat, yend = nm), linewidth = .4) +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL * 1.2) +
    { if (length(.iO))
        annotate("text", x = j$stat[.iO], y = j$nm[.iO], label = "  pre-specified",
                 hjust = 0, size = 2.1, colour = "#0072B2", fontface = "bold") } +
    scale_colour_manual(values = .PAL_DIR, name = NULL,
                        breaks = names(.PAL_DIR), drop = FALSE) +
    ## TWO ROWS. On one row the third entry ran past the right page edge and
    ## the PDF shipped it as "the cohorts disag".
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
    ## ROOM FOR THE FLAG. At 0.22 the "pre-specified" label ran off the right
    ## edge, because it starts at the leading point and that point is the
    ## panel's maximum by construction.
    ## 19 Oct: AND CLIP OFF, rather than more headroom still. With the legend
    ## out of the bottom the 0.50 expansion no longer fits the label either.
    ## Widening it to 1.3 does, but stretches the axis to 3 and shrinks every
    ## bar by a third. The label sits on the top row, where the margin beside it
    ## is empty, so letting it overflow costs nothing and the axis stays 0 to 2.
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .50))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Smaller of the two cohorts' enrichment scores, where they agree in sign",
         y = NULL,
         title = "The pre-specified category leads the family it was never drawn from",
         subtitle = sprintf(paste("%d COG categories scored in both cohorts; the paper's own",
                                  "constructed sets are excluded so\nthe target is not ranked",
                                  "against variants of itself.%s The family supplies a scale,",
                                  "not a test."),
                            nrow(j),
                            if (!is.na(.rk)) sprintf(" COG O ranks %d of %d.", .rk, nrow(j)) else "")) +
    ## 17 Oct: 6 pt COLLIDED, and 5 pt was the answer then -- twenty-four
    ## categories shared a 78 mm cell of which the title, subtitle, a two-row
    ## legend and the x axis took some 33 mm, leaving about 1.9 mm a row against
    ## the 2.1 mm a 6 pt line needs.
    ## 19 Oct: THE CAUSE IS FIXED, SO THE 5 pt GOES BACK. The legend moves to the
    ## right and the cell grows to 93 mm (ED9 weights its rows now), which leaves
    ## about 2.8 mm a row. Rendered at both sizes before changing it: 6 pt fits
    ## with separation to spare, and the labels were the thing being read.
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))
}, "ED9F joint position")

## What the enrichment is made of in each cohort. Panel B gives the GroEL/DnaK
## FRACTION; this gives the composition behind it — which orthologs lead, and the
## tail the discovery cohort has that the pre-treatment cohort does not. It is
## the finest resolution at which these two cohorts can be compared, since they
## share no protein identifiers and only part of an annotation vocabulary.
p5led <- panel({
  need("paths")
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B27_what_leads", "what_leads.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("B27 output not found; run B27_what_leads.R")
  b <- readRDS(f)
  ## Hand-written, so checked against KEGG's own list on 10 Oct: fifteen of the
  ## sixteen agreed and K03545 did not. It was labelled ClpA; K03545 is tig,
  ## trigger factor, and no ClpA (K03694) is in the frozen chaperone set at all.
  ## The wrong label reached the Results prose, which named ClpA as a leading
  ## contributor. Verify any addition here the same way rather than by memory.
  nm <- c(K04077 = "GroEL", K04043 = "DnaK", K13993 = "HSP20", K03687 = "GrpE",
          K03695 = "ClpB", K03545 = "trigger\nfactor", K04078 = "GroES", K04079 = "HtpG",
          K03686 = "DnaJ", K03768 = "cyclophilin B", K03671 = "thioredoxin",
          K04085 = "tusA", K03386 = "peroxiredoxin", K05838 = "ybbN",
          K01304 = "pyroglutamyl-\npeptidase", K01415 = "endothelin-\nconverting enz.")
  mk <- function(x, lab) {
    t <- x$tb
    data.frame(ko = names(t), n = as.integer(t), cohort = lab)
  }
  d <- rbind(mk(b$pitt, "Pittsburgh"), mk(b$sheba, "Sheba"))
  d <- d[d$n >= 2, , drop = FALSE]          # a single protein is not a contributor
  d$cohort <- factor(d$cohort, levels = c("Pittsburgh", "Sheba"))
  d$shared <- d$ko %in% b$shared
  d$lab <- ifelse(d$ko %in% names(nm), nm[d$ko], d$ko)
  ord <- tapply(d$n, d$lab, max); d$lab <- factor(d$lab, levels = names(sort(ord)))
  ggplot(d, aes(n, lab, fill = shared)) +
    geom_col(width = .7) +
    ## A common x-scale: the two leading edges reach similar maxima, so free
    ## scales bought nothing and invited a reader to compare bar lengths that
    ## were not comparable.
    facet_wrap(~ cohort, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = unname(PAL_RESP[["NR"]]), `FALSE` = "grey72"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "Leads in both", `FALSE` = "One cohort only"),
                      name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Proteins in the leading edge", y = NULL,
         title = "GroEL and DnaK lead the enrichment in both cohorts",
         subtitle = "orthologs contributing two or more proteins") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}, "4C leading edge")

## Order follows the order the text cites them: the null, then the rank
## concordance, then the two-protein dominance that explains the breadth
## difference, then the leading edge.
## p5rank -> p5setp (reviewer 5 §4 and §2B): the rank panel ranked by NES, which
## Methods 7 declares non-comparable across sets. p5setp scores each set against
## its own null instead. p5rank keeps its statement and moves to ED9.
## FLAT DESIGN: b sat at x = 220.6 pt and d at 235.4, a 5.2 mm stagger in the
## panel letters. Same cause and same fix as fig_state above.
fig_external <- wrap_titles(p5b) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p5setp)) +
                wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p5led)) + wrap_titles(p5d) +
                plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = TAG_LEVELS) & theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1))
fig_external

fig_baseline <- (wrap_titles(p5b) | wrap_titles(p5d)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = TAG_LEVELS) &
  theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1))
fig_baseline
```

# Assemble and write

```{r fig3-clade}
## Figure 3 — the layer failure is clade-structured.
## Every component is in figure_inputs.rds except the metagenome composition used
## by panel C, which falls back to the proteome-derived branch alone if absent.

p3ca <- panel({
  need("gen_coupling")
  gen_coupling |>
    filter(!is.na(phylum)) |>
    ggplot(aes(rho_clr, reorder(genus, rho_clr), colour = phylum)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    ## Point size carries peptide evidence, so the panel answers on its own the
    ## first question a reader asks of it — whether the uncoupled clade is simply
    ## the thinly-measured one. The Bacteroidota points are not the small ones.
    geom_point(aes(size = psm), alpha = .9) +
    ## breaks_log(3) returned one break, so the legend said nothing. Explicit
    ## breaks spanning the observed range, and the legend placed beneath the
    ## clade key rather than beside it.
    scale_size_area(max_size = 2.6, name = "PSMs",
                    breaks = c(300, 1000, 3000, 10000),
                    labels = scales::label_comma()) +
    ## The clade medians, drawn. The panel's whole point is that one clade sits
    ## apart, and asking a reader to average 29 dots by eye is asking them to
    ## take the title on trust.
    geom_vline(data = ~ .x |>
                 dplyr::filter(phylum %in% c("Bacillota", "Bacteroidota")) |>
                 dplyr::group_by(phylum) |>
                 dplyr::summarise(m = median(rho_clr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
               aes(xintercept = m, colour = phylum), linetype = 2, linewidth = .45,
               show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_CLADE, name = NULL) +
    ## 18 Oct: ACROSS PATIENTS, NOT WITHIN -- the axis said the wrong thing.
    ## rho_clr is one Spearman per genus down the PATIENT axis: rho_of()
    ## correlates A[, g] against Bm[, g], a column being one genus over all
    ## samples. Only the CLR centring is within-sample (sweep over rowMeans),
    ## which is presumably where "within patients" came from. ED5d already
    ## labelled the identical quantity "across patients", so the two panels
    ## contradicted each other. p2f carried the same wrong label and is fixed
    ## too (it is in the superseded list, kept standalone for reviewers).
    labs(x = "Metagenome vs proteome, across patients\n(CLR, Spearman)",
         y = NULL, title = "Genus abundance couples between layers, except in one clade",
         subtitle = "dashed lines: the Bacillota and Bacteroidota medians") +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.2), legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left")
}, "2A genus coupling")

p3cb <- panel({
  need("pep_ph", "chap_new")
  d <- pep_ph |> mutate(is_chap = Protein %in% chap_new) |>
    group_by(phylum = tax) |>
    summarise(n = n(), n_chap = sum(is_chap), pct = 100 * n_chap / n, .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(n >= 500) |> arrange(desc(n))
  d |>
    ggplot(aes(pct, reorder(phylum, pct))) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey72", width = .65) +
    ## The label sits outside the bar, so the panel needs room for it. At 30%
    ## expansion "6,119 / 63,398" was clipped to "6,119 / 63,39" at the edge.
    ## Clipping is turned off as well, so a long label cannot be cut by the panel
    ## border even if the expansion is not quite enough.
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s / %s", format(n_chap, big.mark = ","),
                                  format(n, big.mark = ","))),
              hjust = -0.08, size = 2.1) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .55))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Chaperone share of that clade's PSMs (%)", y = NULL,
         title = stat_sub(sprintf("Chaperone protein is %.0f-fold denser in Bacillota",
                                  clade_val(d, "Bacillota", "pct") / clade_val(d, "Bacteroidota", "pct")),
                          "clade density ratio"),
         subtitle = stat_sub(sprintf("%.1f%% against %.1f%% — the classes are not evenly distributed across clades",
                                     clade_val(d, "Bacillota", "pct"),
                                     clade_val(d, "Bacteroidota", "pct")), "clade densities"))
}, "2C density")

p3cc <- panel({
  need("OP", "pep_g", "chap_new")
  ## norm_id() lives in the analysis document and is not exported, so the
  ## metagenome branch failed with "could not find function". Defined locally.
  ## Must match the analysis document exactly — it uses tolower(), and an
  ## upper-case fallback would have joined differently and silently rather than
  ## failing. Exported now; this is the guard if an old bundle is loaded.
  if (!exists("norm_id"))
    norm_id <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", as.character(x)))
  S <- OP$d$sample; is_chap <- OP$rd$Protein %in% chap_new
  gen <- count(pep_g, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  num <- sapply(gen, function(g) { r <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g]
    colSums(OP$a[intersect(r, which(is_chap)), S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) })
  den <- sapply(gen, function(g) { r <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g]
    colSums(OP$a[r, S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) })
  rownames(num) <- rownames(den) <- S
  obs <- rowSums(num) / rowSums(den)
  pred_from <- function(W) {              # W: rows = samples, cols = genera
    gc <- intersect(colnames(W), colnames(num))
    vapply(rownames(W), function(s) {
      keep <- setdiff(S, s)
      prop <- colSums(num[keep, gc, drop = FALSE]) /
              pmax(colSums(den[keep, gc, drop = FALSE]), 1e-9)
      w <- as.numeric(W[s, gc]); tot <- sum(w, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (!is.finite(tot) || tot <= 0) NA_real_ else sum(w / tot * prop, na.rm = TRUE)
    }, 0)
  }
  d <- tibble(sample = S, observed = obs,
              predicted = pred_from(den / rowSums(den)), source = "from the proteome")
  ## the cross-layer version, if the metagenome composition is in the session
  if (all(vapply(c("mpa_raw", "ko_cpm", "smap", "KEEP_5M"), exists, logical(1)))) {
    link <- OP$d |> select(sample) |>
      inner_join(smap |> select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
      mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
    keep_bio <- ko_cpm |> filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |> distinct(bio) |> pull(bio)
    W <- mpa_raw |>
      filter(stringr::str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == 5, grepl("\\|g__", clade_name)) |>
      mutate(genus = sub(".*\\|g__", "", clade_name)) |> select(-clade_name) |>
      pivot_longer(-genus, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
      mutate(sample_mg = mg_clean(raw)) |>
      inner_join(ko_cpm |> distinct(sample, bio), by = c("sample_mg" = "sample")) |>
      filter(bio %in% keep_bio, genus %in% gen) |>
      group_by(bio, genus) |> summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
      inner_join(link |> select(sample, bio), by = "bio") |>
      select(sample, genus, pct) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = genus, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
    Wm <- as.matrix(W[, -1]); rownames(Wm) <- W$sample
    d <- bind_rows(d, tibble(sample = rownames(Wm), observed = obs[rownames(Wm)],
                             predicted = pred_from(Wm), source = "from the metagenome"))
  }
  d <- d |> filter(is.finite(observed), is.finite(predicted)) |>
    mutate(source = factor(source, levels = c("from the proteome", "from the metagenome")))
  lab <- d |> group_by(source) |>
    summarise(r = cor(observed, predicted), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(txt = sprintf("r = %+.2f", r))
  ggplot(d, aes(100 * predicted, 100 * observed)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = 3, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL, colour = "grey30", alpha = .85) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = .45,
                colour = "#0072B2") +
    ## geom_label, not geom_text: at the top-left of the metagenome facet a data
    ## point sits directly under this annotation and the two overprint. A filled
    ## label with no border keeps the r value readable without adding a box.
    geom_label(data = lab, aes(label = txt), x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.15,
               vjust = 1.25, size = 2.6, inherit.aes = FALSE,
               fill = "white", alpha = .85, label.size = 0,
               label.padding = unit(0.9, "mm")) +
    ## THE TWO ARMS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING, and the facet strips now say
    ## so. The proteome-derived predictor is built from the same measurements as
    ## the observed value, so its r is an internal-consistency check and not a
    ## prediction; only the metagenome arm is out of layer, and it is the one the
    ## claim rests on. Labelling them identically invited the r = +0.58 to be
    ## read as predictive performance.
    facet_wrap(~ source, labeller = labeller(source = c(
      "from the proteome"   = "from the proteome\n(internal consistency)",
      "from the metagenome" = "from the metagenome\n(out of layer: the test)"))) +
    labs(x = "Composition-weighted prediction (%)", y = "Observed chaperone share (%)",
         title = "Composition predicts chaperone output from protein, and anti-predicts it from genes",
         subtitle = "the proteome arm is an internal-consistency check; only the metagenome arm is out of layer, and it runs backwards")
}, "2D prediction")

## THE RE-SEARCH HAD NO PANEL. The concatenated-database experiment is the
## strongest evidence in this paper — it is the only place where a competing
## explanation was tested by experiment rather than by argument, and the result
## ran AGAINST the artefact hypothesis: adding 337,648 Bacteroidota sequences,
## a 171% expansion of that clade's search space, widened the gap instead of
## closing it. It was reported in text only while three main-figure panels showed
## controls. This panel puts it in Figure 3, where the claim it defends lives.
p3ce <- panel({
  ## C2 saves a LIST — per_genus, summary, gap_old, gap_new, prediction, counts —
  ## so as.data.frame() on the whole thing tries to bind components of length 58,
  ## 4, 1, 8, 6 and 3 into one frame and fails. The clade table is `summary`.
  f <- find_first(file.path(paths$out_dir,
         c("concat_research", "final_run/concat_research", ".")),
         "^concat_research_clade\\.rds$")
  d <- if (exists("c2_clade")) c2_clade else if (!is.na(f)) readRDS(f) else NULL
  if (is.null(d)) stop("C2 output not found. Run C2_rescore_clade.R, or place ",
                       "concat_research_clade.rds under ", paths$out_dir)
  tb <- if (is.data.frame(d)) d else if (!is.null(d$summary)) as.data.frame(d$summary) else NULL
  if (is.null(tb))
    stop("the C2 object has no `summary` table; it holds: ",
         paste(names(d), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  need_cols <- c("which", "clade", "median_rho")
  if (!all(need_cols %in% names(tb)))
    stop("C2 summary lacks: ", paste(setdiff(need_cols, names(tb)), collapse = ", "),
         "; it has: ", paste(names(tb), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  tb <- tb[tb$clade %in% c("Bacillota", "Bacteroidota"), , drop = FALSE]
  tb$arm <- factor(ifelse(grepl("^orig", tb$which), "original\ndatabase",
                                                    "concatenated\ndatabase"),
                   levels = c("original\ndatabase", "concatenated\ndatabase"))
  ggplot(tb, aes(arm, median_rho, colour = clade, group = clade)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .6) +
    geom_point(size = PT_BIG) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.2f", median_rho)), size = 2.1,
              vjust = -1.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_CLADE, name = NULL, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .22))) +
    ## The two series are labelled at their own lines rather than in a legend
    ## strip below the panel: fewer eye movements, and the space goes to data.
    ## Room is made INSIDE the panel rather than by widening the margin and
    ## turning clipping off: the previous version ran the clade names off the
    ## right edge and sat them on top of the value labels. The names now sit to
    ## the right of the final point at its own height; the values stay above.
    geom_text(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, arm == levels(.x$arm)[2]),
              aes(label = clade), hjust = -0.18, vjust = 0.5, size = 2.4,
              fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.15, 0.95))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Median coupling (CLR, Spearman)",
         title = "Adding the missing sequences does not rescue the uncoupled clade",
         subtitle = paste("+337,648 Bacteroidota sequences, a 171% expansion of that",
                          "clade's search space")) +
    theme()
}, "2B re-search")

p3cd <- panel({
  need("gen_coupling")
  gen_coupling |> filter(!is.na(phylum)) |>
    ggplot(aes(psm, rho_clr, colour = phylum)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL) +
    ## NO MARGINAL FIT. The line drawn here ignored clade, while the subtitle
    ## reports the clade and depth terms of a joint model -- so the line was not
    ## the model being quoted.
    scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10") +
    ## na.value, as in the fig2 clade panel: this table is not filtered to the
    ## four palette clades, and a named `values` vector gives every other phylum
    ## NA, which drops its genera from a panel whose legend says "each genus".
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_CLADE, guide = "none", na.value = "grey70") +
    ## 18 Oct: THE Y TITLE NAMES BOTH LAYERS, and the subtitle names the clade.
    ## "Coupling (CLR, Spearman)" did not say coupling of what to what; the
    ## quantity is the per-genus correlation ACROSS PATIENTS between that
    ## genus in the metagenome and the same genus inferred from peptides --
    ## the +0.332 the Results quote over these 29 genera. And "clade term" is
    ## the coefficient on I(phylum == "Bacteroidota"), not a taxonomy-wide
    ## term, so it is named for what it is.
    labs(x = "PSMs for that genus (log scale)",
         y = "Metagenome-to-proteome correlation\nacross patients (Spearman on CLR)",
         title = "Not evidence depth",
         subtitle = stat_sub(sprintf(
         "Bacteroidota against other phyla %+.3f (p = %.4f), with evidence depth at %+.3f (p = %.3f)",
         gen_depth_terms["I(phylum == \"Bacteroidota\")TRUE", 1],
         gen_depth_terms["I(phylum == \"Bacteroidota\")TRUE", 4],
         gen_depth_terms["log10(psm)", 1], gen_depth_terms["log10(psm)", 4]),
         "clade/depth terms"))
}, "ED4D depth")
```

## p3cd ("Not evidence depth") moves to Supplementary. It is a control — it says
## what the clade gap is NOT. The re-search says what it SURVIVES, which is the
## stronger statement and the one that belongs in the main figure.
## Letters follow the citation order in the manuscript: the coupling failure,
## then the re-search that tests the database explanation for it, then the
## chaperone density, then the composition-weighted prediction. The observation
## and its control are row one; the consequence and its quantification row two.
fig_clade <- (wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p3ca)) | wrap_titles(p3ce)) /
             (wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p3cb)) | wrap_titles(p3cc)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = TAG_LEVELS) & theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1))
fig_clade
