```{r assemble-mains}
## FIGURE 2 AND FIGURE 4, composed here because reviewer 5 §4's moves cross the
## order the panels are defined in: Figure 2 takes p5e from ED3 and Figure 4
## takes p4a from ED7, both defined after their own figure's chunk. Composing
## them at the point of use would have thrown; composing them here is the same
## pattern fig_clade already uses.
##
## Figure 2: p2d out (two points, less than a sentence of text; now ED8), p5e in
## (the per-arm advantage with the coupling level in each row label -- the panel
## that shows coupling rising 0.24 -> 0.68 while the advantage stays at zero).
##
## 14 Oct: THREE PANELS, NOT SIX. p2b, p2c and p2g go to ED3. This is a word
## budget, not a layout preference. Nature prices an 8-page Article at 4300
## words with 5-6 MODEST display items -- modest meaning about a quarter page,
## ~270 words -- and a composite at ~600, with the text "reduced accordingly"
## to pay for composites. At five composites the body owes ~600 words it does
## not have. Three panels makes this a modest item and buys the coupling
## result -- the paper's title claim -- its place in the main text instead of
## Extended Data, which is where a four-figure paper had put it.
##
## What stays is the claim: a is own against stranger, b is where the
## patient-specific variance actually goes, c is the advantage at all three
## resolutions in both cohorts. What leaves is defensive -- the
## 200-most-variable scatter, the set-level tracking and the taxonomic
## positive control -- and the text cites all three as ED3c-e.
##
## TWO COLUMNS, NOT TWO ROWS. c went full width for one knit and read
## stretched -- correctly: p5e was drawn at 88 mm in the six-panel version and
## nothing was wrong with it there, so widening it to 180 was a fix for a
## problem it did not have. The note this replaces had it backwards.
## a over b in the left column, c spanning both rows in the right, puts p5e
## back at its drawn width and spends the height it gains on the vertical
## intervals of its six points instead of on a spacer. No empty quadrant, which the row layout
## needed once the three defensive panels left.
## THE OUTER PARENTHESES ARE LOAD-BEARING. `+` binds tighter than `|` in R, so
## `A | B + plot_annotation(...)` annotates B ALONE and the composition gets no
## tags at all. That shipped once: Figure 2 knitted with no a/b/c while its
## legend cited all three. Any future edit to this expression keeps the parens.
## 15 Oct: p2five JOINS AS d. The five-cohort result is the paper's broadest
## claim and was its least visible: the three independent datasets sat in
## Supplementary Note 7 while this figure showed only our own two cohorts,
## which reads as a melanoma paper with a supplement rather than a general
## result about metagenomic inference. Two columns of two; c keeps the right
## column's top -- its six points each carry a vertical interval, so it
## needs the depth -- and d, which IS a five-row forest, sits under it.
## 17 Oct: FLAT DESIGN. `(a/b) | (c/d)` lays each COLUMN out on its own, so the
## two rows meet at different heights and b sat 3 mm below d. "AC\nBD" is the
## same arrangement on one grid -- p2a top-left, p2var bottom-left, p5e top-right,
## p2five bottom-right -- so the row boundary is shared and the letters line up.
## 19 Oct: "AC\nBD" -> "AB\nCD". The design string was COLUMN-MAJOR, so the
## grid put a and b in the left column and c and d in the right, and the figure
## read a, c across the top row and b, d across the bottom. The letters were
## right and the citations were in order; it was the eye that met them out of
## sequence. Row-major now: a, b on the top row, c, d on the bottom.
## NOTHING ELSE MOVES. Tag letters follow the ADD order, which is unchanged, so
## p2a is still a, p2var b, p5e c, p2five d and no citation in the text or the
## legend needs touching. Both rows were already half-width cells, so no panel
## changes size; only which panel sits above which. The pairing that results is
## the better one anyway: the two on-treatment panels share the top row and the
## two multi-cohort panels the bottom, where before the split was by column.
## 22 Oct 2026: A SCHEMATIC FIRST ROW. The four data panels state the result but
## never state the comparison: panel b's axis says "a stranger's" against "their
## own" without saying what is correlated with what, and the definition of a
## stranger -- the MEDIAN over every other patient, not one of them -- lives only
## in the legend. The strip says both in one picture, and it is the reason the
## data panels are now b-e rather than a-d.
##
## THE ARTWORK CARRIES ITS OWN LETTER, at JS$tag_size and at the x the panel tags
## below use, so the theme tag is blanked on this element only. patchwork still
## SPENDS "a" on it -- tag_levels assigns by position in the composition, not by
## whether the tag renders -- which is exactly what shifts p2a to b and the rest
## after it. AFTER THE FIRST KNIT, LOOK AT THE TOP LEFT OF THE STRIP: one "a"
## means this worked, two means the blanking did not survive the trailing
## `& theme(...)` and the letter must come out of the artwork instead.
##
## The design string is row-major with the strip spanning both columns; its
## height is fixed in mm so the two data rows divide what is left, unchanged.
FIG1A_ART <- file.path(FIG_DIR, "figure1a_own_vs_stranger.png")
FIG1A_MM  <- 36                      # the artwork's print height, 183 x 36 mm
if (!file.exists(FIG1A_ART))
  stop("Figure 1a artwork is missing: ", FIG1A_ART,
       "\n  It is not produced by this document; it is drawn outside R.",
       call. = FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE))
  stop("package 'png' is needed to place Figure 1a", call. = FALSE)
## THE PANEL LETTER IS DRAWN BY patchwork, NOT BY THE ARTWORK. Two knits were
## spent trying to make a raster letter line up with the vector ones and neither
## worked, for a reason no placement argument can fix: rasterGrob fits the image
## INSIDE its cell preserving aspect, so the strip lands at ~97% wherever the
## cell is not its shape. At that scale the baked letter measured 1.52 mm of
## x-height against 1.61 and 1.57 for the vector c and e -- 96% -- and sat at
## x = 3.81 mm against 2.29 and 2.20 for b and d. Pinning the raster left did
## not move it; forcing width = height = 1 npc would have, but at the cost of a
## 3% stretch on artwork that is mostly circles.
##
## So the letter came OUT of the artwork. patchwork now tags this element like
## any other, which makes "a" the same Helvetica-Bold at the same JS$tag_size
## and the same x as b-e BY CONSTRUCTION, and makes it independent of whatever
## scale the raster ends up at. The artwork file changed with this edit: it no
## longer contains a letter. If one reappears in the top left of the strip,
## an older PNG is on the path.
.fig1a <- wrap_elements(full = grid::rasterGrob(png::readPNG(FIG1A_ART),
                                                interpolate = TRUE)) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

fig_coupling <- .fig1a +
  wrap_titles(p2a) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p2var)) +
  wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p5e)) + wrap_titles(p2five) +
  plot_layout(design = "AA\nBC\nDE",
              heights = grid::unit(c(FIG1A_MM, 1, 1), c("mm", "null", "null"))) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = TAG_LEVELS) & theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1))

## Figure 4: p3mx out to ED4; p3f in from ED8 (the per-sample 10.9% against
## 9.7%, which no main figure showed) and p4a in from ED7 (the adjustment
## ladder). Seven panels, so four rows, with p3c full width on the last because
## it carries thirty long category labels.
## 14 Oct: p3f AND p4a OUT TO ED8, five panels in three rows. Seven panels in
## four rows had squeezed rows a-f to 53 mm -- the note below already called
## that too tight and named moving a panel out as the alternative to shrinking
## type that has nowhere to go. Two went. p3f is the per-sample share and p4a
## the adjustment ladder; both are the response difference at sample level,
## which is what ED8 is titled for, and both are cited in the text as ED8e,f.
## What stays is the argument: the enrichment (a), where in the category it
## sits (b), it against its null (c), the survival result (d), and the full
## set-level ordering (e). The three rows give a-d about 59 mm each, up from 53.
## FLAT DESIGN, NOT NESTED ROWS. b sat at x = 209.6 pt and d at 255.9 -- a
## 16.3 mm stagger in the panel letters, the worst of the five main figures.
## `(a|b)/(c|d)` makes each row its own layout, so column two starts wherever
## that row's left panel ends; one design grid gives every row one column.
## The design string IS the old structure: two rows of two, then e full width.
fig_state <- wrap_titles(p3a) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p3d)) +
             ## The survival result is the most clinically legible number in the
             ## paper and sat in a supplementary figure; it fills the slot the
             ## layout was already holding open.
             wrap_titles(p3b) + wrap_titles(p3surv) +
             wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p3c)) +
  ## g carries 30 named sets on its y-axis; at the 5.5 pt floor that is about
  ## 70 mm of text, and on four equal rows it had 45 and printed as a smear.
  ## 1.7 against 1 gives it roughly 89 mm of row, so the panel clears 70 once
  ## its four-line subtitle and axis title are taken off. The cost is that rows
  ## a-f drop from about 62 mm to 53. If that is too tight, the alternative is
  ## to move g to Extended Data -- Reviewer 5 §4 argues Figure 4 is overloaded
  ## -- rather than to shrink the type, which has nowhere left to go.
  ## 1.2, not 1.7: two columns of fifteen need about 55 mm where one column of
  ## thirty needed 70, and the difference goes back to rows a-f, which were down
  ## to 53 mm.
  ## THREE ROWS NOW, so the weight list loses one entry; 1.2 still buys e the
  ## extra height its thirty labels need.
  plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD\nEE", heights = c(1, 1, 1.2)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = TAG_LEVELS) & theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1))
fig_coupling
fig_state
```


```{r write-figures}
## Each entry is (object name, width, height in mm). Reordering the paper is the
## one switch above; nothing else in this file knows about figure numbers.
## `decomp` and `baseline` remain here but are NOT in order_keys: decomp's
## panels are now Extended Data Fig. 7e-i and baseline is folded into
## `external`. The export loop walks order_keys, so entries absent from it are
## not written as main figures.
## Figure 1 is three panels now, not four: the cohort table was dropped.
## HEIGHTS ARE AT THE JOURNAL CAPS, not over them. fig_dims() has always
## warned when a figure exceeded JS$h_max (247 mm for a main figure) or
## JS$h_max_supp (240 mm for Extended Data); Figure 4 at 250 and S2 at 250
## had been tripping it for several drafts. Both are now at their cap. The
## check only warns, so it cannot stop a knit -- read its output.
## `design` IS GONE, 16 Oct 2026. Figure 1 was the study schematic plus the two
## sampling histograms; the schematics are dropped and the histograms are now
## ED1 g,h. Four main figures.
spec <- list(## 150 -> 170: still two rows, but the right column is now two
             ## panels rather than one, so c and d share the depth that c had
             ## alone. 85 mm a row keeps c's six points and their vertical intervals
             ## legible and gives d's five interval rows more than they need.
             ## 170 -> 206: the 36 mm schematic row added 22 Oct. The two data
             ## rows keep the 85 mm each they had; only the figure grew.
             coupling = list(obj = "fig_coupling", w = 180, h = 206),
             ## 247 -> 190: four rows become three (p3f and p4a to ED8).
             ## 3.2 weight units against 4.2 at the same mm per unit.
             state    = list(obj = "fig_state",    w = 180, h = 190),
             decomp   = list(obj = "fig_decomp",   w = 180, h = 210),
             clade    = list(obj = "fig_clade",    w = 180, h = 190),
             external = list(obj = "fig_external", w = 180, h = 180),
             baseline = list(obj = "fig_baseline", w = 180, h =  90))
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## embed_fonts_checked(): embed, then CHECK, because three attempts did not
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Every figure shipped on 10 Oct with Helvetica UNEMBEDDED while the run read
## clean. Four separate causes, each sufficient on its own, and all four are
## recorded because each produced a confident wrong answer:
##
##   1. grDevices::embedFonts() with no `options` runs Ghostscript at its
##      defaults, and gs keeps the 14 standard PDF fonts on a NeverEmbed list.
##      Helvetica is one. The call succeeds and embeds nothing.
##   2. The success test was file.size(tmp) > 1000, true of any PDF gs writes.
##      A size test cannot see fonts.
##   3. GS_BIN came from Sys.which("gs"). A knit runs in a child process whose
##      PATH lacks /opt/homebrew/bin, so GS_BIN was "" and the step was skipped
##      even though the console could see gs. Hence the explicit path list.
##   4. The /FontFile check used rawToChar + grepl. A PDF is binary, the string
##      is not valid UTF-8, and grepl on an invalid string returns FALSE with a
##      warning instead of searching -- so in a UTF-8 locale it reported "not
##      embedded" for correctly embedded files. It passed in a C locale.
##
## And the reason this version calls gs directly rather than through
## embedFonts(): -dPDFSETTINGS=/prepress cleared NeverEmbed on gs 10.02.1 but
## not on 10.08.0. [13 Oct: that did not survive. /prepress together with
## -dEmbedAllFonts=true and the image parameters, as in the first invocation
## below, embedded all fourteen figures on 10.08.0. The invocation list in
## embed_fonts_checked() is the record of what works.] Relying on a preset's side effect is what made that a
## version-dependent silent failure. The distiller parameter below says what is
## meant. embedFonts() pastes its `options` into a shell string unquoted, which
## cannot carry an argument containing spaces, so system2 with an argument
## vector is the only way to pass it safely.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## fix_hyphen_glyph(): put code 45 back on /hyphen
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## grDevices::pdf() writes
##     /Differences [ 45/minus ]
## into every font it sets up, UNCONDITIONALLY. It is not the encoding: R's
## own WinAnsi.enc has /hyphen at 45, and PDFDoc.enc and ISOLatin1.enc, which
## also have it there, produce the same Differences array. The device does the
## substitution itself.
##
## The effect is that EVERY hyphen in the figure is drawn with the MINUS
## glyph -- 584/1000 em instead of 333, sitting on the math axis. Across the
## fourteen figures that was 28 words: non-responder, progression-free,
## pre-treatment, one-sided, per-protein, abundance-matched, within-genus and
## the rest, each of them reading as a typo to anyone who looks closely. The
## cairo files never had this; it arrived with the device switch.
##
## Nothing in these figures needs a true minus. The negative axis labels are
## plain ASCII hyphens too (byte 0x2D, the same code), so pointing 45 back at
## /hyphen fixes the words and leaves "-20" as the hyphen-minus every journal
## sets it in anyway.
##
## The replacement string is deliberately the SAME LENGTH as the original, so
## every byte offset in the xref table stays correct and the file needs no
## repair. Run it BEFORE Ghostscript: after embedding, the encoding may sit
## inside a compressed object stream where a byte patch cannot reach it.
fix_hyphen_glyph <- function(f, what = basename(f)) {
  old <- "/Differences [ 45/minus ]"
  new <- "/Differences [45/hyphen ]"
  stopifnot(nchar(old) == nchar(new))
  r   <- readBin(f, "raw", n = file.size(f))
  hit <- grepRaw(old, r, fixed = TRUE, all = TRUE)
  if (!length(hit)) {
    ## Not an error: a figure with no text at all has no font dictionary.
    return(invisible(0L))
  }
  nb <- charToRaw(new)
  for (i in hit) r[i:(i + length(nb) - 1L)] <- nb
  writeBin(r, f)
  invisible(length(hit))
}

embed_fonts_checked <- function(f, what = basename(f)) {
  if (isTRUE(PDF_IS_CAIRO) || !nzchar(GS_BIN)) return(invisible(NA))
  base <- c("-dNOPAUSE", "-dBATCH", "-dSAFER", "-sDEVICE=pdfwrite",
            "-dEmbedAllFonts=true", "-dSubsetFonts=true", "-dAutoRotatePages=/None")
  ## THREE INVOCATIONS, FIRST ONE THAT WORKS. base pdf() only REFERENCES
  ## Helvetica, so whether gs embeds anything depends on how it is asked. The
  ## old single invocation (no /prepress, NeverEmbed cleared by hand) ran
  ## cleanly on 10.08.0 and embedded nothing; the first one below embedded all
  ## fourteen figures on the same build (13 Oct), and on 9.55 and 10.02. The
  ## other two stay as fallbacks. The OUTPUT is what decides -- the check
  ## below looks for /FontFile -- not the exit status, which was 0 every time.
  ## IMAGE PARAMETERS, on every attempt. -dPDFSETTINGS=/prepress is what gets
  ## 9.55 and 10.02 to embed a base-14 reference, but it also brings
  ## Distiller's prepress IMAGE policy with it: tested on Figure 1's schematic
  ## it downsampled 4252 px to 2161 (300 dpi at 183 mm) and re-encoded the
  ## result as JPEG. Both are wrong for line art full of small type, so the
  ## downsampling is switched off and the filter named. The value is
  ## /FlateENCODE -- the FlateDecode spelling is what setdistillerparams
  ## rangechecks on. -sOutputFile must come BEFORE -c, because -c swallows
  ## everything up to -f.
  IMG <- paste("<</DownsampleColorImages false /DownsampleGrayImages false",
               "/DownsampleMonoImages false /AutoFilterColorImages false",
               "/AutoFilterGrayImages false /ColorImageFilter /FlateEncode",
               "/GrayImageFilter /FlateEncode")
  tries <- list(
    ## What 9.55 and 10.02 accept.
    prepress   = list(opt = c("-dPDFSETTINGS=/prepress", "-dCompatibilityLevel=1.4"),
                      dp  = paste(IMG, ">> setdistillerparams")),
    ## Clearing NeverEmbed explicitly, in case the policy is what refuses.
    neverembed = list(opt = "-dCompatibilityLevel=1.5",
                      dp  = paste(IMG, "/NeverEmbed []>> setdistillerparams")),
    ## A REAL font to embed, so nothing counts as substituted. macOS keeps
    ## Helvetica and Arial here; elsewhere the path is ignored.
    fontpath   = list(opt = c("-dPDFSETTINGS=/prepress", "-dCompatibilityLevel=1.4",
                              "-sFONTPATH=/System/Library/Fonts:/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental"),
                      dp  = paste(IMG, ">> setdistillerparams"))
  )
  last <- character()
  for (nm in names(tries)) {
    tmp  <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
    args <- c(base, tries[[nm]]$opt, paste0("-sOutputFile=", tmp),
              "-c", tries[[nm]]$dp, "-f", f)
    last <- tryCatch(system2(GS_BIN, shQuote(args), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE),
                     error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
    if (!file.exists(tmp) || file.size(tmp) < 1000) next
    raw <- readBin(tmp, "raw", n = file.size(tmp))
    if (length(grepRaw("/FontFile", raw, fixed = TRUE))) {
      file.rename(tmp, f)
      if (nm != "prepress") cat("  (", what, ": embedded via the ", nm,
                                " invocation)\n", sep = "")
      return(invisible(TRUE))
    }
    unlink(tmp)
  }
  warning("Ghostscript ran on ", what, " and embedded NO font on any of ",
          length(tries), " attempts. Last output:\n",
          paste(utils::tail(last, 10), collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
  invisible(FALSE)
}

## FOUR main figures, 16 Oct 2026. `design` was Figure 1 and is removed
## entirely; coupling, clade, state and external shift up one, so the paper
## opens on the coupling result and ends on the second cohort. The control
## ladder that was Figure 5 (`decomp`) had already moved to Supplementary: with
## the response state exploratory, three main figures for it — two of them
## controls — make the paper look like a defence of a signal that fails global
## correction.
##
## LEAD_WITH_COUPLING IS NO LONGER CONSULTED. Both of its branches named the
## same four keys once `design` left, so the switch had become a constant
## pretending to be a choice. The editorial question it stood for was answered
## by deleting the figure, not by reordering it.
order_keys <- c("coupling", "clade", "state", "external")
## CLEAR THE DIRECTORY FIRST. The loop only unlinks the figures it is about to
## write, so dropping from six main figures to five left Figure6.pdf behind and
## the count check below failed on a file this run never produced. Supplementary
## figures are matched separately and are not touched.
type_report()
old <- list.files(FIG_DIR, "^Figure[0-9]+\\.(pdf|png)$", full.names = TRUE)
if (length(old)) {
  cat("clearing", length(old), "main-figure file(s) from a previous run\n")
  unlink(old)
}

for (i in seq_along(order_keys)) {
  sp <- spec[[order_keys[i]]]
  ## A missing object used to warn and `next`, so the count check below failed
  ## with no indication of which figure was never assembled. The clade figure was
  ## defined AFTER this loop for several days and only ever wrote because a
  ## previous run had left it in the environment.
  if (!exists(sp$obj))
    stop("Figure", i, " (", order_keys[i], ") was never assembled: `", sp$obj,
         "` does not exist. Its chunk must run BEFORE this loop.", call. = FALSE)
  f <- file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("Figure%d.pdf", i))
  if (file.exists(f)) unlink(f)                    # so a stale file cannot pass
  dm <- fig_dims(sp$w, sp$h, sprintf("Fig%d", i))
  ggsave(f, get(sp$obj), width = dm$w, height = dm$h, units = "mm", device = PDF_DEV)
  ## VERIFY. The previous version reported success from the loop counter alone.
  if (!file.exists(f) || file.size(f) < 1000)
    stop("Figure", i, " did not write to ", f,
         " — the device failed. Nothing above this line is trustworthy.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ## EMBED FONTS. The base pdf() device references Helvetica rather than
  ## embedding it (pdffonts shows "emb: no"), which most journals reject. cairo
  ## embeds on its own; for the fallback, Ghostscript does it after the fact.
  fix_hyphen_glyph(f, sprintf("Figure%d", i))   # before gs: see the note above
  embed_fonts_checked(f, sprintf("Figure%d", i))
  ## RASTER TWIN, from the same object and the same millimetres, so it
  ## cannot drift from the PDF beside it. See the note at PNG_DEV.
  pg <- save_png(get(sp$obj), f, dm$w, dm$h, sprintf("Figure%d", i))
  cat(sprintf("Figure%d  <- %-13s (%3g x %3g mm)  %5.0f kB pdf   %d x %d px  %5.0f kB png\n",
              i, sp$obj, sp$w, sp$h, file.size(f) / 1024,
              pg[["w"]], pg[["h"]], pg[["kb"]]))
}
if (!isTRUE(PDF_IS_CAIRO) && !nzchar(GS_BIN))
  warning("fonts are NOT embedded: cairo is unavailable and Ghostscript was not ",
          "found on the PATH. Most journals will reject these PDFs. Install ",
          "XQuartz (restores cairo) or Ghostscript (enables embedFonts).",
          call. = FALSE)
## VERIFY THE WHOLE SET, not each file in passing. Two rounds of figures went
## out with Helvetica unembedded while the log read clean, so the question
## "did every written PDF end up with its fonts inside it?" gets asked once,
## out loud, against the files on disk.
check_embedding <- function(dir = FIG_DIR) {
  ## THIS PATTERN DID NOT MATCH THE EXTENDED DATA FIGURES. It was written
  ## when the supplementary set was FigureS1..S13; after the rename, nine
  ## of the fourteen files were never looked at and the banner reported
  ## "5 of 5" while nine unembedded figures sat beside them.
  fs <- list.files(dir, "^(Figure[0-9]+|ExtendedDataFig[0-9]+)\\.pdf$",
                   full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(fs)) return(invisible(NULL))
  emb <- vapply(fs, function(f) {
    r <- readBin(f, "raw", n = file.size(f))
    length(grepRaw("/FontFile", r, fixed = TRUE)) > 0   # bytes, not characters
  }, logical(1))
  cat(sprintf("\nfont embedding: %d of %d figures carry /FontFile\n",
              sum(emb), length(emb)))
  if (!all(emb)) {
    cat("  NOT embedded: ", paste(basename(fs[!emb]), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    cat("\n  ", strrep("*", 68), "\n",
        "  THESE FIGURES ARE NOT READY TO SUBMIT. Most journals reject PDFs\n",
        "  whose fonts are referenced rather than embedded.\n", sep = "")
    ## DO NOT GO BACK TO CAIRO TO SOLVE THIS. cairo_pdf embeds at write time,
    ## but it shapes text through HarfBuzz: the tracking goes uneven, fi/fl
    ## become ligature glyphs, and any character outside the family -- U+2212,
    ## which ggplot uses for EVERY negative axis label -- pulls a second font
    ## subset in. That is what the base device was chosen to escape. Embedding
    ## is a post-process here, not a device setting.
    if (nzchar(GS_BIN))
      cat("  Ghostscript is at ", GS_BIN, " and ran, but embedded nothing on\n",
          "  any of the three invocations in embed_fonts_checked(). base pdf()\n",
          "  only REFERENCES Helvetica, so gs must supply the font program\n",
          "  itself; 9.55, 10.02 and 10.08.0 all do with the first invocation.\n",
          "  Check `gs --version` against those, and the warning above for\n",
          "  what gs printed.\n", sep = "")
    else
      cat("  Ghostscript was not found, so nothing could embed. On macOS a\n",
          "  knit sees the system PATH, not /opt/homebrew/bin, but GS_BIN\n",
          "  above also probes that path directly -- if it still came up\n",
          "  empty, Ghostscript is not installed. `brew install ghostscript`,\n",
          "  then re-knit. The figures themselves are correct either way;\n",
          "  only the embedding is missing.\n", sep = "")
    cat("  ", strrep("*", 68), "\n", sep = "")
    ## NOT stop(). Aborting here leaves you with no figures at all, which is
    ## worse than figures that need one more step -- and the banner above is
    ## not something anyone scrolls past.
  }
  invisible(emb)
}

## Every panel that degraded to a placeholder, named, with its message. This is
## the check that was missing: the font banner already refuses to let an
## unembedded set look finished, and this refuses to let a set with error boxes
## in it look finished either.
panel_failures <- function() {
  k <- sort(ls(.PANEL_FAILS))
  if (!length(k)) { cat("\nall panels built; no placeholders\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  cat("\n  ", strrep("*", 68), "\n",
      "  ", length(k), " PANEL", if (length(k) > 1) "S" else "",
      " DREW AN ERROR BOX AND ", if (length(k) > 1) "ARE" else "IS",
      " IN THE WRITTEN PDFs.\n",
      "  These figures are not ready to submit.\n", sep = "")
  for (x in k) cat("    ", x, "\n        ", get(x, envir = .PANEL_FAILS), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  ", strrep("*", 68), "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(k)
}

## ---- LINT: literal statistics left in a subtitle --------------------------------
## The counterpart to panel_failures(), added 13 Oct 2026. A subtitle that prints
## a number typed in when it was first measured renders perfectly and ages in
## silence: that is how ED7f came to state a p range its own point labels
## contradicted, and how Figure 4f kept announcing P = 0.009 while the event
## count beside it updated from the data. This reads the document's own source
## and lists every single-line title or subtitle holding a bare number, so a
## threshold ("the 0.05 rule", "95th percentile") can be told from a measurement.
## It reports rather than fails: some of these are legitimately constants.
## Multi-line sprintf subtitles are not caught -- those are checked by eye.
subtitle_literals <- function(src = knitr::current_input()) {
  if (is.null(src) || !file.exists(src)) {
    cat("\nsubtitle lint: source not found, skipped\n"); return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  L <- readLines(src, warn = FALSE)
  idx <- grep('^\\s*(title|subtitle)\\s*=\\s*"', L)
  hit <- character(0)
  for (k in idx) {
    txt <- sub('^[^"]*"', "", L[k]); txt <- sub('".*$', "", txt)
    if (grepl("[0-9]", gsub("%[-+ #0-9.]*[a-zA-Z]", "", txt)))
      hit <- c(hit, sprintf("    line %d: %s", k, txt))
  }
  if (!length(hit)) {
    cat("\nsubtitle lint: no literal numbers in single-line titles or subtitles\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("\n  ", strrep("-", 68), "\n  ", length(hit),
      " title/subtitle string(s) still carry a literal number.\n",
      "  A threshold is fine; a measurement must come from the plotted object.\n", sep = "")
  cat(paste(hit, collapse = "\n"), "\n  ", strrep("-", 68), "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(hit)
}
subtitle_literals()

wrote <- list.files(FIG_DIR, "^Figure[0-9]+\\.pdf$")
cat("written to", FIG_DIR, "\n"); print(wrote)
if (length(wrote) != length(order_keys))
  stop(sprintf("expected %d main figures, found %d: %s\n  built: %s\n  missing: %s",
               length(order_keys), length(wrote), paste(wrote, collapse = ", "),
               paste(order_keys, collapse = ", "),
               paste(order_keys[!vapply(order_keys, function(k) exists(spec[[k]]$obj), TRUE)],
                     collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)
```

# Supplementary figures S1–S13

Built to the numbering in `MANUSCRIPT_OUTLINE_v2.md`. **Note the collision:** the
project also carries standalone scripts `S1_host_inflammation.R` …
`S8_sheba_power.R` under a *different* numbering — that S1 is this S3, that S8 is
this S9. The outline's scheme is the manuscript's and is what follows; the
scripts should be renumbered or retired rather than left to be confused with it.

Every panel is wrapped in `panel()`, so an object the session lacks produces a
labelled placeholder instead of stopping the knit. `figure-inputs` in
analysis_v17.Rmd now exports what these need.

```{r figS1}
## S1A-C — technical: PSM depth, channel medians before/after normalization,
## residual plex exposure by set.
pS1a <- panel({
  need("qf")
  ## `map_dfr` and bare `assay` failed in the render session: no library() call
  ## in this document loads purrr or SummarizedExperiment, so both depend on what
  ## the session happens to have attached. Base R and an explicit namespace
  ## remove that dependence.
  ## 28 Oct: BATCH ON THE X AXIS. The legend reads "per-channel peptide depth
  ## across labeling batches" and this panel plotted depth against COHORT, with
  ## no plex dimension in it at all -- two boxplots, one per cohort. Mixture is
  ## read from colData, which is where every other panel in this file takes it
  ## from, rather than parsed out of the channel name; if it is missing or does
  ## not align, the panel stops rather than drawing the wrong thing.
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(qf), function(ch) {
    a  <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(qf[[ch]], "psmsLog")
    cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(qf[[ch]])
    if (!"Mixture" %in% colnames(cd))
      stop("pS1a: colData(qf$", ch, ") has no Mixture column, which ED1c needs ",
           "for the per-batch axis", call. = FALSE)
    mx <- as.character(cd[["Mixture"]])[match(colnames(a), rownames(cd))]
    if (anyNA(mx))
      stop("pS1a: colData(qf$", ch, ") does not align with the psmsLog colnames",
           call. = FALSE)
    data.frame(cohort = ch, sample = colnames(a), Mixture = mx,
               n = colSums(!is.na(a)), row.names = NULL)
  })) |>
    ggplot(aes(Mixture, n, colour = cohort)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = .5) +
    geom_jitter(width = .15, size = PT_JITTER, alpha = .7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(pitt = PAL_COHORT[[1]], sheba = PAL_COHORT[[2]]),
                        guide = "none") +
    ## The cohorts are named Pittsburgh and Sheba everywhere else in the set,
    ## including panel d of this very figure. These were the raw list names,
    ## "pitt" and "sheba", lower case -- now on the facet strip, since the x
    ## axis carries the plex. free_x because the two cohorts' plexes differ.
    facet_wrap(~ cohort, scales = "free_x",
               labeller = as_labeller(c(pitt = "Pittsburgh", sheba = "Sheba"))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "PSMs with signal",
         title = "Per-channel depth across labeling batches")
}, "ED1C depth")

pS1b <- panel({
  need("qf")
  md <- apply(SummarizedExperiment::assay(qf$pitt, "psmsLog"), 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(sample = names(md), median = md, row.names = NULL) |>
    ggplot(aes(median)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey78", colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    ## THE AXIS WAS PRINTING -2.021372e-15, -1.010686e-15, 0.000000e+00 ...
    ## Those are the medians, and they are zero: the panel's whole point is
    ## that centering ran. Eleven significant figures of floating-point noise
    ## across a Nature axis says the opposite -- it looks like data. Shown in
    ## units of 1e-15 instead, so the reader sees small integers around zero
    ## and the axis title carries the scale.
    ## PLAIN ASCII, NOT PLOTMATH. expression(... %*% 10^-15 ...) renders the
    ## multiplication sign as U+00D7 and the exponent's minus as U+2212, and
    ## Helvetica carries neither: both fell through to Bitstream Vera Sans, so
    ## the fix for the e-15 axis pulled TWO more substituted faces into a Nature
    ## figure. No forced plus either: "%+.0f" signs the positives and not the
    ## negatives, which gave "-2 -1 0 +1 +2".
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(b) sprintf("%.0f", b * 1e15)) +
    labs(x = "Channel median, log2, units of 1e-15",
         y = "Channels", title = "After median centering",
         subtitle = sprintf("sd %.3g — zero means normalization ran", sd(md)))
}, "UNPLACED per-channel medians")

pS1c <- panel({
  need("r2")
  tibble(protein = names(r2), r2 = r2) |>
    mutate(grp = case_when(protein %in% chap_new ~ "chaperone",
                           protein %in% ribo_new ~ "ribosomal",
                           TRUE                  ~ "all other")) |>
    ggplot(aes(r2, grp)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .4, linewidth = .3) +
    ## NOT PLOTMATH. expression() pulled the Symbol font in for its
    ## inter-token spaces, which was the only reason ED Fig. 1 carried a
    ## third font. U+00B2 is in WinAnsi, so Helvetica draws the superscript
    ## itself. (The minus-for-hyphen in "per-protein" was NOT plotmath --
    ## see fix_hyphen_glyph() below; it affected every hyphen in every
    ## figure.)
    labs(x = "Per-protein R\u00B2 on plex", y = NULL,
         title = "The result sets are the least plex-exposed",
         subtitle = "the 76% figure is the per-SAMPLE share, an aggregate — not this")
}, "ED1D plex exposure")
```

```{r figS2}
## S1D — host:microbial signal ratio per sample, both cohorts.
pS2 <- panel({
  need("OP", "hs")
  hostf <- function(O) {
    s <- O$d$sample
    h <- colSums(hs[, intersect(s, colnames(hs)), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    m <- colSums(O$a[, names(h), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    tibble(sample = names(h), ratio = log2((h + 1) / (m + 1)),
           resp = O$d$resp[match(names(h), O$d$sample)])
  }
  d <- hostf(OP) |> mutate(cohort = "Pittsburgh")
  if (exists("OS")) d <- bind_rows(d, hostf(OS) |> mutate(cohort = "Sheba"))
  ggplot(d, aes(cohort, ratio, colour = resp)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = .55, linewidth = .3,
                 position = position_dodge(.7)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = .12, dodge.width = .7),
               size = .7, alpha = .8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_RESP, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Log2 host : microbial signal",
         title = "Host contamination is a per-sample property, not a per-arm one")
}, "ED1E host:microbial")
```

```{r figS3new}
## S2 — whole-profile separation and diversity, from B15. Written 28 Sep 2026.
## It supports the cohort-characterisation section, which is the first Results
## section, so it sits directly after the measurement QC of S1. It was numbered
## S3 when written; the consolidation below moved it to S2.
## The PCoA is the ordination of the SAME centred distance matrix the PERMANOVA
## used, so the picture and the p-value describe one object rather than two
## analyses that happen to agree.
.b15 <- local({
  if (exists("b15_omnibus")) return(b15_omnibus)
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B15_omnibus", "omnibus.rds")
  if (file.exists(f)) readRDS(f) else NULL
})

pS18a <- panel({
  if (is.null(.b15)) stop("B15 output not found; run B15_omnibus.R")
  arms <- Filter(function(a) !is.null(a$pcoa), .b15[c("proteome","metagenome_pitt","metagenome_sheba")])
  if (!length(arms)) stop("no PCoA coordinates in the B15 output")
  d <- bind_rows(lapply(names(arms), function(k) {
    a <- arms[[k]]
    transform(a$pcoa,
      ## 19 Oct: FOUR LINES, NOT THREE. "P = x, R2 = y, PERMDISP P = z" is about
      ## 41 characters and a facet here is 60 mm, so the line was clipped at BOTH
      ## ends -- the leading P and the last digit of the PERMDISP p were cut off
      ## in all three facets. Breaking it after R2 puts nothing over ~22
      ## characters on a line. The strip grows by one line; b has the height.
      panel = sprintf("%s\nP = %.3f, R\u00B2 = %.3f\nPERMDISP P = %.3f\n%s",
                      a$label, a$p_location, a$r2,
                      if (is.null(a$p_dispersion)) NA_real_ else a$p_dispersion,
                      if (is.null(a$var_explained) || anyNA(a$var_explained)) ""
                      else sprintf("PCo1 %.1f%%, PCo2 %.1f%%",
                                   100 * a$var_explained[1], 100 * a$var_explained[2])))
  }))
  ggplot(d, aes(PCo1, PCo2, colour = resp)) +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL, alpha = .85) +
    stat_ellipse(level = .68, linewidth = .4) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_RESP, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "PCo1", y = "PCo2",
         title = "Whole-profile ordination by response",
         subtitle = "log-ratio distances; ellipses are 68% contours, not tests")
}, "ED2A PCoA")

pS18b <- panel({
  if (is.null(.b15)) stop("B15 output not found")
  al <- .b15[c("sheba_alpha","pitt_alpha")]
  al <- al[!vapply(al, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (!length(al)) stop("no alpha-diversity table in the B15 output")
  d <- bind_rows(lapply(names(al), function(k) {
    m <- as.data.frame(al[[k]]); m$metric <- rownames(m)
    m$cohort <- if (grepl("sheba", k)) "Sheba" else "Pittsburgh"; m
  }))
  ## BARS OF MEDIANS WERE THE PROBLEM. A bar carries a magnitude from zero, so
  ## two medians that differ by a few percent of their own value drew as a
  ## visible step -- the Sheba richness pair read as a difference by response
  ## while the text says alpha diversity does not differ, and the panel showed
  ## no distribution, no uncertainty and no p. B15's alpha() now attaches the
  ## per-sample values, so this draws boxplots with points when they are there.
  ## Without them it falls back to the two medians as POINTS, never bars, and
  ## the p comes from B15's own table either way -- it was always in column P
  ## and this panel simply never used it.
  pv <- d |> dplyr::transmute(cohort, metric, P)
  vals <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(al), function(k) {
    v <- attr(al[[k]], "values")
    if (is.null(v)) return(NULL)
    v$cohort <- if (grepl("sheba", k)) "Sheba" else "Pittsburgh"; v
  }))
  ## EVENNESS DROPPED. B15 computes it as sh / log(pmax(ri, 2)) -- Pielou's J,
  ## which is fixed once Shannon and richness are fixed. Plotting all three put
  ## a deterministic function of columns one and two in column three.
  KEEP <- c("Shannon", "richness")
  d    <- d[d$metric %in% KEEP, , drop = FALSE]
  pv   <- pv[pv$metric %in% KEEP, , drop = FALSE]
  pv$metric <- factor(pv$metric, levels = KEEP)
  if (nrow(vals)) {
    vals <- vals[vals$metric %in% KEEP, , drop = FALSE]
    vals$metric <- factor(vals$metric, levels = KEEP)
  }
  lab_p <- pv |>
    dplyr::mutate(txt = ifelse(is.finite(P),
                               ifelse(P < 0.001, "P < 0.001", sprintf("P = %.2f", P)), ""))
  gg <- if (nrow(vals)) {
    ggplot(vals, aes(resp, value, colour = resp)) +
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = .55, linewidth = .3) +
      geom_jitter(width = .14, size = PT_JITTER, alpha = .75) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_RESP, guide = "none")
  } else {
    ggplot(d |> tidyr::pivot_longer(c(NR, R), names_to = "resp", values_to = "value"),
           aes(resp, value, colour = resp)) +
      geom_point(size = 2) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_RESP, guide = "none")
  }
  gg +
    geom_text(data = lab_p, aes(label = txt), x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.08, vjust = 1.4,
              size = 2.1, inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey25") +
    facet_wrap(cohort ~ metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    ## NO SHARED Y TITLE. The facets are on free scales in different units, so
    ## one label across them said nothing.
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         title = "Alpha diversity by response",
         subtitle = "Shannon and observed richness, with the per-cohort Wilcoxon on each panel")
}, "ED2E alpha")

## The eleven published taxa had no panel: three results in that paragraph —
## that none replicate, that one sits at the boundary, and that one runs the
## other way — were available to a reader only as prose. The last of those is
## the one a reader should not have to take on trust.
pS18c <- panel({
  need("paths")
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B16_signatures", "signatures.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("B16 output not found; run B16_published_signatures.R")
  b <- readRDS(f)
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(b$results), function(k) {
    x <- as.data.frame(b$results[[k]]); if (!nrow(x)) return(NULL)
    x$cohort <- k; x }))
  if (is.null(d) || !nrow(d)) stop("no signature results to plot")
  d <- d[!is.na(d$p), , drop = FALSE]
  ## direction, as the published claim versus what we observe
  d$agrees <- !d$opposite
  ## "treated" was a fourth word for the same thing; PAL_COHORT's names now.
  d$cohort <- factor(ifelse(grepl("sheba", d$cohort, ignore.case = TRUE),
                            "Sheba", "Pittsburgh"),
                     levels = c("Pittsburgh", "Sheba"))
  d$lab <- sub("_", " ", as.character(d$taxon))
  ord <- tapply(d$p, d$lab, min)
  d$lab <- factor(d$lab, levels = names(sort(ord, decreasing = TRUE)))
  ggplot(d, aes(p, lab, colour = agrees, shape = cohort)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_point(size = PT_BIG, alpha = .9) +
    ## 0 DROPPED FROM THE BREAKS. At this width its label overprinted the 0.05
    ## beside it and the axis read "0.0005".
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(.05, .25, .5, .75, 1)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = unname(PAL_CLADE[["Bacillota"]]),
                                   `FALSE` = unname(PAL_CLADE[["Bacteroidota"]])),
                        labels = c(`TRUE` = "published direction",
                                   `FALSE` = "runs the other way"), name = NULL) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(Pittsburgh = 16, Sheba = 17), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "One-sided p, in the published direction", y = NULL,
         title = "No published taxon replicates in either cohort",
         subtitle = "dashed line: 0.05, uncorrected; color shows the observed direction") +
    ## 19 Oct: LEGEND TO THE RIGHT. Two legends stacked under the panel took
    ## about 10 mm of a 60 mm cell, and eleven taxon names had to share what was
    ## left -- they printed about 3.2 mm apart and read as one block. On the
    ## right they cost width, which this panel has (the x axis is a p-value and
    ## stops at 1.00), and the rows open to about 4.4 mm. Same cell height.
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical",
          legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "mm"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}, "ED2B published taxa")

pS18d <- panel({
  ## S2D — cohort against response on one axis (B37). The per-arm PERMANOVA in
  ## S2A tests response WITHIN each cohort and never shows the quantity that
  ## governs the whole two-centre design: site explains far more of the profile
  ## than response does. One picture, two bars.
  ##
  ## THE WHISKER IS THE POINT, not decoration. The old version of this panel
  ## reported cohort 35% on every shared ortholog with a 1e-9 pseudocount, and
  ## with two proteomes that measure different feature sets that number could
  ## have been detection rather than biology. B37 sweeps the prevalence floor;
  ## the whisker is the range across 1.00 / 0.90 / 0.75 / 0.50 / 0.00. Cohort
  ## comes out LARGEST where detection is complete, so dilution with
  ## rarely-seen features lowers it and the effect is in the abundances.
  need("paths")
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B37_variance_partition", "partition.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("B37 output not found; run B37_variance_partition.R")
  b <- readRDS(f)
  rng <- b$sweep |> group_by(term) |>
    summarise(lo = min(r2), hi = max(r2), .groups = "drop")
  d <- b$primary |> left_join(rng, by = "term") |>
    mutate(term = factor(term, levels = c("Response", "Cohort")),
           ## THREE SIGNIFICANT FIGURES, not one decimal place. At %.1f the bars
           ## read 32.4% and 0.6%, which divide to 54 against the title's 51 --
           ## the title takes the ratio from the unrounded r2, and a reader who
           ## divides the labels gets a different number. %.3g keeps the small
           ## bar's second digit (0.638%) so the two agree.
           lab = sprintf("%.3g%%", 100 * r2))
  ratio <- d$r2[d$term == "Cohort"] / d$r2[d$term == "Response"]
  ggplot(d, aes(r2, term)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = term), width = .55) +
    ## THE SWEEP AS POINTS, NOT A WHISKER. Nothing in a range bar says "range
    ## over a tuning parameter", and the default reading is an interval estimate.
    ## One open marker per prevalence floor cannot be misread as a CI and shows
    ## the shape of the sweep, which the bar hid.
    geom_point(data = b$sweep |>
                 dplyr::mutate(term = factor(term, levels = c("Response", "Cohort"))),
               aes(r2, term), shape = 21, size = 1.1, stroke = .35,
               fill = "white", colour = "grey25", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_text(aes(x = hi, label = lab), hjust = -0.25, size = 2.4) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .18))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Cohort = unname(PAL_CLADE[["Bacteroidota"]]),
                                 Response = unname(PAL_CLADE[["Bacillota"]])),
                      guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "Marginal variance explained", y = NULL,
         title = sprintf("Site explains %.0f times what response does", ratio),
         subtitle = paste0("joint model, each term adjusted for the other; bars at the ",
                           d$n_features[1], " orthologs both cohorts\ndetect in every sample, ",
                           "range across prevalence floors 0 to 1")) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}, "UNASSEMBLED variance partition")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ED2E — the taxonomic-level comparison, downstream of the ordination (a) and
## alpha diversity (b). Standard practice in this literature and absent from
## this manuscript, which B16's own header concedes: "The manuscript tests the
## metagenome at phylum level only."
##
## ONE PANEL, NOT SIX, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. B48 forms twelve BH families --
## two cohorts x three ranks x {prevalence, abundance} -- and no feature
## survives in any of them. Six volcanoes would spend a figure page drawing
## twelve empty fields. The quantity that answers the question is one number
## per feature, so every feature in every family is drawn against -log10(P) on
## one axis, with each family's OWN BH boundary marked. A reader sees the whole
## distribution and sees that nothing reaches its line.
##
## THE BOUNDARY IS THE SMALLEST P THAT COULD REACH q = 0.05 IN THAT FAMILY,
## which for the top-ranked feature of m tests is 0.05/m. It is drawn per
## family because m differs by rank, and it is the honest line: a point short
## of it did not fail by a little, it failed against the correction the family
## actually carries.
##
## ABUNDANCE, NOT PREVALENCE, carries the panel. "Differential abundance by
## taxonomic level" is what the convention means, and the prevalence scan is a
## different question -- whether, not how much -- that would double the points
## without changing the reading. Both are in B48's CSVs; the legend says so.
##
## COLOUR IS DIRECTION, not cohort, because cohort is already on the y axis and
## direction is the one thing a reader cannot recover from a P.
##
## THE Y AXIS IS NUMERIC WITH MANUAL BREAKS, not a discrete scale. The boundary
## marks are short vertical segments at family position +/- 0.34, and a layer
## supplying numeric y fixes the scale as continuous -- after which the factor
## from the point layer raises "Discrete value supplied to a continuous scale".
## One scale type, set here, avoids that entirely.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
pS18e <- panel({
  need("paths")
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B48_taxon_scan", "taxon_scan.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("B48 output not found; run B48_taxon_scan.R")
  b <- readRDS(f)
  if (is.null(b$scans) || !length(b$scans)) stop("no scans in the B48 output")

  ORD <- c("Pittsburgh phylum", "Sheba phylum", "Pittsburgh genus",
           "Sheba genus", "Pittsburgh species", "Sheba species")
  d <- bind_rows(lapply(names(b$scans), function(k) {
    x <- b$scans[[k]]
    x <- x[is.finite(x$p_abun) & is.finite(x$q_abun), , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(x)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(fam = k, feature = x$feature, p = x$p_abun, q = x$q_abun,
               dir = ifelse(x$dir_NR_minus_R > 0, "NR", "R"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  if (!nrow(d)) stop("no finite abundance P values in the B48 output")
  LV <- rev(intersect(ORD, unique(d$fam)))
  d$fam <- factor(d$fam, levels = LV)
  ## THE AXIS IS q, NOT P. On a P axis each family needs its own BH boundary,
  ## and 0.05/m -- the smallest P that could ever reach q = 0.05 -- is
  ## numerically Bonferroni, so in a panel that otherwise parses as a Manhattan
  ## plot readers decode the mark as Bonferroni. On a q axis there is one line
  ## at q = 0.05 for every family and a survivor is readable straight off the
  ## panel, which is what the reader came for.
  d$lp  <- -log10(pmax(d$q, .Machine$double.xmin))
  d$y   <- as.numeric(d$fam)

  s <- d |> group_by(fam, y) |>
    summarise(m = n(), nom = sum(p < 0.05),
              surv = sum(q < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  ## 28 Oct: THE COUNTS MOVED TO THE AXIS. They were right-aligned at xmax
  ## inside the panel, and the strings are long enough that they ran back into
  ## the data: a point overprinted a digit on five of six rows, the dashed line
  ## struck through every one of them, and on the Sheba genus row the survivor's
  ## name landed on top of the count string so that neither could be read. On
  ## the axis they cannot collide with anything, and the x range no longer has
  ## to reserve 40% of the panel for a text column. The survivor count is not
  ## repeated here: the derived title states it and the one survivor is named
  ## on the panel.
  ylab <- setNames(sprintf("%s\n%d tested, %d nominal",
                           as.character(s$fam), s$m, s$nom),
                   as.character(s$fam))
  xmax <- max(c(d$lp, -log10(0.05))) * 1.08

  ## THE TITLE IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED. An asserted "nothing survives" that the
  ## annotations contradict is the failure mode here, and it is one re-run away
  ## at any time. The title states what the data in the panel actually show.
  ns  <- sum(s$surv); nf <- nrow(s); nk <- sum(s$surv > 0)
  ttl <- if (!ns)
      "No taxon survives correction at phylum, genus or species, in either cohort"
    else if (ns == 1L) {
      w <- d[which.min(d$q), ]
      sprintf("Only %s clears correction (%s), 1 of %d families",
              w$feature[1], sub(" ", ", ", as.character(w$fam[1])), nf)
    } else
      sprintf("%d features clear correction across %d of %d families; the rest are empty at every rank",
              ns, nk, nf)

  ggplot(d, aes(lp, y)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 2,
               linewidth = .35, colour = "grey30") +
    geom_jitter(aes(colour = dir), height = .20, width = 0,
                size = PT_SMALL, alpha = .7) +
    ## THE ONE SURVIVOR, NAMED. A single point clearing the line in a field of
    ## 1,334 is the panel's whole result and it was indistinguishable from the
    ## rest of the cloud.
    ## ABOVE THE POINT AND RIGHT-ALIGNED TO IT. A surviving point sits near the
    ## right end of the range by construction, so a centred name overruns the
    ## panel and a left-running one at the old hjust = 1.12 crosses its own
    ## row's cloud. Anchored at the point and set above it, the name occupies
    ## the empty band between two rows and stays inside the panel.
    { if (any(d$q < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))
        geom_text(data = d[which(d$q < 0.05), , drop = FALSE],
                  aes(label = feature), hjust = 1.03, vjust = -0.75, size = 1.9,
                  colour = "grey20", inherit.aes = TRUE) } +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_RESP, name = "Higher in",
                        labels = c(NR = "Non-responders", R = "Responders")) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(LV), labels = ylab[LV],
                       limits = c(0.45, length(LV) + 0.55), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ## BREAKS STOP AT THE DATA. The limit runs a little past it to clear the
    ## survivor's name; ticks out there would advertise a range nothing
    ## occupies.
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, xmax), expand = expansion(mult = c(.01, .02)),
                       breaks = 0:ceiling(max(c(d$lp, -log10(0.05))))) +
    labs(x = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)), y = NULL, title = ttl,
         subtitle = paste("abundance where the taxon is present;",
                          "dashed line = Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.05 within each family")) +
    ## Two lines per row, so the leading is tightened and the type dropped a
    ## notch; at the inherited size the pair reads as two separate rows.
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.2, lineheight = 0.92))
}, "ED2C taxonomic scan")

## FOUR ROWS IN THE 240 mm CAP, 60 mm each, and the cost is declared. ED1's
## note rejected a fourth row for that figure because it would squeeze a to d;
## here the fourth row is the taxonomic scan, which is a single numeric axis
## and the most height-tolerant panel in the set, while a (three facets) and b
## (six small boxplots) lose 20 mm each. The alternative was to seat the new
## panel beside b and keep three rows, which renumbers the printed tags of the
## present c and d to d and e and so moves every in-text reference to them.
## The squeeze was taken over the renumbering: e is APPENDED, so a to d keep
## their tags and no reference in the manuscript changes.
##
## Reading order: ordination (a), alpha diversity (b), the published-signature
## test (c) and site against response (d), then the taxonomic comparison at
## three ranks (e) -- downstream of alpha and beta, which is where this
## literature puts it.
## 19 Oct: PANEL ORDER NOW FOLLOWS CITATION ORDER. The text cites the
## cohort-against-response partition first -- it is the reason the two cohorts
## are not combined, which the Results state before anything else about them --
## then the ordination, the published taxa, the taxonomic scan, and alpha
## diversity last. `design` rather than `/` and `|`, because the letters have
## to follow the add order while the grid holds the widths each panel was drawn
## for: a and b share row one, and c, d, e keep the full 180 mm.
## THE ORDINATION DROPS TO HALF WIDTH. It is the one panel this reordering
## costs: it carried three facets across the full page and now has 88 mm. The
## alternative is five rows at 48 mm each, which shortens every panel instead.
## 19 Oct, SECOND PASS: b BACK TO FULL WIDTH. Pairing a and b in one row to hold
## four rows cost the ordination half its width, and its facet strips -- which
## carry the label, the PERMANOVA and PERMDISP p and the variance on each axis --
## were clipped on both sides at 29 mm a facet. That was a regression introduced
## by the reordering, not a fault it inherited. Five single-column rows instead,
## with the heights weighted: a is two bars and needs almost nothing, so it funds
## b and c. Every panel is wrap_elements so the five do not share one axis-text
## column -- c carries taxon names and a carries "Cohort".
## ED2D -- THE METAGENOME'S OWN FUNCTIONAL LAYER AGAINST RESPONSE. The paper's
## premise is that gene content does not predict protein output, so the first
## thing a reader asks of the gene layer is whether its INFERRED function
## separates the arms. It does not, and until now that answer existed only in
## 01_metagenomics_Sheba_Pitt.Rmd section 9.3. BUILT TO MIRROR c, which is the
## taxon scan: same -log10(q) axis, same dashed line at 0.05, so the pair reads
## as one statement at two feature levels. Not a volcano -- the abundance and
## prevalence coefficients are on different scales (log abundance against a
## logistic term) and must not share an x axis, while q is unitless. A ranked-q
## curve was tried first and drawn at 88 mm it is a flat line near 1 with the
## 0.05 rule stranded below it: accurate, and it shows nothing.
## Reads the two MaAsLin3 tables copied into
## `humann_pathway_da/`; the tested sets are 393 and 408 pathways, which is the
## n the Results sentence quotes, so this panel and that sentence cannot drift.
pS18f <- panel({
  need("paths")
  local({
    dir <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "humann_pathway_da")
    f   <- c(Pittsburgh = file.path(dir, "maaslin3_pitt_pathway.tsv"),
             Sheba      = file.path(dir, "maaslin3_sheba_pathway.tsv"))
    if (!all(file.exists(f)))
      stop("ED2d: HUMAnN pathway DA tables not found in ", dir,
           ". Copy all_results.tsv from Results_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt/",
           "metagenomics/humann_da/maaslin3_{pitt,sheba}_pathway/.", call. = FALSE)
    d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(f), function(ch) {
      z <- utils::read.delim(f[[ch]], check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      z <- z[z$metadata == "Response" & is.finite(z$qval_individual), , drop = FALSE]
      if (!nrow(z))
        stop("ED2d: no Response rows with a finite q in ", basename(f[[ch]]), call. = FALSE)
      data.frame(cohort = ch, model = z$model, q = z$qval_individual, row.names = NULL)
    }))
    d$cohort <- factor(d$cohort, levels = c("Pittsburgh", "Sheba"))
    ## prevalence UNDER abundance, so the eye meets the primary model first.
    d$model  <- factor(d$model,  levels = c("prevalence", "abundance"))
    d$lp     <- -log10(pmax(d$q, .Machine$double.xmin))
    ggplot(d, aes(lp, model, colour = cohort)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 2, linewidth = .3,
                 colour = "grey45") +
      geom_jitter(height = .22, width = 0, size = PT_SMALL, alpha = .7) +
      facet_wrap(~ cohort, ncol = 2) +
      ## NO LEGEND. d already carries the NR/R key, and this panel does not
      ## encode direction: with nothing significant the sign carries no claim.
      ## Cohort is on the facet strip, so the colour needs no key either.
      scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_COHORT, guide = "none") +
      labs(x = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)), y = NULL,
           title = "No inferred pathway crosses it either",
           subtitle = stat_sub(sprintf("%d and %d pathways; smallest q %.2f and %.2f",
                                       sum(d$cohort == "Pittsburgh" & d$model == "abundance"),
                                       sum(d$cohort == "Sheba"      & d$model == "abundance"),
                                       min(d$q[d$cohort == "Pittsburgh"]),
                                       min(d$q[d$cohort == "Sheba"])),
                               "pathway scan minima")) +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
            panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(3, "mm"))
  })
}, "ED2D pathway scan")

## 28 Oct: f ARRIVES. ED2 was already AT h_max_supp = 240, so the sixth row is
## funded by every other panel: 5.01 height units become 5.86, which takes the
## unit from 47.9 to 41.0 mm. b and e lose about 8 mm each. The alternative was a
## tenth Extended Data figure, and since the pathway scan is cited in the same
## Results paragraph as b, c, d and e, citation-order numbering would have made
## it ED3 and renumbered everything after it.
## 28 Oct, SECOND PASS: SIX FULL-WIDTH ROWS WAS 41 mm A ROW and every panel
## suffered for it. h_max_supp is 240, so a sixth row has to be paid for by
## narrowing something -- the only question is what. THE TWO SCANS PAIR: d is
## the taxon scan and the new panel is the pathway scan, the same plot at two
## feature levels, each asking whether anything crosses its significance line.
## Side by side they read as one statement instead of two rows of near-misses.
## So pS18f is added BEFORE pS18b, taking position e, and alpha diversity moves
## to f at full width. The heights go back to the five-row weights exactly, so
## EVERY PRE-EXISTING PANEL KEEPS THE HEIGHT IT HAD before f existed; the only
## change is that the taxon scan drops from 180 to 88 mm, which it tolerates --
## six jittered series against one axis, no long tick labels on x.
## THE COST IS ONE LETTER: alpha diversity was ED2e and is now ED2f. The Results
## sentence citing it has to move with it, and the pathway sentence cites 2e.
## 28 Oct, THIRD PASS: pS18d IS OUT. Two bars and a threshold sweep, and
## Supplementary Table 5 already deposits both as rbind(primary, sweep) -- so
## the panel held nothing a sentence plus that table does not. Five panels in
## four rows now, and the height unit goes from 47.9 to 53.5 mm: every
## remaining panel gains about 12%. PANELS RELETTER b-f -> a-e; the Results
## citations move with them and the variance numbers become prose.
fig_omnibus <- (wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS18a)) +
                wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS18c)) +
                wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS18e)) +
                wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS18f)) +
                wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS18b)) +
                plot_layout(design = "AA\nBB\nCD\nEE",
                            heights = c(1.15, 1.25, 0.94, 1.15))) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = TAG_LEVELS) & theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1))
fig_omnibus
```

```{r figS4}
## S4B — specification sensitivity. Conditioned against unconditioned limma on one
## universe; which sets change sign; COG O in both.
pS4 <- panel({
  ## `sets$COG` raised "$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors": in this
  ## session `sets` is not the named list this panel assumed. Resolve the COG
  ## set list explicitly and say what was found if it cannot be.
  need("st0", "st1")
  cog <- if (exists("sets") && is.list(sets) && !is.null(sets$COG)) sets$COG
         else if (exists("SETS_COG")) SETS_COG
         else if (exists("SETS_P") && is.list(SETS_P))
           SETS_P[nchar(bare_nm <- sub("^[^:]+:", "", names(SETS_P))) <= 2]
         else NULL
  if (is.null(cog) || !length(cog))
    stop("no COG set list: `sets` is ",
         if (exists("sets")) paste(class(sets), collapse = "/") else "absent",
         "; tried sets$COG, SETS_COG and the short names of SETS_P")
  ## SEED THESE. fgseaMultilevel estimates its null by adaptive multilevel
  ## splitting, so NES carries Monte Carlo noise, and this document sets no
  ## global seed. The subtitle then takes a Spearman over only 17 points on an
  ## association near 0.1, where a couple of rank swaps move the value a long
  ## way. Four draws of the same quantity are on record -- 0.086 in the 22 Oct
  ## knit, against 0.164, 0.1667 and 0.185 written down earlier -- and the
  ## Methods and the Supplementary Notes quote one of the others. Nothing was
  ## wrong with any of them; they are the same lottery. The seed makes the panel
  ## reproducible so the text can be harmonised to a value that stays put.
  ##
  ## The sign-flip count is the stable quantity and is what the panel's claim
  ## actually rests on: 7 of 17 in both the 0.086 run and the 0.164 record. It
  ## is quoted at full precision; the correlation is now quoted to two decimals,
  ## because a third decimal on 17 points asserts a precision this estimate does
  ## not have.
  set.seed(71)
  f0 <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(cog, st0, minSize = 10, eps = 0) |> as_tibble()
  set.seed(71)
  f1 <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(cog, st1, minSize = 10, eps = 0) |> as_tibble()
  d <- inner_join(select(f1, pathway, cond = NES), select(f0, pathway, uncond = NES),
                  by = "pathway") |>
    mutate(flips = sign(cond) != sign(uncond))
  ggplot(d, aes(uncond, cond, colour = flips)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = 3, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = pathway), size = 2.2, max.overlaps = 20, seed = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL_RESP[["NR"]], `FALSE` = "grey55"),
                        labels = c("Sign stable", "Sign flips"), name = NULL) +
```

```{r figS8}
## S6B,C and S7A — metagenome depth and composition at three floors, both cohorts.
pS8a <- panel({
  need("depth")
  ggplot(depth, aes(reads)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey78", colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(1e6, 5e6), linetype = 2, linewidth = .3,

                         ifelse(z < 1e6, sprintf("%.1fM", z / 1e6),

    ## TITLE CORRECTED 10 Oct. It read "Coupling does not track sequencing
    ## depth", which is a claim this panel does not make: it is a histogram of
    ## read counts and plots no coupling at all. That sentence belongs to p3cd,
    ## which regresses coupling on evidence depth and was built but placed in
    ## no figure, so its claim had migrated here to the panel that merely
    ## mentions depth. p3cd is now S6D and makes the claim itself.
    labs(x = "Reads after kneaddata (log scale)", y = "Samples",
         title = "Sequencing depth across samples",
         subtitle = "dashed: the 1M and 5M floors")
}, "ED4B depth")

pS8b <- panel({
  need("comp_all")
  comp_all |>
    filter(phylum %in% c("Bacteroidota", "Firmicutes", "Actinomycetota", "Pseudomonadota")) |>
    ## RECOMPUTED 11 Oct 2026 from the profile, the kneaddata logs and the
    ## metadata: p = 0.039 / 0.053 / 0.050 for Bacteroidota at the none / 1M / 5M
    ## floors, 0.018 / 0.010 / 0.011 for Actinomycetota, 0.127 / 0.087 / 0.064 for
    ## Firmicutes and 0.237 / 0.316 / 0.272 for Pseudomonadota. So Bacteroidota
    ## crosses the rule TWICE, not three times, and Actinomycetota is the clade
    ## that never crosses -- the subtitle this panel carried said the opposite of
    ## both. Three points cannot cross a line three times.
    ## MetaPhlAn keeps Firmicutes where PAL_CLADE and every other panel in this
    ## file use Bacillota. A named `values` vector with no entry for a level
    ## gives that level NA, so the Bacillota line was dropped from this panel
    ## while the legend described four clades and three were drawn. Rename for
    ## display; the filter stays on the names the profile actually carries
    ## (vJan25 emits Actinomycetota, not Actinobacteria -- checked against the
    ## merged profile, which the note in analysis_v17 has the wrong way round).
    mutate(phylum = dplyr::recode(phylum, Firmicutes = "Bacillota")) |>
    mutate(floor = factor(floor, labels = c("None", "1M", "5M"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(floor, p, group = phylum, colour = phylum)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .05, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .4) + geom_point(size = PT_SMALL) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_CLADE, name = NULL) +
    ## 18 Oct: THE Y TITLE NAMES THE TEST. "Wilcoxon p, response" left the
    ## reader to guess the quantity; the test is on each phylum's percentage
    ## of the metagenome, which is also why a read floor is the x axis.
    ## SUBTITLE CORRECTED against comp_all: Bacteroidota is 0.0274 / 0.0378 /
    ## 0.0352, below the rule at every floor rather than on it, and Bacillota
    ## is the one that lands on it, at 0.0501 under the 5M floor.
    labs(x = "Depth floor",
         y = "Wilcoxon p, responders vs non-responders\n(phylum share of the metagenome)",
         title = "Stability across depth floors",
         subtitle = paste("no phylum changes side as the floor moves;",
                          "Bacteroidota stays below the 0.05 rule\nand Bacillota just above it"))
}, "ED4C floors")

pS8c <- panel({
  need("sh_comp")
  ## ONE NOMENCLATURE, AND ONLY PHYLA. MetaPhlAn emits the pre-2021 names, so
  ## this axis listed Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria and
  ## Verrucomicrobia beside Bacteroidota -- two naming schemes in one panel,
  ## while the Methods say exactly one name differs between the layers. pS8b
  ## already carries the Firmicutes recode; the rest are the same 2021
  ## renamings. And an "*_unclassified" bin is not a phylum: it was being
  ## listed as one on an axis whose label says phylum, so those rows are
  ## dropped and the panel says how many.
  PHY_NOW <- c(Firmicutes = "Bacillota", Actinobacteria = "Actinomycetota",
               Proteobacteria = "Pseudomonadota", Verrucomicrobia = "Verrucomicrobiota",
               Bacteroidetes = "Bacteroidota")
  sc <- sh_comp |> dplyr::mutate(phylum = dplyr::recode(as.character(phylum), !!!as.list(PHY_NOW)))
  drop_n <- sum(grepl("unclassified", sc$phylum, ignore.case = TRUE))
  sc <- sc[!grepl("unclassified", sc$phylum, ignore.case = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  sc$phylum <- gsub("_", " ", sc$phylum)
  sc |> slice_min(p_within_family, n = 8) |>
    ggplot(aes(p_within_family, reorder(phylum, -p_within_family))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = .05, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL) +
    labs(x = "P, within sample family", y = NULL,
         ## RETITLED 28 Sep 2026. "Nothing differs by response" now reads as a
         ## contradiction of the Results, which report that this cohort's
         ## metagenome separates on whole-profile composition (P = 0.032). It is
         ## not one: this is a per-phylum univariate test and that is a
         ## whole-profile test at species level, and diffuse structure with no
         ## single taxon responsible is precisely what an omnibus test detects
         ## and per-taxon tests do not. Said properly, this panel SUPPORTS the
         ## newer result rather than conflicting with it.
         title = "No single phylum differs by response in the second cohort",
         subtitle = if (drop_n)
           sprintf("names are current nomenclature; %d unclassified bin%s excluded, not being phyla",
                   drop_n, if (drop_n == 1L) "" else "s")
         else "names are current nomenclature")
}, "ED5A sheba")
```

```{r figS12}
## S13C — MS2-only sensitivity analysis, patient level, labeled post hoc.
pS12 <- panel({
  ## The MS2 archive was transferred to nulls_sheba_MS2, not sheba_ms2, and its
  ## set names may carry a source prefix. Find a directory by STRUCTURE — many
  ## .rds files plus an observed table — then confirm it is the MS2 arm by its
  ## observed value (-1.75; the superseded episode arm is -1.76, one hundredth
  ## away, so the directory name is what separates them).
  bare <- function(z) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(z))
  cand <- grep("ms2", list.dirs(paths$out_dir, recursive = TRUE), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  cand <- Filter(function(x) {
    ff <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$"); ob <- grepl("^observed", ff, ignore.case = TRUE)
    sum(!ob) >= 100 && any(ob) }, cand)
  if (!length(cand)) stop("no MS2-only draw directory found under ", paths$out_dir)
  d <- cand[1]
  ff <- list.files(d, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  isob <- grepl("^observed", basename(ff), ignore.case = TRUE)
  nl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ff[!isob], function(x) as.data.frame(readRDS(x))))
  ob <- as.data.frame(readRDS(ff[isob][1]))
  x <- nl$NES[bare(nl$pathway) == "O"]; o <- ob$NES[bare(ob$pathway) == "O"][1]
  ggplot(data.frame(NES = x), aes(NES)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey78", colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = o, colour = PAL_COHORT[["Sheba"]], linewidth = .6) +
```

```{r figS14}
  ggplot(d, aes(resp, qlogis(f), colour = resp)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = .5, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_jitter(width = .12, size = PT_JITTER) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_RESP, guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Logit ribosomal share within Blautia",
         title = "It does not replicate in Sheba",
         subtitle = stat_sub(sprintf("%d KOs against Pittsburgh’s %d; p = %.2f",
                                   ribo_blautia_ko[["sheba_KOs"]], ribo_blautia_ko[["pitt_KOs"]],
                                   ribo_blautia_ko[["p_two"]]), "Blautia KO counts"))
}, "ED7F sheba")
```

```{r figS15}
## S5A — metagenome against metaproteome at KEGG pathway level, with the
## attenuation caveat stated rather than implied.
pS15 <- panel({
  need("sysv")
  both <- sysv |> filter(!is.na(NES_mp), !is.na(NES_mg))
  ggplot(both, aes(NES_mp, NES_mg, colour = category)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = 3, colour = "grey65") +
    geom_point(size = PT_SMALL, alpha = .85) +
    labs(x = "Metaproteome NES", y = "Metagenome NES", colour = NULL,
         title = "The two layers' enrichment scores are unrelated",
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "Spearman %.3f, sign agreement %.0f%% over %d pathways",
           cor(both$NES_mp, both$NES_mg, method = "spearman"),
           100 * mean(sign(both$NES_mp) == sign(both$NES_mg)), nrow(both))) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)) +
    ## THREE ROWS, NOT ONE, and the panel is now FULL WIDTH (ED3e). Measured at
    ## 5.4 pt the nine keys span 91 mm in three rows: over an 88 mm half panel,
    ## which clipped the first column in ED4e, and comfortable across 180 mm.
    ## Five rows would be 68 mm if this ever goes back into a half cell.
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 5.4),
          legend.key.size = grid::unit(2.6, "mm"))
}, "ED3B systems")
```
