```{r supp-assemble}
## EXTENDED DATA, 12 Oct 2026. Thirteen supplementary figures became NINE
## Extended Data figures. Nature allows about ten Extended Data display items
## (figures and tables together) and forbids figures in Supplementary
## Information entirely, so every supplementary figure had to become Extended
## Data and the count had to come down. Four of the nine are merges; the rest
## are renumbered unchanged. The old numbering is preserved in the `was` field
## of each entry, because the manuscript's revision history and half the
## comments in this file still speak it.
##
## PANEL LETTERS MOVED, and the manuscript cites the new ones. ED7 is the one
## to watch: it carries nine panels drawn from three old figures, so a, b come
## from S8, c, d from S9 and e-i from S12.
##
## ED7 AND ED8 ARE BUILT FROM PANEL OBJECTS, NOT FROM fig_decomp. Nesting a
## patchwork that already carries plot_annotation() inside another one makes
## the inner figure a single tagged element: ED7 would be tagged a, b, c, d, e
## with e covering five panels. fig_decomp is still assembled and echoed in
## fig4-assemble for working renders; its five panels enter ED7 individually.
##
## Object names are frozen at the ORIGINAL numbering on purpose: pS16 is the
## object that was once Supplementary 16 and is now panel ED9d. Renaming them
## would break every comment and note that refers to them, so the name is an
## ID, not a position. This list is the only place that translates one to the
## other. NOTHING CHECKS IT: the "orphan audit" reads Sheba draw directories,
## not panel labels, so this block drifts silently. Edit it when you edit `supp`.
##
## WHICH OBJECT IS WHICH PANEL: THE LINT COMPUTES IT, THIS BLOCK NO LONGER
## CLAIMS TO. A hand-written object-to-position table stood here and went stale
## at every renumbering -- on 28 Oct its ED1 line cost two readers an hour each,
## and the rest of it still described the pre-19-Oct numbering (p1d, pS4 and
## pS7a were listed at ED4 while they assemble into ED6). It was marked "not to
## be trusted", which is not a state a deposited document should be left in, so
## it is gone. The LABEL LINT near the end of this file builds the same map from
## the live `order_keys`, `spec` and `supp` objects and prints every panel whose
## own label disagrees with where it actually lands; `supp` below is the
## authority and the lint is how to read it. Nothing here has to be maintained
## by hand.
##
## Two things that are NOT positions and are worth keeping:
##   pS1b is deleted -- see the note inside supp$ED1.
##   p5e is NOT in Extended Data: it is a panel of the coupling figure. The
##   object names are deliberately not positions (pS16 is the object that was
##   once Supplementary 16), so a name is an ID and never a location.
## Built but assembled nowhere: pS6a (superseded by Figure 3C), declared in the
## orphan audit's list of deliberate orphans below.
## The cohort table that used to be p1c is not built here: it is now main
## Table 1 (B40_table1.R), which is what its content always was. The frozen KO
## sets are Supplementary Table 1 (B41_supp_tables.R) and stay in the SI, the
## only table left there.
supp <- list(
  ## p1b, the plex-by-channel layout, was Figure 1c until the external
  ## schematic took the top of that figure. It belongs here: ED Fig. 1 is the
  ## measurement-and-provenance figure, and which channel carried which
  ## response group is a property of the run, not a result. It shares row
  ## three with pS10 rather than adding a fourth row, which would have put
  ## four rows in the 240 mm cap and squeezed a to d.
  ## pS1b DELETED (reviewer 5 §4). A histogram of per-channel medians at 1e-15
  ## demonstrates that median-centring ran; it is a unit test, not a result, and
  ## it belongs in Methods as a sentence. Five panels in three rows, with pS10
  ## full width on the last because it is the provenance table and reads wide.
  ED1 = list(was = "S1",
             ## 16 Oct: p1bs ARRIVES AS e, the Sheba plex layout, and pS10
             ## moves to f. It fills the half of row three that held a spacer,
             ## so the figure stays at three rows and no panel before e changes
             ## its letter. pS10 at half width was already the decision (the
             ## note it carries) -- it now has a neighbour instead of a gap.
             ## FLAT DESIGN, NOT NESTED ROWS. `(a|b)/(c|d)` lays each row out
             ## on its own, so column two begins wherever that row's left panel
             ## happens to end and the panel LETTERS of b, d, f land at
             ## different x. One design grid gives them one column. See the
             ## note on ED8 for the measurement.
             ## 16 Oct, SECOND CHANGE: p1a AND p1a_pre ARRIVE AS g AND h, from
             ## the deleted Figure 1. APPENDED, so a-f keep their letters and
             ## the ED1 citations written earlier today do not move. They are
             ## the only data panels Figure 1 had and they belong here: ED1 is
             ## the measurement-and-provenance figure and when each cohort was
             ## sampled is a property of the study, not a result.
             ## They lose the per-panel axis-font overrides Figure 1 gave them
             ## (`.fig1_tag`, deleted with the schematic machinery) -- those
             ## existed because c and d were narrow panels in a 136 mm figure.
             ## Here they are half-width cells like every other ED1 panel and
             ## take the journal theme through wrap_titles() like the rest.
             ## 19 Oct: SAMPLING FIRST, because that is where the text sends
             ## the reader first -- ED1a and ED1b are the two timelines, cited
             ## in the cohort sentence, and the measurement and provenance
             ## panels follow as c-h. Every cell is half width, so the grid is
             ## unchanged and only the order and the letters move.
             p = wrap_titles(p1a)  + wrap_titles(p1a_pre) +
                 wrap_titles(pS1a) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS1c)) +
                 wrap_titles(pS2)  + wrap_titles(p1b)  +
                 wrap_titles(p1bs) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS10)) +
                 plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD\nEF\nGH"),
             ## 200 -> 240: three rows become four. 240 is JS$h_max_supp for
             ## Nature and there is no headroom left in this figure either.
             w = 180, h = 240),                     # measurement, provenance and sampling
  ## 28 Oct: pS18d (the cohort-against-response partition, B37) LEFT THIS
  ## FIGURE -- see the note on fig_omnibus. What follows described the layout
  ## it had when that panel was still here. It is AT the cap
  ## rather than over it: fig_dims had been warning on 250 against Nature's 240
  ## for Extended Data for several drafts and the warning was being read and
  ## ignored. Three rows in 240 mm is 80 mm each, which is what the other
  ## multi-row Extended Data figures already use.
  ED2 = list(was = "S2", p = fig_omnibus,           w = 180, h = 240),
  ## p2h was built and placed in no figure for several drafts. It belongs here
  ## and nowhere else: ED3 is where the coupling advantage is bounded, and p2h
  ## is the control that rules out the obvious objection to that bound -- that
  ## the coupling is low because the metagenome is shallow. Full width on its
  ## own row because it carries a colour bar.
  ## p5e MOVED TO FIGURE 2 (reviewer 5 §4): it is the dynamic-range answer and
  ## was invisible to anyone who did not read Extended Data. What remains is the
  ## bound and the control that rules out the obvious objection to it.
  ## ONE ROW OF TWO, not two stacked full-width rows. ED3 held three panels
  ## until p5e went to Figure 2; the two that remain then had the whole 180 mm
  ## each, which is the same fault as ED6c and ED9e -- a panel given more width
  ## than its content has. Side by side they are 88 mm each, and the figure
  ## loses 40 mm of height it was not using.
  ## 14 Oct: p2b, p2c AND p2g ARRIVE FROM FIGURE 2, which is now a modest
  ## three-panel item -- see the note in assemble-mains for why. Five panels in
  ## three rows, and the tag order IS the legend order: the bound and its depth
  ## control first, then the three that left Figure 2 in the order Figure 2 had
  ## them, so ED3c-e in the text are p2b, p2c, p2g. patchwork tags in the order
  ## plots are added and plot_spacer() takes no tag, so e is p2g, not the gap.
  ## p2g KEEPS ITS HALF WIDTH beside a spacer rather than taking the full 180
  ## mm. It is a two-variable scatter; the ED1e note applies -- width spent on
  ## fill, not on information -- and it is the width the panel was drawn at.
  ED3 = list(was = "S3",
             ## e IS WRAPPED, AND THAT IS THE Y-AXIS TITLE FIX. patchwork
             ## aligns the axis-text block across a whole column, so e's two
             ## category labels -- "gene-family protein output" starts at
             ## x = 16.8 pt where a's "1.00" starts at 75.8 -- set the block
             ## for a and c as well and pushed THEIR titles out to the far
             ## left: measured 21.4 mm on a and 22.6 mm on c in the 15 Oct
             ## render, against the 1-2 mm that is normal in this set.
             ## wrap_elements() takes e out of that alignment and leaves it
             ## drawn exactly as before; a and c then size the column from
             ## their own four-character ticks. Nothing else was available:
             ## there is no axis.title.y anywhere in this file to adjust, the
             ## labels are the panel's content, and free() is patchwork >= 1.2
             ## with a `type` argument this file cannot assume.
             ## 18 Oct: p2c DROPPED, pS15 ARRIVES AS e AT FULL WIDTH.
             ## p2c showed set-level capacity tracking for the chaperone and
             ## ribosomal sets -- neither of which the reader has met by ED3,
             ## which is still establishing the coupling limit. pS15 is the
             ## pathway-level enrichment null and belongs with the rest of the
             ## coupling evidence rather than in ED4 with the permutation
             ## machinery. FULL WIDTH IS THE LEGEND FIX: its nine category keys
             ## at nrow = 3 measure 91 mm, against an 88 mm half panel, which
             ## is why the first column was clipped in ED4e. At 180 mm it fits
             ## with room to spare and the guide needs no change.
             ## 19 Oct: ORDER FOLLOWS THE CITATIONS. The text reaches the
             ## 200 most variable families first, then the enrichment-score
             ## comparison, then the bound and its depth control, and the
             ## positive control last. pS15 LOSES ITS FULL-WIDTH ROW: it is now
             ## b and shares row one, and p2g keeps the half width beside a
             ## spacer that the note above argues for. Three rows as before.
             ## 28 Oct: c AND d SWAPPED to follow the Results, which now reach
             ## the depth control first ("deeper sequencing would not raise it")
             ## and the detection curve second. The panels are unchanged; only
             ## which one is c. d's legend sentence that refers back to "the
             ## limit in c" has to become "the limit in d".
             p = wrap_titles(p2b) + wrap_titles(pS15) +
                 wrap_titles(p2h) + wrap_titles(p5f) +
                 wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p2g)) +
                 plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD\nE#"),
             ## 100 -> 230: one row of two becomes three. 77 mm a row is what
             ## p2b, p2c and p2g had in Figure 2, so they render as drawn, and
             ## p5f and p2h drop from a generous 100 to the same 77. The cap is
             ## JS$h_max_supp = 240; fig_dims() warns if this goes over it.
             w = 180, h = 230),
  ## 19 Oct: WAS ED5. Renumbered so the Extended Data figures are
  ## numbered in the order the text first cites them; the panels and the
  ## layout below are unchanged.
  ## p3cd was the other long-standing orphan. The clade supports say what the
  ## gap survives; p3cd says what it is NOT -- evidence depth -- and that
  ## belongs beside them rather than in the main clade figure, where the
  ## re-search makes the stronger statement. It fills the empty half of row two.
  ED4 = list(was = "S6",
             ## 17 Oct: FLAT DESIGN. d's letter sat 3 mm right of b's, because
             ## `(a|b)/(c|d)` sizes each row's second column against whatever
             ## that row's first column spent. One grid, one column.
             p = wrap_titles(pS6b) + wrap_titles(pS8a) +
                 wrap_titles(pS8b) + wrap_titles(p3cd) +
                 plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD"),
             w = 180, h = 150),                     # what the clade result is not
  ## 19 Oct: WAS ED6. Renumbered so the Extended Data figures are
  ## numbered in the order the text first cites them; the panels and the
  ## layout below are unchanged.
  ## c IS HALF WIDTH, NOT FULL. b and c are the same two-group comparison in the
  ## two layers -- Bacteroidota share of the proteome and of the metagenome --
  ## and c had the whole 180 mm to itself for two boxes. At that width the boxes
  ## read as the result and the points as decoration, which is backwards, and
  ## the panel no longer matched b beside it. A spacer holds the other half, so
  ## b and c are drawn at one width and can be compared directly. Panel letters
  ## are unchanged (a, b, c), so the caption needs no edit.
  ED5 = list(was = "S7",
             ## b AND c SIDE BY SIDE. They are the two halves of one
             ## comparison -- the proteomes agree where the metagenomes do not
             ## -- and the old layout put them on different rows in different
             ## columns with an empty quadrant between, so the comparison the
             ## panels exist to make could not be made by eye. a takes the full
             ## width it already had; the letters are unchanged.
             p = wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS8c)) /
                 (wrap_titles(pS13a) | wrap_titles(pS13b)),
             w = 180, h = 150),                     # the two cohorts, layer by layer
  ## 19 Oct: WAS ED4. Renumbered so the Extended Data figures are
  ## numbered in the order the text first cites them; the panels and the
  ## layout below are unchanged.
  ## MERGE S4 + S5. p1d moved here from Figure 1: it shows the empirical null
  ## against the parametric one, which is the first thing this figure's subject
  ## needs to establish, and it was cited 55% of the way through Results rather
  ## than at the start where Figure 1 implied. pS15 was Supplementary 5 on its
  ## own -- a single panel is not a figure under a ten-item cap -- and is now
  ## panel e, on its own full-width row because it is a count distribution and
  ## reads better wide than squeezed into a half.
  ## pS7b DELETED and p3mx ARRIVES in its slot (reviewer 5 §4). pS7b plotted sd
  ## against range at rho = 0.986 -- near-tautological, and what it was there to
  ## say is already in pS7a. p3mx, the distribution of the smallest per-set p
  ## across the 565-set family, is a statement about how the correction behaves,
  ## which is this figure's subject and not Figure 4's.
  ED6 = list(was = "S4+S5",
             ## e IS HALF WIDTH. It is a scatter of 68 points with an
             ## identity line; across the full 180 mm the cloud stretched
             ## and the identity line, which is the whole reading, flattened
             ## towards horizontal. The empty half of row three holds it to
             ## the width of the panels above it.
             ## FLAT DESIGN: b sat at x = 231.0 pt and d at 263.4, an 11.4 mm
             ## stagger in the panel letters, because nested rows split their
             ## own width. "#" is the empty half.
             ## 18 Oct: pS15 MOVED TO ED3e. Four panels in two rows, so the
             ## height comes back from 230 to 155.
             p = wrap_titles(p1d)  + wrap_titles(pS4)  +
                 wrap_titles(pS7a) + wrap_titles(p3mx) +
                 plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD"),
             w = 180, h = 155),                     # null, statistic, feature counts
  ## 19 Oct: WAS ED8. Renumbered so the Extended Data figures are
  ## numbered in the order the text first cites them; the panels and the
  ## layout below are unchanged.
  ## MERGE S10 + S11. p3f and p3g are the per-sample side of the response
  ## result -- the shares themselves and the flat chaperone-to-ribosomal ratio
  ## the Discussion calls what separates the two readings -- and pS14a,b are the
  ## ribosomal residual, which is the same observation failing to replicate.
  ## Each was a single row of two; together they are a 2 x 2.
  ## p3f MOVED TO FIGURE 4 and p2d ARRIVES in its slot (reviewer 5 §4). p2d is
  ## the response coefficient on gene capacity for the two classes, which sits
  ## with the other response coefficients here rather than in Figure 2, where it
  ## was two points and less than a sentence of text.
  ## 14 Oct: p3f COMES BACK, and p4a ARRIVES, from Figure 4, which was carrying
  ## seven panels. Both belong to this figure's subject -- the response
  ## difference at sample level -- and p3f was here before reviewer 5 moved it
  ## out. APPENDED AS A THIRD ROW rather than placed first: a-d keep their
  ## letters, so the four citations the text already makes to ED8a-d do not
  ## move, and the two arrivals are e and f.
  ED7 = list(was = "S10+S11",
             ## a AND g ARE WRAPPED, AND THAT IS THE Y-AXIS TITLE FIX.
             ## MEASURED on the 15 Oct render: every tick-label block in
             ## column one ends at x = 132.9 pt, because patchwork aligns the
             ## axis text across the whole column. g's species labels start at
             ## 16.8 ("Aggregate, median across species") and a's at 101.6
             ## ("chaperones"), so the block is 116 pt wide -- and e, whose own
             ## ticks are "30 20 10", had its title stranded at x = 8.3 with
             ## 39.2 mm of white between the title and the axis.
             ## BOTH had to come out: wrapping g alone leaves a driving the
             ## column and the gap at 8.8 mm. Wrapping a costs nothing it was
             ## using -- it has no y-axis title, and c beside it has been a
             ## wrapped element all along, so column one was never flush.
             ## FLAT DESIGN for the panel letters: b, d, f sat at 285.9, 305.5
             ## and 296.6 pt, a 6.9 mm stagger, because `(a|b)/(c|d)` lays out
             ## each row against its own width. One grid, one column.
             ## 17 Oct, MEASURED AND LEFT ALONE. The rendered letters are
             ## a, c, e at x = 6.3 pt and b, d at 250.8 with f at 251.9 -- a
             ## 1.1 pt (0.4 mm) spread in column two and none in column one.
             ## The flat design below is already doing its job; wrapping the
             ## two bare panels to match the other four would change how the
             ## columns divide the width for no alignment gain.
             ## 19 Oct: ORDER FOLLOWS THE CITATIONS -- the two shares and
             ## their ratio first, then the per-sample share, then gene
             ## capacity, the adjustment ladder, and the ribosomal residual.
             ## Every cell is half width, so the grid does not change.
             p = wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p3g)) + wrap_titles(p3f) +
                 wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p2d)) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p4a)) +
                 wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS14a)) + wrap_titles(pS14b) +
                 plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD\nEF"),
             ## 215 -> 230: two rows become three. 230 is what ED7 already
             ## uses and is at or under h_max_supp in every JSTYLE variant;
             ## 240 is the cap in only one of them.
             ## 17 Oct, 240 -> 230: g IS GONE. The PTR analysis was cut from
             ## the paper, so the fourth full-width row goes with it and the
             ## figure returns to the three-row height it had before 15 Oct.
             ## a-f keep their letters, so no citation moves.
             w = 180, h = 230),                     # sample level, ribosomal residual
  ## 19 Oct: WAS ED7. Renumbered so the Extended Data figures are
  ## numbered in the order the text first cites them; the panels and the
  ## layout below are unchanged.
  ## MERGE S8 + S9 + S12, the three "what could explain it away" figures: the
  ## host inflammatory panel, treatment exposure, and the covariate adjustment
  ## ladder. Nine panels in THREE ROWS OF THREE. Two columns would need five
  ## rows, which at the row heights these panels were drawn for comes to about
  ## 400 mm against a 240 mm cap, so three across is not a preference. Each
  ## panel gets 60 mm; the axis text is already sized from JS and does not need
  ## a separate rule here.
  ## p4a MOVED TO FIGURE 4 (reviewer 5 §4): the adjustment ladder is
  ## load-bearing for the chaperone claim and belonged in a main figure. Eight
  ## panels now, so row two carries two and the other rows three.
  ED8 = list(was = "S8+S9+S12",
             ## 17 Oct: FLAT DESIGN, AND ROW THREE RE-PROPORTIONED.
             ## Rows one and two carry two panels, row three carries three, so
             ## the grid is twelve columns wide and each row spends them.
             ## e TAKES HALF THE ROW (6/12, 90 mm against the 60 mm it had).
             ## It is 22 genus labels and a pointrange for each; at a third of
             ## the width the labels took more of the cell than the intervals.
             ## f AND g SPLIT THE OTHER HALF (3/12 each). f is two rows and a
             ## band and never needed 60 mm; g is a tight cluster whose axis
             ## runs out to zero by design (see the note in p2e), so most of
             ## its width was empty whatever it was given.
             ## THE LETTERS: e starts where a and c start, and f starts where
             ## b and d start. Only g is unaligned, which is the best a 2-2-3
             ## figure can do.
             ## 19 Oct: ORDER FOLLOWS THE CITATIONS -- the abundance-matched
             ## specificity check first, then exposure, plex structure, the
             ## covariate correlation, host protein, within-genus, and
             ## leave-one-genus-out. ROW THREE IS NOW THREE EQUAL THIRDS: the
             ## two panels that were 90 mm there are 60 mm, and p2e rises from
             ## 45 mm to 60. The figure stays at three rows and 230 mm.
             p = wrap_titles(p4e) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS11b)) +
                 wrap_titles(pS3b) + wrap_titles(p4b) +
                 wrap_titles(pS3a) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p4d)) +
                 wrap_titles(p2e) +
                 plot_layout(design = paste("AAAAAABBBBBB",
                                            "CCCCCCDDDDDD",
                                            "EEEEFFFFGGGG", sep = "\n")),
             w = 180, h = 230),                     # host protein, exposure, the ladder
  ## p5rank ARRIVES from Figure 5b (reviewer 5 §4). The rank statement is still
  ## worth having as a second view of the same agreement -- it is the weaker of
  ## the two and no longer the one the main text rests on.
  ## e IS HALF WIDTH. It is a slopegraph with two x-positions, and across the
  ## full 180 mm the two columns sat at the extreme edges with the set labels
  ## stranded in the middle distance -- the same fault as ED6c, a panel with few
  ## categories given the whole page. Half width puts the two cohorts close
  ## enough that the slopes read as slopes. Panel letters are unchanged.
  ED9 = list(was = "S13",
             ## f FILLS THE SPACER. The slot was empty because e is half
             ## width; ED9F is the joint-position panel, which belongs
             ## beside the rank view -- both are the ensemble read two ways.
             ## FLAT DESIGN. This figure had the worst panel-letter stagger in
             ## the set: b at 286.9 pt, d at 262.1, f at 229.9 -- 20.1 mm
             ## between the first and the last. a carries a right-hand legend
             ## and e a bottom one, and a nested row sizes its second column
             ## against whatever its first column spends, legend included.
             ## 19 Oct: ORDER FOLLOWS THE CITATIONS -- the Sheba running
             ## enrichment first, then power, the MS2-only check, and the set
             ## membership panel fourth. Half-width cells throughout, so the
             ## grid is unchanged.
             p = wrap_titles(pS16)   + wrap_titles(pS9)  +
                 wrap_titles(pS12)   + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(pS5)) +
                 wrap_titles(p5rank) + wrap_elements(full = wrap_titles(p5joint)) +
                 ## 19 Oct: ROW THREE CARRIES THE TWO PANELS THAT NEED HEIGHT.
                 ## f lists 24 categories and e is a slopegraph; rows one and two
                 ## hold histograms and a running score, which do not. Weighted
                 ## 0.9 / 1.0 / 1.25, row three goes from 78 mm to about 93 and
                 ## the other two give up 11 mm and 3.
                 plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD\nEF",
                             heights = c(0.9, 1.0, 1.25)),
             w = 180, h = 235))                     # what the second cohort can resolve

## Same hazard as the main loop: a figure dropped from the list would otherwise
## survive on disk and pass the count check below. The OLD FigureS*.pdf names
## are cleared too -- thirteen of them are sitting in FIG_DIR from the last
## render and nothing else would ever remove them, so a submission assembled
## from this directory would carry both numbering schemes.
type_report()
old_s <- list.files(FIG_DIR, "^(FigureS[0-9]+|ExtendedDataFig[0-9]+)\\.(pdf|png)$",
                    full.names = TRUE)
if (length(old_s)) {
  cat("clearing", length(old_s), "figure file(s) from a previous run\n")
  unlink(old_s)
}

for (nm in names(supp)) {
  sp  <- supp[[nm]]
  num <- sub("^ED", "", nm)
  lbl <- sprintf("ExtendedDataFig%s", num)
  f   <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(lbl, ".pdf"))
  if (file.exists(f)) unlink(f)
  ## NO SUPPLEMENTARY FIGURE HAD PANEL LETTERS, and this line is why. A
  ## patchwork object's class is c("patchwork", "gg", "ggplot"), so
  ## inherits(x, "ggplot") is TRUE for a composed figure as well as a plain
  ## one: every multi-panel figure took the "leave it alone" branch and
  ## plot_annotation() was never reached. The legends have been citing panels
  ## a-e against figures that showed none. Test for the composed class, which
  ## is the thing that actually distinguishes the two cases.
  pp <- if (inherits(sp$p, "patchwork"))
          sp$p + plot_annotation(tag_levels = TAG_LEVELS) & theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1))
        else sp$p
  dm <- fig_dims(sp$w, sp$h, nm, supp = TRUE)
  ggsave(f, pp, width = dm$w, height = dm$h, units = "mm", device = PDF_DEV)
  if (!file.exists(f) || file.size(f) < 1000)
    stop(lbl, " did not write to ", f, call. = FALSE)
  fix_hyphen_glyph(f, lbl)
  embed_fonts_checked(f, lbl)
  pg <- save_png(pp, f, dm$w, dm$h, lbl)
  cat(sprintf("%-20s (%3g x %3g mm)  was %-9s %5.0f kB pdf   %d x %d px  %5.0f kB png\n",
              lbl, dm$w, dm$h, sp$was, file.size(f) / 1024,
              pg[["w"]], pg[["h"]], pg[["kb"]]))
}
wrote_s <- list.files(FIG_DIR, "^ExtendedDataFig[0-9]+\\.pdf$")
cat("\nExtended Data figures written:", length(wrote_s), "of", length(supp), "\n")
## PNG PARITY. Every figure PDF in this directory must have a PNG twin at
## the same stem. Without this the manuscript can be assembled from a
## mixture of resolutions and nothing says which figure came from where --
## which is how four 80 dpi figures reached collaborators.
.pdfs <- sub("\\.pdf$", "", list.files(FIG_DIR, "^(Figure[0-9]+|ExtendedDataFig[0-9]+)\\.pdf$"))
.pngs <- sub("\\.png$", "", list.files(FIG_DIR, "^(Figure[0-9]+|ExtendedDataFig[0-9]+)\\.png$"))
if (length(setdiff(.pdfs, .pngs)))
  stop("no PNG was written for: ", paste(setdiff(.pdfs, .pngs), collapse = ", "),
       call. = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("PNG twins: %d of %d, %s at %d dpi\n", length(.pngs), length(.pdfs),
            attr(PNG_DEV, "backend"), PNG_DPI))
rm(.pdfs, .pngs)
## Called here, after BOTH loops, so it sees the complete set.
check_embedding()
panel_failures()
if (length(wrote_s) != length(supp))
  stop(sprintf("expected %d Extended Data figures, found %d: %s", length(supp),
               length(wrote_s), paste(wrote_s, collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)

## PANEL-COUNT LINT. The manuscript's Extended Data legends declare how many
## panels each figure has, and a merge is exactly the edit that silently drops
## one. Counted from this list's own source rather than from the objects,
## for the reason the orphan audit gives: patchwork rebuilds its operands.
## 16 Oct: FOUR OF THESE NINE WERE WRONG, and this is the lint that exists to
## catch exactly that. Counted off the assemblies above, panel by panel:
##   ED1 5 -> 6 (p1bs arrives as e), ED3 3 -> 5 (p2b, p2c, p2g came from
##   Figure 2 on 14 Oct), ED7 9 -> 7 (p4a left for Figure 4; the entry's own
##   comment says "Eight panels now" and that was wrong too), ED9 4 -> 6
##   (p5rank and p5joint). The declared counts had not been updated with the
##   moves, so the lint compared the legends against a stale list and passed.
##   The Extended Data LEGENDS still have to be checked against these.
ED_PANELS <- c(ED1 = 8, ED2 = 5, ED3 = 5, ED4 = 4, ED5 = 3,
               ED6 = 4, ED7 = 6, ED8 = 7, ED9 = 6)
## 28 Oct: ED2 stays 5 -- the pathway scan arrived and the variance partition
## left -- and ED5 goes 4 -> 3. ED5 has been assembling three panels since the
## 19 Oct renumbering while this said four, so the one check meant to catch a
## panel-count drift was itself carrying one.
##
## 9 Nov: FOUR MORE WERE WRONG, which is this list's third drift and the reason
## it should not be maintained by hand. Counted off the assemblies in `supp`,
## where the panel list and the plot_layout design string agree with each other
## and both disagreed with the number here:
##   ED4 5 -> 4  pS6b, pS8a, pS8b, p3cd on "AB\nCD"
##   ED6 3 -> 4  p1d, pS4, pS7a, p3mx on "AB\nCD"
##   ED7 7 -> 6  p3g, p3f, p2d, p4a, pS14a, pS14b on "AB\nCD\nEF" -- the 16 Oct
##               entry above set 7 on the reading that p4a had left for Figure 4;
##               it is back in this assembly
##   ED8 6 -> 7  p4e, pS11b, pS3b, p4b, pS3a, p4d, p2e on a seven-cell design
## ED1, ED2 (via fig_omnibus), ED3, ED5 and ED9 were checked the same way and
## were already right. THE EXTENDED DATA LEGENDS IN THE MANUSCRIPT DECLARE THESE
## COUNTS TOO, and the four above have to be checked there before submission.
if (!identical(sort(names(ED_PANELS)), sort(names(supp))))
  warning("ED_PANELS and supp disagree on which figures exist", call. = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("panels per figure: %s\n",
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", names(ED_PANELS), ED_PANELS), collapse = " ")))
```

```{r orphan-audit}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ORPHAN AUDIT — which built panels are assembled into no figure?
##
## This is the defect this script has shipped twice. p3f and p3g were built and
## placed nowhere for several drafts; pS6a went the same way when S6 was
## regrouped, even though that chunk's own header promises it. Nothing
## downstream notices, because the figure-count checks only ever see what IS in
## the lists -- a panel that fell out of a list is invisible to them.
##
## It is a lint on this file's own source, not runtime introspection: wrap_titles
## returns a modified copy and patchwork rebuilds its operands, so an attribute
## stamped on a panel cannot be followed reliably through assembly. Reading the
## source is the thing that actually works.
##
## Precision comes from intersecting against the set of panel() assignments, so
## stray tokens in comments and patchwork's own functions (plot_layout,
## plot_spacer) cannot be mistaken for panels.
##
## It never stops the knit. An orphan may be deliberate; declare those below.
DELIBERATE_ORPHANS <- c(
  "p2c",     # set-level capacity tracking for the chaperone and ribosomal
             # sets; dropped from ED3 on 18 Oct because neither set has been
             # introduced at that point in the Results
  "p2f",     # superseded by Figure 3A, kept standalone in case a reviewer asks
  "p3e",     # chaperone evidence by phylum in raw counts; Figure 3C carries the
             # same comparison as shares (see fig3EF)
  "pS6a",    # chaperone density 11-fold apart between clades; superseded by
             # Figure 3C, which draws it as part of the clade result
  "pS18d"    # cohort-against-response variance partition; out of ED2 on
             # 28 Oct. Two bars and a prevalence sweep, both deposited in
             # Supplementary Table 5, so the Results state the numbers and
             # cite the table. Kept built in case a reviewer asks for it.
)
## p2h and p3cd were the last two of these, carrying comments that said they
## moved to Supplementary while appearing in no supplementary figure. Both are
## now placed -- p2h as ED3c, p3cd as ED5d -- so this list is empty of accidents
## and holds only deliberate orphans. Keep it that way: a panel whose comment
## says where it goes is not the same as a panel that goes there.

invisible(tryCatch({
  src_path <- tryCatch(knitr::current_input(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(src_path) || !file.exists(src_path)) src_path <- "figures_v2.Rmd"
  if (!file.exists(src_path)) {
    cat("orphan audit skipped: cannot locate this file's source\n")
  } else {
    src <- readLines(src_path, warn = FALSE)

    ## Blank every comment, whole-line and trailing alike, so prose cannot
    ## contribute tokens -- "## p3e is superseded" must not count as placing
    ## p3e. Blanking rather than DELETING keeps indices aligned with src, which
    ## is what makes the reported line numbers true.
    bare <- sub("#.*$", "", src)
    ## Whether a line was blank BEFORE comments were stripped. The block
    ## collector below ends a block on a blank line, and the supp list has ##
    ## comment lines between its entries; testing the stripped text would end
    ## that block at the first one and report everything after it as an orphan.
    was_blank <- !nzchar(trimws(src))

    ## 1. every panel this script BUILDS, by object name. The `p` prefix in
    ##    the pattern is load-bearing, not cosmetic: K_all is also wrapped in
    ##    panel(), but only to borrow its error trapping -- it is a matrix other
    ##    panels read, never a figure panel, and must not be reported as an
    ##    orphan. Any genuine panel must therefore be named p-something.
    built <- unique(sub("^\\s*(p[A-Za-z0-9_]*)\\s*<-\\s*panel\\(.*$", "\\1",
                        grep("^\\s*p[A-Za-z0-9_]*\\s*<-\\s*panel\\(", bare, value = TRUE)))

    ## 2. every panel PLACED into a figure. Placement happens in exactly two
    ##    places: a `fig_* <-` assembly and the `supp <- list(` block. Collect
    ##    them line-wise, ending a block at a blank line or a chunk fence,
    ##    rather than with a multi-line regex that is easy to get subtly wrong.
    ##    A bare `fig_design` echo line inside a block is harmless -- it carries
    ##    no panel tokens.
    blocks <- character(0); inb <- FALSE
    for (i in seq_along(bare)) {
      if (grepl("^fig_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\\s*<-", bare[i]) ||
          grepl("^supp\\s*<-\\s*list\\(", bare[i])) inb <- TRUE
      if (inb) {
        if (was_blank[i] || grepl("^```", src[i])) { inb <- FALSE; next }
        blocks <- c(blocks, bare[i])
      }
    }
    toks   <- unlist(regmatches(blocks, gregexpr("\\bp[A-Za-z0-9_]*\\b", blocks)))
    placed <- intersect(unique(toks), built)

    orphans <- setdiff(built, placed)
    undecl  <- setdiff(orphans, DELIBERATE_ORPHANS)
    stale   <- setdiff(DELIBERATE_ORPHANS, orphans)

    cat(sprintf("\norphan audit: %d panels built by panel(), %d placed in a figure\n",
                length(built), length(placed)))
    if (!length(orphans)) {
      cat("  every built panel is assembled into a figure\n")
    } else {
      for (o in orphans) {
        ln  <- grep(sprintf("^\\s*%s\\s*<-\\s*panel\\(", o), bare)[1]
        lab <- sub('^.*\\}\\s*,\\s*"([^"]+)"\\s*\\).*$', "\\1",
                   grep('\\}\\s*,\\s*"', src[seq(ln, min(ln + 120L, length(src)))],
                        value = TRUE)[1])
        cat(sprintf("  %-7s line %5d  %-26s %s\n", o, ln,
                    if (is.na(lab)) "" else lab,
                    if (o %in% DELIBERATE_ORPHANS) "(deliberate)" else "<<< PLACED NOWHERE"))
      }
    }
    if (length(undecl))
      warning(sprintf("built but placed in no figure: %s. Either assemble them or add them to DELIBERATE_ORPHANS.",
                      paste(undecl, collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)
    if (length(stale))
      cat(sprintf("  note: %s listed in DELIBERATE_ORPHANS but now placed; drop from that list\n",
                  paste(stale, collapse = ", ")))

    ## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    ## LABEL LINT. Each panel's second argument to panel() opens with the
    ## position it believes it occupies ("3A running score"), and that string is
    ## what a reader sees inside the grey box when the panel fails. It is a
    ## position written down in a second place, so reordering the paper silently
    ## falsified it: at the 8 Oct audit 52 of 61 placed panels named the wrong
    ## figure, including one that named a figure in a stop() message. Recompute
    ## the true position from the assembly and compare.
    ##
    ## Object names are deliberately NOT positions (pS16 is panel S13D), so this
    ## checks the LABEL only. See the map in supp-assemble.
    fig_panels <- list(); inb2 <- FALSE; curf <- NULL
    for (i in seq_along(bare)) {
      mf <- regmatches(bare[i], regexpr("^fig_[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?=\\s*<-)", bare[i], perl = TRUE))
      if (length(mf)) { curf <- mf; fig_panels[[curf]] <- character(0); inb2 <- TRUE }
      if (inb2 && !is.null(curf)) {
        if (was_blank[i] || grepl("^```", src[i])) { inb2 <- FALSE; curf <- NULL; next }
        tk <- unlist(regmatches(bare[i], gregexpr("\\bp[A-Za-z0-9_]*\\b", bare[i])))
        fig_panels[[curf]] <- unique(c(fig_panels[[curf]], intersect(tk, built)))
      }
    }
    ## main figures: order_keys and spec are live, so the numbering is read from
    ## the same objects the export loop uses rather than guessed.
    truth <- character(0)
    for (i in seq_along(order_keys)) {
      ps <- fig_panels[[spec[[order_keys[i]]]$obj]]
      ## A single-panel figure is exported as a bare ggplot, which the loop
      ## never passes through plot_annotation, so no tag letter is drawn on it
      ## and its label must not claim one.
      if (length(ps)) truth[ps] <- paste0(i, if (length(ps) > 1) LETTERS[seq_along(ps)] else "")
    }
    ## supplementary: entry order from source; an entry built from a fig_* object
    ## inherits that assembly's panel order.
    sl <- grep("^supp\\s*<-\\s*list\\(", bare)[1]
    if (!is.na(sl)) {
      cur <- NULL
      for (i in seq(sl, length(bare))) {
        if (was_blank[i] || grepl("^```", src[i])) break
        ## WAS "S[0-9]+(?=\\s*=)", which matched the OLD `S1 = list(` keys. The
        ## list has used `ED1 = list(` since the Extended Data renaming, so this
        ## matched nothing and the lint silently checked zero supplementary
        ## panels -- every Extended Data legend drifted unseen. Accept both.
        ms <- regmatches(bare[i], regexpr("(ED|S)[0-9]+(?=\\s*=)", bare[i], perl = TRUE))
        if (length(ms)) { cur <- ms; acc <- character(0) }
        if (!is.null(cur)) {
          tk <- unlist(regmatches(bare[i], gregexpr("\\bp[A-Za-z0-9_]*\\b", bare[i])))
          inh <- unlist(regmatches(bare[i], gregexpr("\\bfig_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\\b", bare[i])))
          if (length(inh)) tk <- fig_panels[[inh[1]]]
          acc <- unique(c(acc, intersect(tk, built)))
          if (length(acc))
            truth[acc] <- paste0(cur, if (length(acc) > 1) LETTERS[seq_along(acc)] else "")
        }
      }
    }
    ## compare each label's leading token with the truth
    bad <- character(0)
    for (o in names(truth)) {
      dl <- grep(sprintf("^\\s*%s\\s*<-\\s*panel\\(", o), bare)[1]
      if (is.na(dl)) next
      lb <- grep('\\}\\s*,\\s*"', src[seq(dl, min(dl + 200L, length(src)))], value = TRUE)[1]
      if (is.na(lb)) next
      lb <- sub('^.*\\}\\s*,\\s*"([^"]+)"\\s*\\).*$', "\\1", lb)
      claim <- sub("\\s.*$", "", lb)
      if (!identical(toupper(claim), toupper(truth[[o]])))
        bad <- c(bad, sprintf("%s says %s but is %s", o, claim, truth[[o]]))
    }
    ## THIS LINT FIRED AND WAS USELESS. On 14 Oct it printed "21 placed panels
    ## checked, 5 mislabelled" and stopped -- it counted `bad` and never showed
    ## it, so the one person reading the log could not act on it. Reviewer 5
    ## then found the same drift by hand. Print the offenders.
    cat(sprintf("label lint: %d placed panels checked, %d mislabelled\n",
                length(truth), length(bad)))
    if (length(bad)) cat(paste0("  ", bad, collapse = "\n"), "\n", sep = "")

    ## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    ## CAPTION HARVEST. Under PANEL_TITLES = FALSE the panels lose their titles
    ## and subtitles, which is what the journals want and what loses the most
    ## work in this file: those subtitles carry the statistics, and many are
    ## built with sprintf so the numbers exist only at render time. wrap_titles
    ## captures them as it goes; this writes them out against the position the
    ## lint just computed, so each one can be folded into the legend sentence
    ## for that panel instead of being retyped from a previous render.
    cp <- mget(ls(CAPTIONS), envir = CAPTIONS)
    if (length(cp)) {
      tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cp, function(z) data.frame(
        panel = z$panel,
        position = if (!is.null(truth[[z$panel]])) truth[[z$panel]] else "unplaced",
        title = gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", z$title),
        subtitle = gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", z$subtitle),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
      ord <- order(grepl("^S", tab$position), suppressWarnings(
        as.integer(sub("^S?([0-9]+).*$", "\\1", tab$position))), tab$position)
      tab <- tab[ord, ]
      cf <- file.path(FIG_DIR, "figure_captions.tsv")
      utils::write.table(tab, cf, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = TRUE)
      cat(sprintf("caption harvest: %d panels written to %s\n", nrow(tab), cf))
      if (!PANEL_TITLES)
        cat("  PANEL_TITLES is FALSE, so this text is NOT in the figures.",
            "Fold it into the legends.\n")
    }
    if (length(bad)) {
      for (b in bad) cat("  ", b, "\n", sep = "")
      warning(sprintf("%d panel label(s) name the wrong figure: %s", length(bad),
                      paste(bad, collapse = "; ")), call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
}, error = function(e)
  cat("orphan audit failed (not fatal):", conditionMessage(e), "\n")))
```
